The model represents each scene through a group-level latent state that captures shared interaction dynamics and person-level latent states that capture individual behaviour conditioned on the evolving group context. This modelling choice enables coherent generation under full, sparse, or partial observations while exposing compact social-state vectors that can serve as an interface for downstream embodied-agent systems. We evaluate BRAID under a unified SMPL-based representation on social forecasting, tracking and in-filling, and response generation, using metrics that assess not only reconstruction accuracy but also realism, diversity, temporal alignment, and interpersonal coordination. We further analyse the hierarchical latent space, showing that it captures separable group- and individual-level structure.

articles.title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.37875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inverse design of physical systems (molecules, devices, microstructures) often reduces to optimizing a high-dimensional structure against an expensive black-box simulator. Direct search is difficult because the space is non-Euclidean, feasibility is hard to encode, and each evaluation is expensive. We present Co-PiLOT, a latent optimization approach that maps candidates through a generative encoder-decoder, uses the decoder as a learned validity prior, and searches the latent space with physics-informed black-box optimization. The framework is applied on the inverse design of magnesium alloy microstructure/texture. We develop a vision transformer based-encoder; paired with latent diffusion, diffusion transformer and rectified-flow transformer-based decoders on sim80,000 EBSD-derived microstructure dataset to learn a minimal bottleneck, z. The ViT-FMDiT model (z=768) reconstructs high-fidelity microstructure images (FID 27.86, MS-SSIM 0.178), which our self-segmenting orientation codec converts into input grids for crystal plasticity solver. Finally, we introduce MERIDIAN, an active latent optimizer driven by deep-kernel Gaussian-process uncertainty, failure-aware feasibility prediction, manifold-aware trust regions, and target-aware acquisition. Within a budget of 160 simulations, the ViT-FMDiT and MERIDIAN combination yields the best target-driven objective score, reducing the relative target error by 3--22% against seven baselines (DANTE, TuRBO, BAxUS, CMA-ES, DDOM, SEIKO, DDPO) on the same decoder.

articles.title: BrainNet Studio: A Unified Toolkit for Brain Network Construction, Intelligent Analysis, and Visualization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.37956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Brain networks characterize structural and functional relationships among brain regions and support research on cognition, brain disorders, and brain-computer interfaces. Their time-varying topology and higher-order spatiotemporal dependencies are not adequately represented by conventional static networks. Existing tools primarily focus on static connectomes and provide limited integration of dynamic network modeling with modern graph and sequence learning methods. We present BrainNet Studio, an integrated toolkit for static and dynamic brain network analysis. It provides a unified workflow encompassing network construction, feature extraction, predictive modeling, candidate biomarker identification, visualization, and assisted interpretation. The toolkit integrates 27 algorithms, including deep learning, graph neural networks, and spatiotemporal sequence models, to support classification and the identification of discriminative brain regions and connections. A large language model generates researcher-verifiable summaries of functional connectivity, structural connectivity, and structure-function coupling at individual and group levels. Within a consistent computational framework, users can configure analytical tasks, compare methods, inspect outputs, and extend functionality without repeatedly assembling application-specific pipelines. BrainNet Studio provides a practical and extensible platform for connectome analysis in cognitive neuroscience, exploratory studies of brain disorders, and brain-computer interfaces. The toolkit is publicly available at https://github.com/xbrainnet/Brainnet-Studio.

articles.title: PE-EK-PINN: Physics Embedding with Evolving Kernel for Scalable Physics-Informed Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.38023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) embed governing equations into deep learning, but enforce them only through loss residuals, leaving highly oscillatory wave behavior to be discovered by optimization. As a result, methods that achieve relative L₂ errors below 10⁻³ on standard manufactured Helmholtz benchmarks can fail on practical radiation problems involving singular excitations, absorbing boundaries, and wave fields spanning tens of wavelengths. Architectural physics embedding addresses this limitation by factorizing the field into analytically derived oscillatory kernels and learnable envelopes. However, the kernel dictionary must be manually constructed and scales with the number of elementary units, growing exponentially with the depth of hierarchically structured systems such as antenna arrays and metasurfaces. We propose PE-EK-PINN (Physics Embedded with Evolving Kernels), which treats physics kernels as reusable learned representations rather than fixed analytical inputs. A converged subsystem field is frozen and promoted to an evolved kernel, whose transformed copies are reused to represent higher-level configurations without deriving new governing equations. The resulting hierarchy makes the peak number of active kernels independent of system size and reduces cumulative training cost from O(N) to O(log N). Experiments on dipole arrays, composite line-source geometries, and cross arrays demonstrate the dramatic training cost reduction, while achieving a reduced or comparable relative L₂ error. One notable example is PE-EK-PINN solves a 256-dipole array more than 30 times faster than direct PE-PINN.

articles.title: Solvent Effect on Excited-State Hydrogen Transfer and Luminescent Properties of Anthranilic Acid in Solution and in Polymer Matrix
articles.abstract: Luminescent properties of anthranilic acid (AA) are studied in solution and in polymer matrix using polar and nonpolar solvents. The fluorescence of AA is found to depend on the environment, which favours improved molecular orientation. In dilute solution, emission arises from the neutral molecule and exhibits a smaller Stokes shift from the long-wavelength absorption band. The fluorescence from concentrated solution shows a large, Stokes-shifted, intense emission band, and the estimated values of Stokes shift are found to be solvent dependent. The Stokes-shifted fluorescence band in polar ethanol and water is attributed to the rotamer formed by intramolecular hydrogen bonding and to a water-bridge structure of AA, respectively. The water cluster of AA formed by solvation in aqueous solution was examined through the fluorescence properties of the molecule. The strongly Stokes-shifted emission band in concentrated carbon tetrachloride solution of AA is assigned to an intermolecular hydrogen-bonded dimer. Concentration-dependent fluorescence studies indicated increased emission intensity of AA without any accompanying spectral change. Polymer films doped with AA were prepared from its solutions in the solvents used in the present study. The behaviour of AA in the polymer matrix was examined by recording the fluorescence spectra of AA-doped polymer films. Polystyrene films doped with AA exhibited dual fluorescence: the band at 410 nm, corresponding to the rotamer formed by intramolecular hydrogen bonding, decreased with increasing wt% of AA, while the band at 437 nm increased. The emission band corresponding to the water-bridge structure of AA was not observed in the AA-doped PVA films. The AA-doped polymer films prepared in the present study by the solvent-evaporation technique are of potential use in electroluminescent light-emitting devices.

articles.title: Topological Percolation and Jamming Define the Universal First Critical Density in Granular Densification
articles.abstract: We present a first-principles topological framework that links integral geometry and jamming criticality to two key micro-CT observables: the Structure Model Index (SMI) and Degree of Anisotropy (DA). SMI is identified with the normalized mean curvature of the ice–void interface, and its evolution is captured by a Landau-type quadratic law describing the convex-to-concave pore network crossover. DA is derived from the fabric tensor of the jammed granular phase, yielding a cusp-shaped anisotropy function with distinct scaling regimes below and above jamming. Our closed-form expressions achieve R² = 0.99 for SMI and R² = 0.91 for DA. The percolation threshold (ρc = 556 kg m⁻³) and jamming density (ρⱼ = 550 kg m⁻³) coincide within uncertainties, establishing a unified, observation-based topological criterion for the first critical density in granular porous media-demonstrated for firn densification and universally applicable to other geo-porous materials.

articles.title: Modeling Radiative Magnetohydrodynamic Mixed Convection in Second-Grade Viscoelastic Flow over a Continuously Stretching Cylinder
articles.abstract: Motivated by its significance in industrial operations such as polymer extrusion, chemical manufacturing, and thermal processing, this study investigates the radiative magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) mixed convection flow of a second-grade viscoelastic fluid over a continuously stretching cylinder. Unlike conventional analyses based on flat stretching sheets, the present configuration incorporates curvature effects, thereby offering a more realistic representation of cylindrical extrusion and coating processes. The governing boundary layer equations are transformed into a coupled system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations using appropriate similarity transformations. A key mathematical challenge arises because the obtained fourth-order nonlinear momentum ODE is subject to only three boundary conditions. The mismatch between the high order of the coupled ODEs and the limited boundary conditions presents a distinct uniqueness challenge. We overcome this by imposing an additional constraint derived from mass conservation that is introduced to uniquely determine the system. The alignment of multiple obtained solutions demonstrates robustness. Crucially, instead of traditional 2D curves, the simultaneous impacts of the governing parameters are mapped using 3D surface topologies. This multi-dimensional approach successfully captures the non-linear coupling effects on the skin friction coefficient, Nusselt number, and Sherwood number, revealing critical parameter thresholds that remain obscured in conventional one-dimensional plots. Benchmarking with previously published results, further validates the robustness, accuracy, and physical reliability of the model. The findings suggest strong potential of practical significance and offer experimental investigations and engineering applications in advanced thermal management systems, including MHD generators, nuclear and solar thermal energy systems, metallurgical processing, polymer extrusion, electronic cooling modules, and high-performance heat exchangers.

articles.title: Machine-Learning Surrogates for Airfoil Aerodynamics: Accuracy, Extrapolation, and the Role of Known Physics: A Case Study with a Panel-Method Testbed
articles.abstract: Aerodynamic coefficients of an airfoil can be computed with physics-based solvers, and machine-learning surrogates are trained to replace repeated solver runs. We ask how such surrogates behave, using a testbed in which the physics is known exactly: lift and drag coefficients of NACA 4-digit airfoils, generated by the author's own potential-flow panel method and a simple drag estimate. The panel method is checked against thin-airfoil theory, a lift computation from the surface pressure, and an exact conformal-map solution. A random forest and a linear-regression baseline are compared under repeated random splits, splits that hold out entire airfoil shapes, a learning curve, permutation feature importance, residual analysis, and 48 queries outside the training ranges. Inside the training range the forest reaches a mean held-out R2 of 0.9994 (lift) and 0.9954 (drag), and the inputs it relies on match the physics: angle of attack and camber for lift, with thickness also mattering for drag. Outside the training range the forest's accuracy collapses (R2 = 0.81 and 0.18), while linear regression extrapolates lift well (R2 = 0.99). The spread of predictions across the forest's trees does not increase on out-of-range queries, so it gives no warning, whereas a simple input-range check flags every one. A two-stage model that builds in the known dependence of drag on lift extrapolates drag well (R2 = 0.97), but only because that dependence generated the data. Because the ground truth is a simplified model with no stall, the results concern the behavior of the surrogates, not real airfoils.

articles.title: Multidimensional processing profiles reveal the relational geometry of areal typological features in L2 reading
articles.abstract: Linguistic features form relational systems, yet second language (L2) reading research has treated isolated constructions and single eye-tracking measures as units of analysis. Using the Southeast Asian linguistic area as a natural experiment, we examined eye movements of native Chinese speakers (L1) and six L2 Chinese learner groups (N = 440) reading 75 Chinese texts. We integrated seven eye-tracking measures into a multidimensional processing profile, constructed the relational geometry of 28 areal typological features, and compared these with seven pre-trained language models via representational similarity analysis. Processing profiles reliably reconstructed feature relational geometry across all groups. Despite different language families, the six learner groups showed highly convergent processing relations, deviating from the L1 group along one common dimension. Language models partially reconstructed human processing geometry, but multilingual pretraining and linear decodability did not ensure human-like relational organization. These findings show that areal typological structure leaves a quantifiable signature in real-time L2 reading, providing a representational interface among language contact, L2 processing, and computational modelling.

articles.title: Application of Gröbner basis methodology to geometrically nonlinear axisymmetric circular isotropic plates
articles.abstract: This paper presents a systematic method for obtaining closed-form solutions to nonlinear engineering mechanics problems by combining weighted-residual approximations with Gröbner basis algebraic elimination. The proposed new approach begins with a weighted residual approximation technique of the governing nonlinear equations, such as Rayleigh–Ritz or Galerkin method, resulting in a coupled system of multivariate polynomial algebraic equations. Gröbner basis methodology is then used to transform the coupled system into an equivalent decoupled form that can, under certain conditions, be solved analytically. The novelty of the work lies in exploiting Gröbner basis techniques can be used as an enabling tool to derive closed-form solutions from nonlinear mechanics formulations that would traditionally be solved numerically. The methodology is demonstrated through the geometrically nonlinear analysis of axisymmetric circular isotropic plates based on Kirchhoff–von Kármán plate theory. Three representative boundary-condition cases are considered: clamped, simply-supported immovable, and simply-supported with an overhang. The Rayleigh–Ritz formulation generates the coupled polynomial equations that are symbolically decoupled using Gröbner bases and subsequently solved to obtain closed-form expressions for transverse displacement, stresses, moments, and shear forces. Results are validated against finite element solutions and show good agreement, with errors below 4% for large-deflection cases where linear theory becomes highly inaccurate. The resulting symbolic solutions retain the geometric, material, and loading parameters in explicit form, making parametric studies and design investigations significantly more efficient than repeated numerical simulations. The study therefore demonstrates the potential of a new general framework for deriving analytical solutions in many nonlinear structural mechanics that arise in several engineering applications.

articles.title: Feature-Optimized Quantum Classification Model for Financial Transaction Anomalies
articles.abstract: The exponential growth of digital financial transactions has increased the demand for intelligent and accurate fraud detection systems. This study proposes a Quantum-Enhanced Fraud Detection Framework that integrates classical feature engineering with advanced quantum machine learning techniques. The framework begins with comprehensive data preprocessing, including Mean, Median, and Mode Imputation to handle missing values and Z-Score Standardization along with Min–Max Scaling to normalize the data. The processed features are then transformed into quantum states using the ZZFeatureMap, enabling the representation of complex, non-linear correlations through quantum entanglement and superposition. The Quantum Kernel evaluates the pairwise similarity of quantum-encoded samples, capturing intricate relationships in high-dimensional feature spaces. Finally, a Quantum Support Vector Machine (QSVM) classifier is trained using the quantum kernel matrix to differentiate between fraudulent and legitimate transactions. The proposed method achieved an accuracy of 91%, demonstrating superior performance over conventional approaches by efficiently identifying subtle fraud patterns. The results validate the potential of Quantum Machine Learning (QML) as a powerful paradigm for financial fraud detection, combining classical data preprocessing with quantum computational advantages to achieve higher generalization and robustness.

articles.title: Quantifying Structural and Elemental Contributions to Local Electric Fields on Metal Nanoclusters with Interpretable Machine Learning
articles.abstract: Local electric fields (LEFs) govern field-assisted catalysis, but distinguishing the contributions of local geometry and metal identity remains challenging because changing the metal inevitably alters the equilibrium structure of the catalyst. Here we combine density functional theory (DFT) calculations with interpretable machine learning to quantify the structural and elemental contributions to the LEF on monometallic nanoclusters spanning nine transition metals, cluster sizes from 20 to 90 atoms, and external electric fields from − 0.5 to + 0.5 V/Å. A matched-site ΔLEF analysis shows that metal-substitution-associated LEF variations are below 0.08 V/Å and are explained predominantly by accompanying changes in local geometry. Consistently, SHAP analysis of the absolute LEF identifies geometric descriptors as the dominant predictors across the full dataset, whereas electronic contributions are secondary and are better captured by higher-order band-shape descriptors than by the conventional d-band center. An XGBoost model predicts the LEF with a test mean absolute error of 0.013 V/Å, and symbolic regression further reduces the relationship to a four-variable analytical equation with a test error of 0.031 V/Å. These results identify local geometry as the primary determinant of the LEF on transition-metal nanoclusters and provide an interpretable framework for predicting local electric fields in field-assisted catalysis.

articles.title: Interface-Engineered Ru/WS2/g-C3N4 Mott–Schottky Heterostructure for Efficient OER and Rechargeable Zn–Air Batteries
articles.abstract: Progress in metal–air batteries largely relies on efficient electrocatalysts that can drive the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). However, Ru-based electrocatalysts still face limitations in performance and stability due to slow OER kinetics, which are linked to strong adsorption of oxygen intermediates and limited control over interfacial charge transfer. Here, Ru species and WS2 nanosheets were integrated into a conductive g-C3N4 framework to create a Ru/WS2/g-C3N4 heterostructure that functions as an active catalyst. Structural and surface characterization confirmed the formation of the heterostructure and revealed strong electronic interactions among Ru, S, C, and N, facilitating charge redistribution and boosting catalytic activity. The catalyst achieves an overpotential of 209 mV at 10 mA cm− 2 and a Tafel slope of 84.2 mV dec− 1, reflecting improved OER performance due to the combined contributions of Ru sites, WS2 conductivity, and the π-conjugated g-C3N4 framework. The Ru/WS2/g-C3N4 electrode delivered an open-circuit voltage of 1.48 V, along with specific capacity of 811 mAh g− 1 and maximum power density of 161 mW cm− 2, and stable operation for 200 hours. The well-integrated heterointerface, which supported effective charge transfer and stabilized the active catalytic sites over time, was credited with the improved performance. These results show that Ru/WS2/g-C3N4 is an effective catalyst for high-performance Zn–air batteries and OER-driven energy conversion.

articles.title: Reaction Pathway Engineering for Nitrate Production in Atmospheric-Pressure Plasma via an Alternative Organic Nitrogen Source
articles.abstract: Plasma-activated water (PAW) has attracted attention for agricultural applications because plasma treatment can generate reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) and promote nitrate formation. However, increasing plasma power to enhance nitrate production also increases energy consumption, while the resulting nitrate increase may remain limited. In this study, plasma-activated coffee ground solutions (PAC) were prepared by introducing spent coffee grounds into deionized water treated at different plasma input powers. Nitrate production and the physicochemical properties of PAW and PAC were compared to evaluate the effects of plasma power and the presence of the organic species. Although increasing plasma power enhanced nitrate production in PAW, the increase was relatively limited. In contrast, the addition of spent coffee grounds substantially enhanced nitrate production under the same plasma conditions. Optical emission spectroscopy indicated prominent oxygen- and hydroxyl-related emissions, whereas nitrogen-related emissions were comparatively less pronounced, suggesting that reactive oxygen species (ROS) are more readily generated than reactive nitrogen species (RNS) under the present conditions. These results suggest that nitrate production can be enhanced by introducing an organic nitrogen source and utilizing plasma-generated reactive oxygen species, rather than relying solely on increased plasma power. This approach may reduce the need for additional plasma energy input while providing a potential route for the valorization and recycling of nitrogen-containing organic waste.

articles.title: A recognition-enhanced colorimetric sensor based on molecularly imprinted CoFe LDH nanozymes for detection of enrofloxacin in real water samples
articles.abstract: The widespread occurrence of enrofloxacin (ENR) in aquatic environments poses potential risks to ecosystems and human health. To develop a simple and selective method for ENR detection, a colorimetric sensor was constructed by integrating molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) with cobalt iron layered double hydroxides (CoFe LDH). The MIPs@CoFe LDH composite was prepared using chitosan (CS) as the functional monomer and glutaraldehyde (GA) as the crosslinking agent. The imprinted cavities on MIPs@CoFe LDH selectively captured ENR molecules, thereby blocking the diffusion pathway of H2O2 to the active sites of CoFe LDH and inhibiting the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). As a result, the catalytic oxidation of 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) was suppressed, generating a quantifiable colorimetric response. The proposed sensor exhibited a linear detection range of 0.19–50 µM for ENR with a detection limit of 0.03 µM. The method was further applied to river water samples, achieving recoveries with acceptable relative standard deviations (RSDs). This study provides a molecularly imprinted nanozyme-based approach for the selective detection of ENR in complex aquatic environments.

articles.title: Life Cycle Assessment of Geopolymer Concrete Based on Municipal Wastewater Sludge versus Ordinary Portland Cement Concrete: Implications for Sustainable Urban Architecture
articles.abstract: Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) concrete accounts for roughly 5–7% of global CO2 emissions. Geopolymer concrete, synthesized from industrial byproducts and waste-derived aluminosilicate materials, offers a sustainable alternative to conventional concrete for environmentally friendly construction. This study presents a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of 1 m3 of geopolymer concrete based on a municipal wastewater sludge-derived aluminosilicate binder combined with ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS), compared with standard OPC concrete of equivalent compressive strength (approximately 80 MPa at 28 days). The analysis was performed in SimaPro V9 using the CML 2001 baseline method for ten impact categories and the Cumulative Energy Demand (CED) method for energy analysis, within the context of the Isfahan metropolitan area, Iran. Geopolymer concrete showed markedly lower environmental impacts than OPC concrete across all ten CML categories. Its Global Warming Potential (GWP) was 73.2% lower than that of OPC concrete (1070.75 kg CO₂ eq/m3), and its cumulative energy demand was 73.0% lower than that of OPC concrete (8958.76 MJ/m3). Sodium silicate and sodium hydroxide were the largest contributors to the environmental burden of geopolymer concrete, while Portland cement and the chemical superplasticizer dominated the burden of conventional concrete. These findings indicate that geopolymer concrete produced from waste-derived precursors is a more environmentally sustainable alternative to OPC concrete, with considerable potential to reduce the environmental footprint of the built environment.

articles.title: The myxospermous seeds of shepherd’s purse (Capsella bursa pastoris L. Medik.): mucilage expansion, morphology, and ecosystem service potential as a seedbank component.
articles.abstract: Background and aims Myxospermy, the hydration-driven expansion of polysaccharide-rich seed mucilage, is widespread among angiosperms but remains underexplored as a functional plant–soil trait. We investigated myxospermy in shepherd’s purse (Capsella bursa-pastoris (L.) Medik.) to determine how seed mucilage structure, expansion dynamics and seedbank presence may influence seed hydration, germination and rooting-medium water relations.Methods Light- and dark-brown seed morphs were compared for mucilage production, hydration behaviour, desiccation and germination. Mucilage structure and composition were characterised using light, confocal and cryo-scanning electron microscopy, together with GC-MS monosaccharide analysis. Barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) seedling establishment was tested in a sandy rooting medium containing no seedbank, demucilaged seeds or myxospermous seeds.Results Light-brown seeds were consistently myxospermous, whereas dark-brown seeds were largely non-myxospermous. Upon hydration, light-brown seeds rapidly formed a layered mucilage sheath, increased seed volume approximately four-fold, absorbed water faster and germinated earlier than dark-brown seeds. Detailed real-time microscopic observation revealed distinct cellulose-rich structures and supported a four-step model of mucilage expansion. In sandy rooting medium, a myxospermous seedbank reduced the water required to maintain barley seedling growth by approximately 4.5-fold, without reducing root length or seedling fresh weight.Conclusions Myxospermy in C. bursa-pastoris is a functionally significant seed trait that modifies seed hydration and the seed–soil water interface. Myxospermous seedbanks may act as transient biological modifiers of microsite hydrology, with potential relevance to crop establishment and water-use efficiency in sandy or water-limited systems.

articles.title: Cosmetic Defect Detection in Semiconductors Using Deep Learning
articles.abstract: Defect detection in semiconductor packaging remains a critical challenge due to the visual complexity of metallic surfaces and the scarcity of defective samples in controlled manufacturing environments. Traditional Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) systems often lack the flexibility to identify subtle cosmetic blemishes, such as micro-scratches and spots, which directly affect product reliability and customer perception. This work proposes an automated defect detection framework that integrates Deep Learning (DL) architectures with a distributed Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) infrastructure. The methodology evaluates three distinct object detection architectures: a two-stage detector (Faster R-CNN), an anchor-free detector (FCOS), and a one-stage detector (YOLO11). To address the inherent class imbalance, a synthetic data augmentation pipeline was implemented following recent advances in generative and instance-level augmentation. Experimental results show that YOLO11 achieved the highest evaluated detection score, reaching a mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) of 93.5% and a precision of 90.7% on a held-out image-level evaluation subset. This subset contained both real and synthetic images and was obtained by randomly partitioning the final 400-image dataset. Furthermore, the implemented IIoT prototype demonstrates proof-of-concept interoperability using the MQTT protocol and a Raspberry Pi 5 gateway. These findings support further evaluation in industrial inspection workflows; suitability for production use remains to be established through dedicated system-level measurements under representative factory conditions.

articles.title: Quasi-three-phase phasor shielding for low-loss LCC-S wireless power transfer
articles.abstract: Reactive shielding suppresses leakage magnetic fields in wireless power transfer but can increase coil losses. Quasi-Three-Phase Phasor Shielding is introduced for an LCC-S system to reduce coil losses through joint adjustment of the receiver (RX) and shielding (SH) compensation capacitors. In the conventional configuration, SH coupling decreases the effective RX reactance and narrows the transmitter (TX)--RX current phase difference. The proposed adjustment widens this phase difference and increases the SH impedance, reducing both the induced-voltage phasor sum and the SH current. Coupled-circuit equations relate these changes to field superposition and coil conduction loss. With a 6.4,Ω load, simulations yield field reductions of 70.0% and 71.9% for conventional and proposed shielding, respectively, while overall efficiency increases from 85.2% to 86.3%. Experimentally, the TX--RX phase difference widens from 85.57^circ to 97.15^circ, reducing the SH RMS current by approximately 32.5% and increasing DC efficiency from 81.76% to 83.04%. Measured fields remain below the conventional values at all four observation distances. These results show that RX phase adjustment can maintain field suppression while alleviating the current and efficiency penalty of reactive shielding.

articles.title: Economic and Environmental Gains from the Use of Yeast By-Products in the Feeding of Dairy Cows
articles.abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable livestock production has intensified the search for nutritional strategies to improve animal performance while reducing environmental impacts. Among these strategies, yeast by-products have gained attention due to their potential to enhance feed efficiency, animal productivity, and environmental sustainability. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the economic feasibility and environmental benefits of using yeast by-products in dairy cow diets. Economic feasibility was assessed over a 10-year project lifespan using NPV, IRR, MIRR, PI, B/C ratio, discounted payback period, sensitivity analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation. Environmental performance was evaluated through enteric methane (CH₄) emissions and their conversion to CO₂e. The project was economically feasible, with positive financial indicators (NPV = US97,154.11; IRR = 12.39%; MIRR = 8.91%; PI = 1.45; B/C = 1.28) and a discounted payback period of 7.5 years. Economic viability remained robust under sensitivity and Monte Carlo analyses. Yeast supplementation reduced CH₄ emissions by up to 8.02 kg per cow per year (224.6 kg CO₂e) and decreased emissions per kilogram of energy-corrected milk. These findings indicate that yeast by-products are an economically attractive and environmentally sustainable option for dairy production systems. These findings indicate that yeast supplementation represents a viable strategy for dairy farms, simultaneously enhancing productive efficiency, generating economic returns, and contributing to greenhouse gas mitigation. Consequently, the adoption of yeast by-products may support the transition toward more sustainable and environmentally responsible dairy production systems.

articles.title: Supercapacitor-Based Voltage Smoothing in a Solar PV Microgrid: An OpenModelica Simulation Study
articles.abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) generation is inherently variable due to cloud passage and atmospheric scattering, producing rapid power fluctuations that degrade load voltage quality and stress downstream equipment in off-grid microgrid applications. This paper investigates the use of a supercapacitor (SC) as a short-term energy buffer to smooth PV output power fluctuations in a DC microgrid, using the open-source equation-based simulation environment OpenModelica. A PV array model based on a simplified single-diode characteristic is coupled with a two-branch RC equivalent circuit model of a 310 F / 2.7 V supercapacitor (Maxwell BCAP0310) and a first-order low-pass power smoothing filter with a time constant of 5 s. Two scenarios are compared under a realistic multi-frequency irradiance fluctuation profile: PV alone and PV with supercapacitor. The supercapacitor reduces peak load power fluctuation by 20.8%, RMS fluctuation by 17.5%, cumulative squared fluctuation by 32.0%, and load voltage standard deviation by 18.1%. The SC state of charge remains within a practical operating range throughout the simulation, confirming the viability of the passive smoothing strategy. These results demonstrate the potential of supercapacitors for power quality improvement in solar PV microgrids, particularly in off-grid contexts such as rural electrification in sub-Saharan Africa where grid support is unavailable.

articles.title: Degradation Signal Denoising Method for AC Contactors Based on Adaptive Modal Screening
articles.abstract: During the degradation process of AC contactors, the acquired signals are severely interfered by multi-source noises from arc impact, mechanical vibration and electromagnetic coupling, which tends to submerge weak degradation features. Conventional denoising methods also suffer from the loss of faint fault information. To address these issues, this paper proposes a degradation signal denoising method based on adaptive modal screening. First, variational mode decomposition (VMD) is employed to perform multi-scale adaptive decomposition on the raw non-stationary degradation signals, which overcomes the inherent drawbacks of severe mode mixing and endpoint effect in traditional empirical mode decomposition (EMD). Second, a weighted adaptive modal screening index is constructed by fusing modal energy features and sample entropy complexity features, enabling accurate and automatic discrimination between noise-dominated modes and effective degradation modes, and eliminating the subjectivity caused by manual screening. Finally, pure noise modes are removed, and the effective feature modes are reconstructed to obtain clean degradation signals with high signal-to-noise ratio.Comparative experiments are conducted based on measured data collected from an accelerated full-life degradation test platform for AC contactors. Classic denoising methods including wavelet threshold denoising (WTD), Empirical Mode Decomposition denoising (EMD), ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) and complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) are selected as benchmarks. Three quantitative metrics, namely envelope spectrum kurtosis, effective frequency band energy ratio and silhouette coefficient (SC), are adopted for performance evaluation. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional methods. It can fully preserve degradation features such as contact erosion and mechanical wear, and effectively improve the accuracy of subsequent degradation state division and remaining useful life prediction.

articles.title: Machine Learning and Digital Twin in Directed Energy Deposition: A Systematic Literature Review
articles.abstract: Directed Energy Deposition (DED) has emerged as a promising metal additive manufacturing technology for the repair, coating and fabrication of high-value components, offering high deposition rates, efficient material utilization and flexibility in manufacturing complex structures. However, the highly dynamic and nonlinear nature creates persistent challenges in DED processes, including process instability, defect formation, geometric deviation, and costly trial-and-error parameter selection. Addressing these challenges requires data-driven approaches for real-time monitoring, prediction, and adaptive control, highlighting the growing importance of Machine Learning (ML) and Digital Twin (DT). This systematic literature review provides a comprehensive synthesis of 130 studies on ML and DT applications in DED, following the PRISMA guideline. The recent research is concentrated on Wire Arc DED and Powder-fed Laser DED (LDED), and steels and Ni-based superalloys are the most frequently investigated materials, particularly 316L Stainless Steel and Inconel 718. ML has substantially improved the ability to monitor, classify, predict, and optimize DED processes. Vision-based data are widely adopted with supervised learning and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models. DT complements these ML capabilities by providing a cyber-physical framework for translating process predictions from ML models into real-time decision-making and adaptive process control. Despite rapid progress in this field, the transition from laboratory-scale prediction to industrial-scale autonomous DED remains incomplete. Studies integrating DT and ML focus on monitoring and prediction with limited in-process corrective action. Consequently, many reported DT systems in the reviewed literature are still digital shadows or monitoring-oriented frameworks with limited bidirectional communication. Future research should prioritize the integration of ML and DT in DED processes, employing closed-loop ML-DT architecture, multisensor fusion, robust ML models, generalized datasets generation using physics-informed modeling and transfer learning, and standardized benchmarking of datasets.

articles.title: Learning Spectrally Optimised Mesh-Free Discretisations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.02833v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Numerical methods for partial differential equations (PDEs) discretise differential operators, ideally reproducing the action of the continuous operators across all wavenumbers permitted by a given discretisation. Spectral-type methods approach this ideal, but rely on structured grids or high-order meshes that are hard to generate for complex geometries. In contrast, mesh-free methods are geometrically flexible, yet how faithfully they reproduce the operator across resolved scales is strongly influenced by a heuristically chosen kernel, which selects one of many weight sets satisfying the same consistency conditions without regard to the resulting spectral response. To address this, we introduce Spectrally optimised Neural Discretisations (SpeND), a framework that learns the map from local stencil geometry to discretisation weights on unstructured point clouds. A projection layer constrains every predicted stencil to the affine set defined by the discrete moment conditions, so polynomial consistency, and hence formal order of accuracy, holds exactly. Since consistency is enforced by the architecture, the weights can additionally be optimised for accuracy on a prescribed function space. Herein, we use Fourier modes and target the exact differentiation response over a chosen wavenumber band, so training is unsupervised. The loss function is a design interface: changing how it weights wavenumbers yields operators with distinct accuracy profiles. The trained discrete differential operators are PDE-agnostic and are applied without retraining to the Poisson, Burgers and Navier--Stokes equations, to near-boundary stencils, and across resolutions. At the same order and resolution, SpeND matches or improves on established mesh-free discretisations, and has been shown to reduce the wall-clock time between 3-20× to achieve equivalent error as the baselines.

articles.title: Superfluidity in the Interiors of Neutron Stars
articles.abstract: arXiv:1906.09641v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: I review some of the ideas that have been proposed for the structure of neutron star interiors, and concentrate on the theoretical arguments for the existence of superfluidity in neutron stars. I also discuss the implications of neutron superfluidity and proton superconductivity for the rotational dynamics of pulsars, and review arguments that have been proposed for observable effects of superfluidity on the timing history of pulsars and perhaps other neutron stars. The Lecture notes also include discussions of several features that are unique to interacting superfluid-superconducting mixtures, as well as the magnetic structure of quantized vortices in spin-triplet (³P₂) neutron superfluids.

articles.title: Exact Solvability and Integrability Signatures in a Periodically Driven Infinite-Range p-Spin Kicked Top Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.19991v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the signatures of quantum integrability (QI) in a p-spin kicked top model with infinite-range Ising interactions, subjected to periodic pulses of an external magnetic field, with the precession angle fixed at α=mπ. We analytically compute the unitary operator, its eigensystem, time evolution, single-qubit reduced density matrix, and entanglement dynamics for arbitrary initial states. We show that the spectrum of the unitary operator exhibits pronounced clustering of eigenphases in some regions, leading to strongly non-uniform spectral features with p. The entanglement measures and unitary operator dynamics exhibit periodic behavior, while the eigenvalue spectrum shows strong degeneracies when the kicking strength k' is a rational multiple of π for even p. For odd p, both the periodic behavior and spectral degeneracies persist for all values of k'. This periodic behavior extends to the strong-kicking regime (k'=J jp⁻¹π), where for rational values of J the dynamics remain periodic. For any k' and p the spectral statistics shows Poissonian behavior and the average adjacent gap ratio langle r rangle = 2ln 2 - 1, consistent with integrable behaviour. The spectral form factor further supports this nature. Additionally, we compute the ratio of average eigenstate entanglement entropy to its maximum value (langle S rangle /SMₐₓ) and find that it remains significantly far below from 1 in the limit N→ infty. These results collectively establish robust signatures of QI across all k', p, and system sizes. We also discuss possible experimental realizations of the model.

articles.title: Interplay of Nonstabilizerness and Ergotropy in Quantum Batteries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.03600v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Nonstabilizerness plays an essential role in the efficient simulation of quantum systems on quantum computers. In this work, we investigate its role in the context of quantum batteries (QBs). To this end, we consider a system of N spin-1/2 particles, with the left half serving as the charger and the right half as the battery. By studying different classes of interactions between the charger and the battery, we quantify the amount of nonstabilizerness required to store work in the QB. Our results reveal a strong correlation between the ergotropy stored in the battery and the total nonstabilizerness of the composite system whenever the Hamiltonian preserves a U(1) symmetry. In contrast, this correspondence is generally lost for more generic interactions. A similar behavior is observed for unitary circuit dynamics. Finally, we examine the complementary scenario in which the battery is initialized in a nonstabilizer state and subsequently charged through Clifford evolution. In this case, we find that the maximum average charging power is nonmonotonic in the initial nonstabilizerness. Remarkably, the highest average power can be achieved even when the initial state carries no magic (nonstabilizerness), demonstrating that initial magic is not a necessary ingredient for generating optimal charging power.

articles.title: Quantum Multiscale Modeling: A Hierarchy of Algorithms for Complex Chemical Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.11217v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multiscale modeling of complex chemical systems requires algorithms that operate coherently across electronic, atomistic, mesoscopic, and continuum scales. While quantum algorithms have been proposed for each regime, no systematic framework exists to compose them across scale boundaries. Here, we identify the conditions under which fault-tolerant quantum algorithms might preserve scale-specific quantum advantages. We map quantum phase estimation, Hamiltonian simulation with Gibbs state preparation, quantum random walks, and quantum partial differential equation solvers onto electronic structure, molecular dynamics, mesoscopic kinetics, and continuum reactor physics, respectively. Crucially, these correspondences do not imply unconditional end-to-end quantum advantage; speedups depend heavily on state preparation, memory architectures, matrix conditioning, and classical readout costs. Six unresolved questions define this composition problem, illustrated via a quantum hierarchy for ceCO oxidation over cePt(111). We propose viewing inter-scale transfer as a quantum channel composition problem at the interface of algorithm design and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, and ask whether information loss at scale boundaries is intrinsic to multiscale modeling or merely a consequence of lossy classical transduction between algorithmic layers. The resulting roadmap suggests that multiscale quantum advantage is governed primarily by the structure of information transfer between algorithmic layers, rather than by performance at individual scales alone.

articles.title: New device measures curved mirrors' absolute shape to within 2 nanometers without touching them
articles.abstract: Researchers at AIST have developed a device that measures the absolute surface profile of curved optical elements with high precision without touching them.

articles.title: Advancing Fuzzy-Sphere CFTs: SO(3)-Rotation-Resolving Exact Diagonalization, 3D Ising Heavy Primaries, and Quasi-Hole-Space Projection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.35960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fuzzy-sphere regularization has recently emerged as a powerful framework for studying three-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs). In this work, we exploit symmetry and Hilbert-space structures to substantially advance this framework. We develop an exact-diagonalization algorithm that resolves the full SO(3) rotational symmetry, reducing computational costs by factors of several hundred. For the three-dimensional Ising CFT, we identify around 100 primary operators, including a large number of previously unknown heavy scalar primaries up to scaling dimension Δapprox16.5. We also resolve the tension between previous fuzzy-sphere and bootstrap results regarding the parity-odd scalar primary. Furthermore, we identify a branch of scalar primaries associated with φⁿ operators in the φ⁴ Lagrangian description, beginning with the identity, σ, ϵ, ϵ', and σ'. Their wave functions exhibit a semi-classical structure closely related to states invariant under area-preserving diffeomorphisms of the sphere. Finally, we show that critical points involving fractional quantum Hall states can be studied within a substantially reduced Hilbert space spanned by quasi-hole states of the corresponding model quantum Hall wave functions like the Laughlin state. This suggests a general strategy for exploring CFTs intertwined with topologically ordered phases.

articles.title: Accelerating phase-field simulations on exascale computing systems for faster-than-real-time precipitate aging predictions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Three-dimensional phase-field simulations are a gold-standard for microstructure prediction for materials, but their computational cost often limits application-relevant calculations to modest domain sizes and timescales. Here, we present a holistic approach for accelerating Fourier pseudospectral phase-field simulations by combining performance-portable GPU computing, large-scale distributed-memory parallelism, and high-order implicit-explicit time integration within the MEUMAPPS C++ framework. We demonstrate this approach with a 1.5-billion-grid-point simulation of the growth and coarsening of 1,920 gamma'' precipitates in a Ni-Nb-Fe alloy. The simulated seven-hour heat treatment is completed in 5.5 hours, making the calculation faster than real time and an estimated 217-501x faster than a CPU-only, first-order baseline. This performance makes three-dimensional simulations of thousands of interacting precipitates tractable, enabling quantitative studies ocollective microstructural phenomena, large simulation ensembles, and real-time integration into controlling and interpreting experiments. Benchmarking shows single-node GPU speedups of up to 17.5x relative to comparable CPU resources, near-ideal strong scaling to 4096 GPUs for a 12-billion-grid-point problem, and a further 2.6-2.9x acceleration from fourth-order time integration at scientifically relevant error tolerances. These results establish a performance-portable strategy for exploiting leadership-scale GPU systems that is applicable to a broad class of Fourier pseudospectral simulations beyond phase-field models such as fluid dynamics and crystal plasticity simulations.

articles.title: Far-field terahertz spectroscopy across the charge-density-wave transition in 2H-NbSe₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charge-density-wave (CDW) formation in 2H-NbSe₂ modifies the low-energy electronic structure and gives rise to collective excitations coupled to the lattice. Here, we investigate bulk 2H-NbSe₂ single crystals using far-field terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) in reflection geometry across the CDW transition at TCDW approx 33~K. Below TCDW, the THz response shows a pronounced high-frequency feature near 1.5~THz together with longer-lived sub-THz oscillations. Both responses progressively weaken upon warming and are strongly suppressed across the CDW transition, supporting their association with the CDW state. Using time-dependent Ginzburg--Landau simulations, we reproduce the main features of the experimental THz response, associating the high-frequency response mainly with CDW amplitude dynamics and the sub-THz response with defect-pinned phase dynamics. The sim1.5~THz feature lies close to the frequency range reported for the Raman CDW amplitude mode, while coupling to lattice degrees of freedom may also influence its spectral position. We also performed complementary angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements, which reveal momentum-selective redistribution of near-Fermi-level spectral weight across the transition. Together, these results show that far-field THz spectroscopy provides a sensitive probe of collective CDW dynamics in bulk 2H-NbSe₂.

articles.title: Fracture of Lattice Materials from Low to High Relative Density
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lattice materials have highly tunable mechanical properties that are controlled by their internal geometry and base material behavior. While fracture models for low-density lattices are well-established, the fracture of lattices at relative densities above 30% remains largely unexplored. Here, we present an analytical model that combines homogenization methods and blunt-crack fracture theory to predict the fracture toughness of triangular and hexagonal lattices over a wide range of relative densities. Finite element modeling corroborates the analytical framework and demonstrates a shift in failure mechanisms between low and high relative density regimes. At high relative densities, failure is dominated by nodal stress concentrations, which are strongly influenced by the local crack-tip geometry and the macroscopic crack path. Significant stress redistribution is observed as the relative orientation and lattice fillet radius are varied, resulting in increased fracture toughness relative to baseline geometries. Furthermore, quasi-brittle poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) lattices achieve about a 1.6x enhancement in fracture toughness relative to perfectly brittle lattices as failure is delayed by localized plasticity. Notably, some quasi-brittle lattices are found to exceed the fracture toughness of their base material -- a feature only possible when the cell size is large compared to the base material's plastic radius. Experiments on lattice fracture specimens made from laser-cut PMMA validate the finite element results, but highlight the stochastic nature of failure in brittle lattice materials, especially at higher relative densities.

articles.title: Autonomous self-harmonic drift in Langevin dynamics causes a compaction of underlying domain for the density of Stochastic Localization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Our recent research on Langevin dynamics with self-harmonic drift and classical spins has revealed a strong connection to ``Stochastic Localization," a concept attracting attention in the fields of mathematical geometry and data science. Roughly speaking, the former can be viewed as a version of the latter in which the n-dimensional Euclidean space - the domain of the probability distribution function appearing in the latter - is ``compactified'' to the surface of an n-dimensional sphere. By comparing the two frameworks, we argue that this compactification is a consequence of requiring the drift to be autonomous. The relationship between the two approaches may expand the scope of Stochastic Localization.

articles.title: Enhanced Critical Currents and Irreversibility Fields in YBa₂Cu₄O₈ Films through Ca-Substitution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The intrinsic carrier concentration of superconducting materials may not be optimal, and different superconducting properties may have distinct optimal doping levels. Here, we show that Ca substitution increases the hole concentration in intrinsically underdoped epitaxial (Y₁₋ₓCaₓ)Ba₂Cu₄O₈ (YCa124) films with x ≤ 0.10, driving YCa124 toward optimal doping, increasing T_c and J_c. At 40 K, 10% Ca doping increases J_c by factors of 2.4 and 10 at 0.03 and 6 T, respectively, compared with the undoped film. The field dependence of J_c follows J_c propto B⁻⁰.⁵, independent of Ca content, indicating that Ca substitution does not alter the dominant pinning mechanism. This field dependence is consistent with pinning by planar Y-125 stacking-fault intergrowths observed by electron microscopy. In addition, Ca substitution slows thermally activated vortex motion (creep) at T gtrsim 15 K, while at lower temperatures the creep rate S shows an unusual decrease with increasing field. Finally, we consider how doping tunes the upper bound on J_c, set by the depairing current density J_d, and the lower bound on creep, set by the Ginzburg parameter Gᵢ. We find positive correlations between J_c and J_d, and between S and Gᵢ, and compare them with trends across a broad range of superconductors.

articles.title: Orbital-engineered px,y-kagome lattice in a halogen monolayer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-orbital kagome lattices with explicit orbital degrees of freedom remain largely unexplored, as most experimentally realized systems rely on complex d-electron manifolds that are approximated by isotropic single-orbital models. Here, we overcome this limitation by realizing a px,y-orbital kagome lattice through deposition of a Br monolayer on Ag(111), where orbital filtering selectively suppresses the pz channel. Scanning tunneling microscopy, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, and density-functional-theory calculations reveal a large-area, highly ordered kagome structure whose band dispersions quantitatively match the anisotropic px,y tight-binding model. To extract the intrinsic manifold from the substrate background, we construct an effective H-passivated model, which uncover the intrinsic electronic structure and reveals nontrivial topological characteristics of the px,y kagome manifold driven by first-order spin-orbit coupling effect. Our work establishes Br/Ag(111) as an experimentally accessible platform for multi-orbital kagome physics, extending the kagome paradigm from the conventional d-orbital regime to an orbitally engineered topological setting.

articles.title: From Automated Simulation to Autonomous Discovery: A Hierarchical Framework for Agentic Computational Materials Science
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The convergence of large language models, materials-specific foundation models, and agentic artificial intelligence is reshaping the paradigm of computational materials discovery. While high-throughput computation, automated workflows, and data-driven modeling have greatly expanded the scale of materials exploration, the core scientific decision-making loop remains largely human-directed. Agentic AI introduces the possibility of systems that can autonomously reason about materials objectives, execute simulations, and refine strategies. However, the rapid emergence of such systems has created a critical need for a unified and operational framework to define, evaluate, and guide scientific autonomy in computational materials discovery. In this Perspective, we propose the Computational Materials Agent Autonomy Level (CMA-AL) framework, a hierarchical taxonomy defining six levels of autonomous agency in computational materials science: scripted excecutor, LLM-assisted operator, adaptive explorer, experiment-ready modeler, agentic digital twin, and self-extending intelligence. We further map emerging agentic systems onto the framework and identify key scientific and technological challenges toward higher autonomy. CMA-AL provides a common language for characterizing agentic computational materials discovery, evaluating the maturity of emerging systems, and guiding their evolution toward increasingly autonomous materials discovery.

articles.title: Enabling the Ambient Pressure Growth of ScB2 Crystals for AlGaN Power Electronics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Here we report the growth of single crystalline ScB2, an ultrahigh-temperature ceramic, at ambient pressure in a laser-heated Optical Floating Zone via the travelling solvent method. Crystals have been grown from both Sc-rich (55-65 at% Sc) and B-rich self-flux (80-83 at% B) at growth rates in the range of 0.2-2 mm/hr. The structure of grown crystals is in good agreement with an AlB2-type layered hexagonal phase, space group P6/mmm, with lattice constants a = 3.1423(2) Å (resp. 3.1502(3) Å) and c = 3.5084(3) Å (resp. 3.5041(3) Å) for crystals grown under Sc-rich (resp. B-rich) conditions. Crystals natively grow along the in-plane [100] direction. Electron backscattered diffraction shows that Sc-flux growth results in boules with multiple domains containing Sc inclusions, with the domains highly aligned. In contrast, B-flux boules are single domain after the initial nucleation region. Rocking-curve measurements of B-flux crystals for the (h000) and (000l) reflections show single peaks, establishing that the crystals are free from grain boundaries; the asymmetry in the scattered-intensity tails suggests the presence of point defects. Surface X-ray photoemission spectroscopy shows that the electronic environment in B-flux crystals is superior to that of Sc-flux crystals and produces highly resolved binding-energy peaks for B 1s and Sc 2p. Work-function measurements for the (11-20) plane give a value of approximately 5 eV, consistent with the highly electrically conductive nature of ScB2. These results demonstrate the viable ambient-pressure growth of ScB2, establish it as a lattice-matched substrate candidate for Al-rich AlGaN power microelectronics, and show that this growth route enables scalable manufacturing of ScB2 substrates.

articles.title: Mechanical Signature of a Chemically Driven Bath
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using optical tweezers, we demonstrate that the CuAAC click reaction increases the positional fluctuations of a trapped 2 micrometer colloid by at least 20% without altering the trap's corner frequency. This excess variance relaxes to the thermal baseline as reagents are depleted. The additional noise is Gaussian, with a flat power spectrum extending past the corner frequency up to 7 kHz. Notably, the noise amplitude decouples from the macroscale reaction rate, and independent molecular force dipoles are orders of magnitude too small to generate the observed variance. Although the chemical free energy released locally exceeds the energy absorbed by the bead by five orders of magnitude, this energy couples inefficiently. The mechanical action of the reacting bath cannot be represented as a sum of independent molecular events.

articles.title: Polar-Domain Volume as a Unified Descriptor of Transport in Ionic Liquids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Developing molecular scale structural descriptors that can quantitatively predict the macroscopic transport properties of ionic liquids remains a longstanding question, owing to the complex interplay between molecular interactions, nanoscale organization, and collective ion dynamics. Here, we use all atom molecular dynamics simulations to establish quantitative structure property relationships between the equilibrium microstructure and two key transport properties viscosity and ionic conductivity in a series of imidazolium based ILs with chemically distinct anions and varying alkyl chain lengths. While viscosity and ionic conductivity exhibit distinct dependencies on alkyl chain length and anion chemistry, these seemingly different trends largely collapse onto unified correlations when expressed in terms of the mean polar-domain volume. In particular, both transport properties exhibit systematic power-law scaling with the mean polar domain volume fraction, revealing a common structural origin underlying the variations in ion and momentum transport across chemically distinct ILs. These results establish polar-domain volume as a physically motivated molecular-scale descriptor and provide a general structure property framework for connecting nanoscale organization to macroscopic transport properties in ILs.

articles.title: Interlayer coupling between twisted graphenes through atomically-precise barriers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding and controlling interlayer coupling in van der Waals (vdW) materials is crucial for engineering novel electronic phenomena, including correlated states, topological phases, and superconductivity. Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) offers a highly tunable platform to explore how interlayer orientation and separation influence quantum transport and moiré physics. Here, we introduce a method for achieving precise, atomic-scale control of interlayer coupling in TBG using dual-gated devices separated by ultrathin, thickness-tunable hBN spacers. This approach enables systematic control of interlayer interactions, demonstrating that the critical displacement field required for electron-hole bilayer behavior decreases as the layer separation increases at a fixed twist angle. Remarkably, at small twist angles, moiré-related side peaks persist even when layers are separated by tetralayers of hBN (approximately 1.3 nm), indicating robust interlayer band hybridization. By combining atomic-layer-precise control of interlayer coupling with independent twist angle tunability, our platform opens new avenues for discovering novel moiré physics governed by engineered interlayer coupling and moiré patterns.

articles.title: Synthesis and modification of thin NaSICON solid electrolytes using ion beams
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solid electrolytes (SEs) for sodium-based superionic conductors (NaSICON) were first introduced in 1976 and quickly recognized for their excellent ionic conductivity. While considerable effort has been made to develop thin electrolytes for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), only a few sodium-based SEs have been successfully fabricated as thin films. These thin films are particularly desirable for their reduced electrical resistance, which typically increases with the thickness of the SE. By reducing the thickness of the SEs to the nanometer scale, their ionic conductivity can be significantly enhanced. In this study, the NASICON composite was initially prepared in the form of pellets using the mixed oxide technique with a planetary ball mill and synthesized by the solid-state method at 1300 degC. The resulting pellets were used as sputtering targets in a low-energy ion facility to prepare continuous NASICON nanofilms. To explore the effect of ion implantation on the electrical properties of NASICON, the prepared films were bombarded with Ni ions at 1.1 MeV and varying fluences, using the Tandetron accelerator at the CANAM infrastructure (NPI Řež). The electrical properties of both the synthesized and implanted films were analyzed through electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The results, describing the impact of irradiation on NASICON's properties, are presented here.

articles.title: Evidence for Distributed Fault Energetics and Their Impact on Deformation in a Chemically Complex Alloy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chemically complex alloys feature intrinsically heterogeneous local chemical environments and, consequently, fluctuations in local fault energetics. However, experimentally quantifying their relationship remains challenging, leaving the role of this distributed energy landscape in deformation mechanisms incompletely resolved. Here, we develop a distribution based framework linking experimentally measured stacking fault widths to deformation relevant apparent fault energy, revealing a distributed local fault-energy landscape in CrCoNi. The framework reveals the stabilizing role of energy fluctuations and captures an upward shift in the apparent fault energetics, from negative values toward zero following heat treatment, which atomistic simulations associate with the emergence of L12 type chemical short-range order. Using one-dimensional kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, supported by electron microscopy observations, we further show that history-dependent changes in the local fault-energy landscape bias the competition among stacking faulting, nano-twinning and HCP transformation in CrCoNi. Our results provide an experimentally anchored, distribution-based framework for understanding deformation in chemically complex alloys as it evolves within a distributed fault-energy landscape shaped by local chemical order.

articles.title: Quantized Hyperfine Field at an Implanted μ⁺ Site in PrPb₃: Interplay between Localized f Electrons and an Interstitial Charged Particle
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The local effect of an interstitial hydrogen-like particle on localized f electrons was studied in PrPb₃ by means of μ⁺ spin rotation and relaxation. Spontaneous μ⁺ spin precession with harmonic frequencies was observed for the first time in f electron compounds. We demonstrate that the signal is derived from a coupling between the μ⁺ spin and the hyperfine-enhanced nuclear spin of nearest neighbor (nn) ¹⁴¹Pr with Ising-like anisotropy. The signal also suggests a marked suppression of spin dynamics of the nn ¹⁴¹Pr in comparison with that of the bulk ¹⁴¹Pr. These facts strongly indicate modification of the f electronic state due to the interstitial charged particle.

articles.title: Static versus dynamic universality in the site-diluted kagome Ising model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the site-diluted Ising model on the kagome lattice using the Wolff single-cluster algorithm, focusing on both equilibrium and dynamic critical properties. The equilibrium critical exponents ν = 1 and γ/ν = 7/4 retain their exact pure Ising values for all spin concentrations p considered, consistent with the marginal irrelevance of disorder at α = 0, with the specific heat crossing over from logarithmic to double-logarithmic growth upon dilution. These static results are shared between the kagome and square lattices. On the dynamic side, z decreases upon dilution on both lattice, opposite to what is observed under local dynamics, with evidence of saturation to a p-independent value at strong dilution, suggesting a diluted dynamic fixed point. While z is consistent between the two lattices in the pure case, it differs in the diluted regime, an effect we attribute to the two lattices sitting at different positions along the renormalization-group flow between the Ising and percolation fixed points, rather than to a true asymptotic breakdown of dynamic universality.

articles.title: Tuning the secondary electron yield and electronic conductivity of MgZnO multilayers synthesized by Atomic layer deposition
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Secondary electron emission (SEE), arising from the interaction of energetic electrons with material surfaces, can induce deleterious effects in vacuum radio-frequency (RF) systems, notably multipacting, thereby degrading performance and threatening device integrity. Despite extensive efforts, effective and widely adopted mitigation strategies remain limited. Here, we report an approach to simultaneously tailor SEE and electrical conductivity using nanometric multi-element multilayers deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD). The design and fabrication of these heterostructures are presented, and a range of films is systematically characterized to establish correlations between emission properties, electrical conductivity, chemical and structural features. We demonstrate that such heterostructures enable combinations of total electron emission yield (TEEY) and conductivity unattainable in single-phase materials, including regimes combining high TEEY with relatively high conductivity and low TEEY with low conductivities. These results open new avenues for the rational design of functional surfaces for vacuum electronic applications.

articles.title: 24-hr Solid-State Power Generation with Self-Adaptive Tunable Radiative Coatings
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Day-night solid-state power generation is experimentally demonstrated with thermoelectric generators integrated with a tunable radiative coating, which switches between a selective solar absorber during daytime and a radiative cooler during nighttime by temperature without any external control. The self-adaptive radiative coating is carefully designed with thermochromic VO2 thin film on heavily doped silicon substrate along with a phase-shifting silicon spacer in between, whose physical mechanism is elucidated. The fabricated coating exhibits a high solar absorptivity of 0.90 and a low infrared emissivity of 0.23 during daytime, and a high emissivity of 0.85 at night, resulting in large emissivity change of 0.62 within the atmospheric transparency window upon metal-to-insulator phase transition. From outdoor tests in a high vacuum apparatus, the tunable radiative coating in 35-mm squared size achieves 1.64 W/m2 power generation around noon time from a stack of commercial thermoelectric modules of 15 mm squared, which is 32% more from that with a black absorber. At night, it produces 26 mW/m2 power, outperforming the black emitter by 63%. Even exposed the ambient with convective loss, the 2-inch-round tunable coating generates power of 0.48 W/m2 at noon time, 14% more than the black absorber of the same size. The tunable radiative coating covered thermoelectric modules produces open circuit voltages from 433 mV to -62 mV in vacuum and from 300 mV to -51 mV in ambient through 24-hr continuous outdoor tests.

articles.title: Spin separation of Dirac electrons by twisted and vector optical beams
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.37010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that twisted and vector optical beams can spatially separate two-dimensional electrons with opposite spin projections. Spin accumulation arises from diverging spin currents induced by structured light together with spin relaxation and diffusion. We derive analytical expressions for the resulting spin density in the quasi-local and diffusion-controlled regimes and numerically calculate the spin textures for the parameters relevant to transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers. Our results suggest a mechanism by which the twist and vector pattern of optical beams can be imprinted onto the electron spin degree of freedom.

articles.title: Cavity-QED enhancement of quantum entanglement and battery performance in double quantum dots
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.37034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically investigate quantum correlations and energy storage in a single-electron silicon double quantum dot (eDQD) coupled to a single-mode microwave cavity. The charge and spin degrees of freedom are hybridized by Rashba spin-orbit coupling (SOC), while the cavity interacts with the eDQD through spin-photon and charge-photon couplings. Using the reduced thermal density matrix, we characterize spin-charge entanglement by concurrence and quantum coherence by the l₁ norm. At low temperature, the cavity strongly modifies the spin-charge correlations, producing distinct regimes of enhanced and suppressed entanglement. We identify a nonlinear crossover between an eDQD-dominated regime and a photon-dressed regime. This crossover is revealed independently by two signatures: a rapid change in the concurrence and the onset of finite photon occupation in the cavity. Its boundary exhibits a dominant Gᵣₘ cproptosqrtΩ dependence and is robust against cavity Hilbert-space truncation. Beyond the Rashba coupling studied in [Ferreira et al., Phys. Rev. A 107, 052408 (2023)], we show that the cavity provides an additional tunable means of controlling quantum correlations and energy storage. We further characterize the eDQD as a quantum battery under coherent charging and evaluate its stored energy and ergotropy. The ergotropy varies markedly across a cavity-dressing crossover resembling that identified from entanglement, connecting cavity-induced modification of the dressed states to extractable work. Optimization over the charge-photon coupling reveals parameter-dependent optimal charging regimes and enhanced maximum ergotropy with increasing Rashba coupling. Our results establish cavity coupling and SOC as complementary controls of quantum correlations and extractable energy in semiconductor eDQD-cavity systems.

articles.title: Weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensate with stochastic resetting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.37110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic resetting can generate strong correlations in many-body systems through a shared fluctuating environment. Here, we investigate how such dynamically emergent correlations (DEC) coexist with intrinsic (direct) interactions in a weakly repulsive Bose-Einstein condensate described within the Gross-Pitaevskii framework. The condensate undergoes free expansion from an initial Thomas-Fermi state and is stochastically reset to this initial state at a constant rate. We show that the resetting protocol drives the system into a unique nonequilibrium steady state and obtain its density profile, edge statistics, and full counting statistics analytically. The steady-state density retains an inverted-parabolic form within the core, while developing exponentially decaying tails outside it. We further show that resetting induces nontrivial fluctuations of the condensate edge and particle number, yielding exact scaling forms for the edge distribution and the full counting statistics. Our results provide a tractable setting for exploring the interplay between intrinsic repulsive interactions and attractive DEC generated by a common stochastic environment in quantum many-body systems.

articles.title: Engineering Vacuum Fluctuations in Hyperbolic Heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.37182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vacuum fluctuations can be engineered using optical cavities, resonators, and surface-polaritonic modes, but extending such control deep inside a material remains challenging.Here we show that the vacuum field inside a hyperbolic material can be reshaped by a much thinner overlayer with opposite hyperbolicity.This effect requires overlap between the hyperbolic bands of the two materials and modifies the coupling between the vacuum field and matter excitations within the bottom material, without changing its intrinsic dielectric properties. As an application, we use Eliashberg theory to study a two-dimensional superconducting layer inside the bottom material, showing that the overlayer can remotely change its critical temperature.Our results may shed light on recent experiments reporting changes in superconductivity arising from a frequency-matched hyperbolic overlayer, and suggest an on-chip route to long-range control of matter excitations and collective material properties.

articles.title: Engineering Synaptic Dynamics in Ag-Modified TaOₓ Memristive Devices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.37204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Engineering not only the magnitude but also the dynamics of synaptic weight updates is an important challenge for memristive neuromorphic hardware.
