We propose Fully Resilient AC-MARL (FRAC-MARL), a decentralized method in which each agent leverages redundancy in two-hop messages to identify reliable messages. Under linear parameterizations of the value and team-reward functions and Byzantine edge attacks, where adversarial behavior is confined to the communication layer, we prove that agents' parameters converge almost surely to the same limit points as in the attack-free case over time-varying communication graphs. We introduce a novel topological condition for the convergence of our method, present a systematic method to construct such networks, and prove that this condition can be verified in polynomial time. Finally, we demonstrate our method on cooperative multi-robot formation control tasks.

articles.title: Signed Graph Pre-Training and Prompt Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Signed graphs arise in trust--distrust networks, financial correlation systems, biological interaction graphs, and many other domains in which edges can be positive or negative and may also be directed. While signed graph neural networks have improved task-specific learning, graph transfer learning on signed graphs remains underdeveloped. In this paper, we introduce TopoSIGN, a pioneer topology-guided graph pre-training and prompt learning framework for signed graphs. TopoSIGN combines a structural encoder built on the magnetic signed Laplacian with a novel persistent-homology branch that summarizes signed topology through Dowker-complex persistence images. The fused embeddings are then transferred to a prompt learning function. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the efficacy of TopoSIGN in extracting useful structural information in signed graphs, as well as the adaptability and flexibility of the proposed general framework.

articles.title: AURA: Angular Update Rate Adaptation for training complex-valued neural networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complex-valued neural networks (CVNNs) are increasingly adopted for complex-valued data; however, they are often trained with first-order optimizers inherited from the real-valued case. The efficiency of these methods depends largely on the step size, and their step-size rules ignore the angular information available in the complex plane. We address step-size adaptation in the complex domain by introducing AURA (Angular Update Rate Adaptation), a per-parameter step-size adaptation that can be added on top of any first-order optimizer, and removed from it, without altering its update direction. AURA measures the agreement between consecutive updates of each complex parameter, in length, alignment, and sense of rotation, and enlarges the step when they are consistent and reduces it when they are not. It requires no additional gradient evaluations and only inexpensive vector operations per step. We combine AURA with Adam and Muon and compare the resulting methods with well-known first-order optimizers on four test cases of increasing complexity, ranging from the approximation of scalar complex functions to physics-informed training. Fully connected neural networks are used throughout this work. All hyperparameters other than the step size are held fixed across test cases; for one case, we also tune the hyperparameters of each optimizer under the same budget. Our empirical tests show that AURA improves the convergence of its base optimizer in most cases with a small per-step overhead, and we identify the conditions under which it fails to do so.

articles.title: From Risk Scoring to Risk Allocation: A Density-Driven Framework for Diverse Monitoring in Multi-Agent Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.26146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Risk monitoring in multi-agent systems is commonly built on a per-state primitive that scores each state independently and selects the top K. Under crowding, where many agents share the same fragility, this approach picks redundant alerts whose risks are jointly correlated, a pattern we describe as ``herding in monitoring.'' We propose a paradigm shift from risk scoring to risk allocation, supported by two contributions. First, we identify the Crowding Paradox, namely that P(risk | x) propto p(x) rather than 1/p(x), so density rather than anomaly score is the operative risk signal; on financial data, density-based scoring reaches AUROC ≥ 0.94 at 5d/10d/20d crash horizons, while five anomaly baselines all fall below 0.80. Second, given a density-derived fragility score, we recast monitoring as combinatorial subset selection over interdependent states and map it to a QUBO objective with a λ-controlled risk--diversity tradeoff. The resulting Pareto frontier contains standard diverse-subset methods (MMR, k-DPP) as fixed operating points; the gain over greedy grows monotonically with scale, from +24% at n=15 to +66% at n=200; a learned λ policy reaches 99.5% of an oracle grid-search objective; and the formulation transfers to traffic and multi-agent reinforcement learning. The same QUBO instances execute without modification on Rigetti superconducting QPUs (Ankaa-3 and Cepheus-1-108Q via Amazon Braket), which we report as a compatibility property of the formulation rather than a claim of quantum advantage at this scale.

articles.title: OMatG-flash: An All-Atom Flow Map with Reinforce Adjoint Matching for Scalable Materials Discovery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.26402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The discovery of novel inorganic materials drives technological breakthroughs in critical fields such as computing and energy storage. Generative AI has promised to accelerate the materials discovery pipeline, but state-of-the-art flow and diffusion models remain bottlenecked by the cost of proposing candidate materials. To address this, we introduce OMatG-flash, an all-atom flow map for inorganic crystal structure prediction (CSP) and de novo generation (DNG). OMatG-flash is a Pareto-optimal inference engine for materials, sampling candidate materials with an order of magnitude fewer inference steps and less wall-clock time than existing flow and diffusion models while demonstrating benchmark performance on par with the state-of-the-art. To enable post-training fine-tuning we apply Reinforce Adjoint Matching to flow maps, further improving match rates and RMSE on the unconditional CSP task. OMatG-flash showcases the potential of flow maps to accelerate generation of high-quality candidate inorganic materials and demonstrates a step forward in sample throughput necessary for data-hungry materials discovery workflows.

articles.title: DeepFEAv2: Deep Learning for Transient Finite Element Analysis Beyond Structured Meshes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.26426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite Element Analysis (FEA) is widely used for transient mechanical simulations, but its high computational cost limits real-time and high-resolution applications. Deep learning surrogate models can reduce this cost; however, many existing approaches are restricted to steady-state prediction or cannot jointly predict Node- and Element-based Outputs (NEO) over time. The state-of-the-art DeepFEA framework has addressed these issues but remains limited to structured finite element (FE) meshes. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes DeepFEAv2, a deep learning surrogate framework that enables prediction of transient FEA simulations across different FE mesh topologies and element types. The main contributions of DeepFEAv2 are: (a) a module that uses the FE connectivity matrix to organize input features by element and arrange them into an input sequence guided by the mesh topology; (b) a novel neural network architecture designed to process the input sequence and jointly predict NEO over time; and (c) a FEA-informed optimization strategy for regularizing these NEO predictions. DeepFEAv2 was evaluated on structured and unstructured 3D linear elastic datasets, as well as on a pressure-driven aortic valve dataset. DeepFEAv2 achieved R² values up to 0.99 and normalized errors as low as 0.38%. Compared with DeepFEA, it achieved up to 38.0% relative increase in R² and up to 87.1% reduction in normalized error. DeepFEAv2 also performed inference up to three orders of magnitude faster than traditional FEA. These results demonstrate that DeepFEAv2 can efficiently model transient FEA simulations across increasingly complex FE settings, providing a scalable surrogate framework for transient FEA.

articles.title: From IceCube to IT-Sphere: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical GNN for Banking IT Root Cause Analysis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.22822v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present Hybrid Quantum Root Cause Analysis (HQ-RCA), an industrially grounded workflow for root cause analysis in banking IT operations, built on a hybrid Quantum Graph Neural Network (QGNN): the classical backbone of DynEdge (the IceCube neutrino-reconstruction GNN, which we call standalone DynEdge), with its classification head replaced by a Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC). On 13 months of anonymised IT data (13k alarm clusters) from a major European bank, the hybrid QGNN matches standalone DynEdge -- the strongest classical baseline -- on F₁, while standalone DynEdge leads the ranking metrics. A readout-sensitivity and layout-robustness study, analysed via Dimensional Expressivity Analysis (DEA), shows that the effective parameter dimensionality (rank) of the quantum observable has no measurable correlation with F₁; we therefore keep the simplest readout langle Z₀rangle (the Pauli-Z expectation on the first qubit), which in the deployed layout is rank-1, collapsing optimisation to a 1-D problem solvable by a gradient-free grid scan. Execution on IBM Heron r2 (no error mitigation) shows this gradient-free readout is executable on NISQ hardware after threshold recalibration.

articles.title: End-to-End Quantum Semantic Communication with Variational Quantum Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents a quantum semantic communication (QSemCom) framework combining quantum machine learning (QML) and semantic communication (SemCom). Classical data are compressed into low-dimensional semantic representations, encoded and processed by a variational quantum transmitter, transmitted through a quantum channel, and processed by a trainable quantum receiver for classification. The framework considers a distributed quantum communication scenario in which quantum processing units (QPUs) exchange task-relevant semantic information through quantum links. While the general setting may involve multiple quantum nodes, this work focuses on the fundamental two-node case, with transmitter and receiver QPUs connected through a noisy quantum channel. Using MNIST, the framework is evaluated under ideal, bit-flip, depolarizing, and amplitude-damping channels. A baseline model is first trained over a perfect channel and evaluated under increasing noise without retraining. Receiver-side end-to-end training is then performed at fixed depolarizing-noise levels. The perfect-channel model achieves an accuracy of 0.9556 and an F1-score of 0.9551. Results show channel-dependent performance degradation, while receiver training substantially restores task performance under moderate and high depolarizing noise. Moreover, task recovery does not require reconstruction of the transmitted density matrix, highlighting a distinction between physical-state recovery and semantic-feature recovery. These results demonstrate that a trainable quantum receiver can recover task-relevant semantic information from noise-distorted quantum states and maintain high classification performance.

articles.title: Physics-guided deep metric learning with continuous time embeddings for open-world radar pulse de-interleaving
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25057v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Radar pulse de-interleaving is a foundational Electronic Support Measures (ESM) task that aims to separate chronologically interleaved pulse streams from multiple non-cooperative transmitters under unknown emitter cardinality in dense, contested electromagnetic environments. Classical histogram transforms and closed-world deep classifiers degrade under severe pulse loss, agile Pulse Repeti tion Interval (PRI) modulation, and spurious clutter. In this paper, we systematically characterise continuous temporal representations and physics-guided model selection in deep metric learning for open-world radar de-interleaving. Building on the transformer-based metric-learning framework for open-world deinterleaving introduced by Gunn et al. [1], we introduce a continuous Time-of-Arrival (ToA) sinusoidal positional encoding that directly models physical inter-pulse durations rather than ordinal token indices, a design choice that contrasts with [1], who found ordinal positional encodings provided no benefit and omitted them entirely. Neural network parameters are optimised solely via Supervised Contrastive (SupCon) learning, while scale-aware physical domain priors based on PRI Consistency and Angle-of-Arrival (AoA) continuity serve as physics-guided validation and checkpoint-selection criteria operating on unsupervised HDBSCAN cluster assignments.

articles.title: GINIO: A Geometric SO(3)-Equivariant Interface for Neural Inertial Odometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25338v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural inertial odometry increasingly uses networks as learned measurements inside filtering pipelines. Such measurements should transform consistently under arbitrary IMU mounting conventions: their mean must transform as a vector, and their covariance must transform congruently as a second-order tensor. We present GINIO, a geometric SO(3)-equivariant interface for neural inertial odometry under arbitrary rotations of the IMU measurement frame. Given calibrated IMU windows, our framework predicts a motion measurement and uncertainty obeying these tensorial laws. To support efficient sensor-frame learning, we introduce Last-Frame Alignment (LFA), a deterministic preprocessing step that is provably equivalent to world-frame training for SO(3)-equivariant predictors. The connected estimator tracks sensor-local states such as IMU bias, separating nuisance estimation from the geometric law enforced by the learned measurement. We instantiate the same interface in filter-connected NIO, AirIO-style recurrent aerial prediction, EqNIO-style full-SO(3) canonicalization, and ResNet-style temporal backbones. On TLIO, GINIO achieves 2.018 m ID/SO(3) ATE while EqNIO degrades to 76.389 m, using 11.6x fewer FLOPs. On NanoBench, our AirIO-style instantiation improves ATE from 5.579 m to 1.430 m without external attitude input, and our ResNet-style instantiation reaches 0.581 m ATE versus 0.645 m for ResNet1D. On Fetch, GINIO empirically reduces unseen physical-remount ATE from 8.15 m to 0.50 m without retraining, demonstrating robustness beyond the exact coordinate-frame guarantee. For uncertainty, spectral covariance reduces covariance-equivariance error by over three orders of magnitude compared with a diagonal head.

articles.title: Beyond Reconstruction Error: Analytical and Data-Driven Action Tokenization for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discrete action tokenization is central to autoregressive vision-language-action (VLA) models, yet action representations are often evaluated primarily through reconstruction fidelity. We ask which representation properties actually matter for closed-loop control by comparing fixed analytical, data-driven linear, and nonlinear neural representations under a unified tokenization interface. Across rate-distortion analysis, sequence-modeling diagnostics, and 3,500 LIBERO rollouts, representation rankings change with the evaluation criterion. PCA achieves lower nominal reconstruction error than Temporal-DCT, but produces less predictable token sequences and 3.0 percentage points lower mean seen-task success across three policy-training seeds, with the policy ordering reversing in one seed. In a matched seed-42 ablation, an autoencoder further reduces reconstruction error yet does not yield the strongest policy and exhibits greater sensitivity to discrete token perturbations. These findings show that reconstruction fidelity alone cannot reliably select action representations for autoregressive control, motivating joint evaluation of geometric fidelity, sequence predictability, decoder stability, and closed-loop performance.

articles.title: Bridge of Ψ's: Quantum Circuit Optimization with Schrödinger Bridges
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25947v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum circuit optimization replaces a circuit with an equivalent one of fewer gates and lower depth, reducing execution cost and error rate. We ask whether a generative model can learn this transformation directly from examples, rather than selecting from a fixed rewrite library or rigid algebraic routines. We present Bridge of Ψ's (BOPS), a generative model based on Schrödinger bridges, using a custom denoiser architecture, that learns a transformation from a source circuit into an equivalent optimized circuit. We train it on data constructed to be hard for existing optimizers, by applying rewrite rules backwards so that each input has a known lower-cost target. On held-out 8 qubits × 64 depth Clifford+T circuits, BOPS reduces gate count by 2.46× and depth by 2.45× in geometric mean, outperforming all nine baseline optimizers. This constitutes the first generative model bridging quantum circuits and frontier machine learning methods, opening up the quantum compilation stack to learned optimization along multiple axes.

articles.title: The AI Neuroscientist: An Interactive Agentic Interface for Neuroimaging Analysis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Analyzing neuroimaging data requires specialized coding and statistical expertise, which limits accessibility for researchers without computational backgrounds. We present the AI Neuroscientist, a language agent for interactive data exploration. The system integrates a large language model (LLM) with a neuroimaging toolset to perform quality control, modeling, and visualization. This allows researchers to query data quality and specify analysis parameters directly in natural language, providing a transparent and interactive alternative to conventional scripted pipelines for small-scale data exploration. We demonstrate these capabilities using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) data, and evaluate the agent on a custom fNIRS benchmarking suite against general-purpose LLM agents with code sandboxes. Future extensions will generalize the architecture to additional modalities, including functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data, and expand the benchmarking suite to additional fNIRS tasks.

articles.title: Real-Time Hand Gesture Recognition for OpenXR Using Transformer-Based Machine Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hand gesture recognition is a key component in human-computer interaction (HCI), enabling intuitive interfaces for applications in gaming, virtual reality (VR), robotics, and more. This study integrates transformer-based machine-learning models for real-time hand gesture recognition, using hand-tracking data captured through the OpenXR standard in Unity. We leverage positional data of hand joints and wrist rotation angles to train a custom gesture recognition system. By utilizing the sequential modeling capabilities of transformers, the system captures temporal dependencies within short gesture windows and classifies gestures robustly across hand orientations and sizes. The results show a significant improvement in gesture classification accuracy. Building on this, we outline how the approach can be extended toward detecting the flow of movement, i.e., the transitions between gestures, as future work.

articles.title: Weakly Supervised Quantum Error Mitigation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supervised approaches to quantum error mitigation learn a map from noisy circuit outputs to ideal ones, and therefore require the ideal outputs. Producing those ideal outputs demands noiseless classical simulation, whose cost grows exponentially with system size, so supervision is unavailable in exactly the regime where mitigation matters most. We ask whether cheap, individually unreliable signals drawn from circuit structure and hardware calibration can take the place of ideal labels. We assemble sixteen heuristic labeling functions (stabilizer and parity constraints, relaxation and readout characteristics, local depth, gate counts, and neighboring activity), reconcile their disagreements with a probabilistic label model, and read the resulting per-qubit error probabilities as a readout channel whose inverse mitigates the measured distribution. No ideal output enters the training path. On 147,000 five-qubit circuits executed on two IBM devices, the method removes 24.3% (Algiers) and 28.8% (Hanoi) of the Kullback-Leibler divergence to the ideal distribution, against 15.4% and 21.5% for the strongest published analytical baseline, a margin that holds on both devices and lies far outside its bootstrap interval. Supervised neural models trained on ideal distributions remain stronger where such labels exist, and we quantify that gap rather than setting it aside; the method's claim is to the regime where they do not, since the labels they require cannot be computed for the circuits mitigation is needed for. The codes will be released shortly.

articles.title: Towards Omni-dimensional GUI Agent Navigation with Masked Trajectory Prediction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graphical User Interface (GUI) Agents autonomously interact with software to fulfill user requests, where GUI navigation stands out as the most critical and challenging capability. Mastering this capability demands a complex synergy of step-wise decision-making, state-action alignment, and long-horizon planning. While directly mixing these corresponding navigation tasks seems intuitive to simultaneously acquire these skills, such a direct combination is severely bottlenecked by inconsistent optimization objectives and profound data heterogeneity. To overcome these barriers, we propose the MaP (stands for ``Masked Trajectory Prediction''), a unified framework that seamlessly harmonizes divergent GUI navigation tasks. By modeling multi-turn GUI interactions as a trajectory and defining training objectives through component masking and prediction, MaP shifts the optimization from task-specific marginal distributions to a consistent objective. Furthermore, to handle the data heterogeneity across multiple navigation tasks, we design a role-aware adapter learning module that dynamically routes each token to a specialized representation space. Extensive experiments on five representative GUI navigation benchmarks demonstrate that MaP effectively mitigates gradient conflicts and significantly outperforms the direct mixture training, establishing a robust paradigm for multi-task GUI navigation.

articles.title: VACS: Value-Aligned Compositional Shielding for Multi-Agent Reasoning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.26135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent reasoning systems in high-stakes domains must be both accurate and safe, yet agents often follow heterogeneous value priorities (e.g., rigor, conciseness, safety), causing conflicting recommendations. Existing methods do not jointly provide: (i) principled inference of each agent's implicit values from behavior, (ii) compositional formal safety guarantees without full online communication, and (iii) value-aware conflict resolution with faithful explanations. We present VACS (Value-Aligned Compositional Shielding), a four-layer framework addressing all three. Layer 1 learns value-dimension rewards from pairwise preferences using Bradley-Terry modeling and infers per-agent value weights via deep MaxEnt IRL. Layer 2 encodes value constraints in a Lean-inspired DSL and synthesizes compositional assume-guarantee shields for runtime safety. Layer 3 resolves disagreement through nucleolus-based credit allocation and Hamiltonian consensus optimization under long-term value constraints. Layer 4 extracts a critical reasoning path from co-state sensitivities and generates formally grounded natural-language explanations. Our contribution is primarily a unified systems design with formalized interfaces and operational guarantees at the verifier-constrained decision level, rather than a complete end-to-end formal proof of all language-model internals. In controlled proof-of-concept evaluations with role-conditioned agent panels on NEJM-AI QA, MathInstruct-Subset, and a cybersecurity incident-response benchmark (CyberSec-Eval), VACS outperforms strong baselines in accuracy (85.4%, 95.0%, and 90.0%) while reducing logical inconsistency rates to near zero.

articles.title: Neutral-Atom-based Quantum Optimization for Resource Allocation in NOMA Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.26556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In wireless communication networks, many resource optimization problems are nondeterministic polynomial-time hard (NP-hard) due to their combinatorial nature and high computational complexity. Recently, neutral-atom-based quantum computing has emerged as a promising platform for efficiently solving such problems by leveraging quantum superposition and entanglement. However, its application to wireless communication optimization problems remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we investigate the use of neutral-atom quantum platforms to solve the maximum access problem (MAP), formulated as a mixed-integer programming task that jointly considers admission control, user clustering, channel assignment, and power allocation in a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-enabled uplink network. To reduce the computational burden, the MAP is equivalently reformulated as a maximum independent set (MIS) problem in graph theory. This reformulation enables the use of the neutral atom platform based on Rydberg atom arrays, where the MIS problem is naturally encoded into the physical geometry and blockade constraints of the quantum system. Numerical results demonstrate the feasibility and potential of this approach for addressing large-scale wireless resource optimization problems.

articles.title: Quantum-Aided Active Device Detection in Energy-Harvesting Symbiotic Radio Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.26565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Massive connectivity in next-generation networks demands energy- and spectrum-efficient solutions for large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) deployments. Symbiotic radio (SR) enables passive IoT devices to communicate by backscattering existing cellular transmissions. A key challenge in uplink SR is active device detection (ADD), which directly affects decoding reliability, interference management, and system throughput. We propose an energy-harvesting code-domain non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-SR system in which IoT devices harvest energy from ambient uplink signals and backscatter information using low-density spreading (LDS) codes. To reduce the complexity of ADD, Grover's quantum search algorithm is employed, providing a quadratic reduction in oracle-query complexity over exhaustive maximum-likelihood (ML) search. Numerical results show that the proposed approach closely approaches ML performance while substantially reducing the number of search iterations, demonstrating its potential for scalable ambient IoT systems.

articles.title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.26760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents often handle streams of related tasks, yet standard harnesses repeatedly ask the model to reconstruct the same control decisions inside each task's context. We study whether task feedback can instead turn recurring control into reusable executable code, while reserving LLM calls for task-specific semantic reasoning. We introduce Growing Harness, a failure-guided training paradigm that learns the agent harness itself from a strategy-free scaffold that exposes fixed model and tool interfaces but encodes no task-solving controller. Function-level execution traces localize each failure to a bounded code surface, an optimizer repairs a window of failures jointly, and a success-first held-out gate rolls back repair sequences that harm prior capability. Accepted edits accumulate in one shared harness, allowing its control structure to emerge from task feedback. Across BrowseComp-Plus and WebArena-Verified with three deployment models from 4B to 120B parameters, Growing Harness achieves the highest mean success in five of six benchmark-model settings and trails the best mean by 0.7 pp. in the sixth. Relative to a Tool-Calling agent, it reduces LLM calls by 76.0-91.8% and deployed-agent inference cost by 74.4-98.6%. On WebArena-Verified, its success remains 44.7-45.3% across model scales, whereas Tool-Calling falls to 6.7% with the 4B model. Ablations show that trace-local edits, joint repair, and gate-based rollback each improve final success. These results show that persistent program growth can move recurring control out of model context and into low-cost code, yielding reusable specialist agents that remain effective with smaller deployment models.

articles.title: Geometric and Semantic Coupling for Interaction Understanding in 3D Scenes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25247v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interaction understanding in 3D scenes requires a joint description of movable parts, their motion, and the regions through which they can be operated. We present Segment-Snap, which connects these outputs through the physical relationship between parts and handles. Learned predictors identify broad part surfaces and small handles. A geometric decoder uses planar and upright priors to constrain motion, then selects hinge lines using predicted handle locations, without training a motion regressor. Conversely, a joint part-and-handle predictor supplies additional handle candidates, whose motion classes are refined using containing parts. Each information transfer is applied once, without iterative feedback. On Articulate3D validation, handle guidance raises motion-gated AP from 13.74% to 40.98% at fixed masks and axes. Additional handle candidates raise handle AP from 24.63% to 29.65%; part-based class correction adds 0.98 points, and full context reaches 30.99%. Repeated training, learned-decoder controls and paired visualizations establish the benefits and limitations of combining geometric and semantic evidence for interaction understanding.

articles.title: When Quantum Meets AI: Quantum Methods for Machine Learning and Machine Learning Methods for Quantum Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25641v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This thesis studies the intersection of quantum computing and artificial intelligence in two directions: quantum methods for machine learning and machine learning methods for quantum systems. For quantum machine learning, Neural Quantum Embedding learns data representations that increase the trace distance between embedded class ensembles, lowering an embedding-dependent bound on empirical risk and improving classification on noisy quantum hardware. A training objective based on the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product extends this approach to deterministic quantum computation with one qubit (DQC1) and is demonstrated on an NMR quantum processor. A margin-based generalization analysis then connects quantum neural network performance to quantum state discrimination. In the studied benchmarks, margin distributions predict generalization more reliably than parameter-count metrics. For quantum systems, a Mamba-based neural decoder for surface codes matches a reproduced Transformer baseline in memory experiments while reducing inference-cost scaling from quartic to quadratic in code distance. Under an explicit decoder-induced-noise model, it achieves lower logical error rates and a higher effective threshold. For neural quantum states, stochastic reconfiguration is interpreted as tangent-space ridge regression, with its diagonal shift controlling the bias-variance trade-off under finite Monte Carlo sampling. Multi-shift stochastic reconfiguration reduces checkpoint-local validation residuals and update variance relative to fixed-shift SR, at additional computational cost. Together, these contributions show how learned representations, statistical control, and hardware constraints shape the exchange between quantum computing and machine learning.

articles.title: StepTrigger: Contact-State-Triggered Backdoor Attacks on VLM-Powered Legged Robots
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.26131v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models and vision-language models are increasingly used as high-level planners in robotic systems, using task goals and sensor summaries to select navigation or manipulation actions. This creates a new backdoor surface: a compromised planner can behave normally in most runs, yet change its target selection when a hidden trigger is present. Prior attacks on LLM-powered or embodied agents mainly rely on triggers that appear in language, camera-visible objects, scene semantics, or specific sequences of past actions. This paper presents StepTrigger, a contact-state-triggered backdoor attack for VLM-powered legged robots. The trigger is not a prompt token or a visible marker. It is produced by pressure and foot-ground contact patterns that arise when a Unitree Go1 quadruped walks across a dense terrain patch. Unlike conventional visual or textual triggers, contact signals are inherently noisy and may also arise during benign locomotion. To avoid treating every pressure anomaly as a trigger, StepTrigger learns a selective backdoor policy from multimodal robot state, using incidental pressure events as benign examples and dense-patch contacts as poisoned examples. In a stratified offline evaluation, the trained planner achieved 98.75% clean behavior preservation, 92.50% false-trigger rejection, 76.25% true-trigger activation, and 89.17% overall parsed behavior accuracy. These results reveal a backdoor surface in proprioceptive and contact channels that is not captured by defenses focused only on language, vision, or action history.

articles.title: Co-Design of a Quantum Circuit using QGHNN for High Separate Fidelity and Maximum Grover Algorithm Accuracy
articles.abstract: A hybrid physics–machine-learning framework is introduced for the joint optimization of separate fidelity and Grover algorithm performance in superconducting quantum processors. The method combines a Hamiltonian-based open-quantum-system model of a two-qubit architecture coupled through a bus resonator with a QGHNN. Readout performance is evaluated via the Lindblad master-equation simulation of the dispersive measurement process, in which state-dependent resonator dynamics are mapped to realistic I/Q distributions and classified to estimate single-shot measurement fidelity. In parallel, algorithmic performance is assessed by simulating a two-qubit Grover search circuit in the presence of dissipation and dephasing, using effective cross-Kerr interactions derived from the underlying circuit parameters. A physically constrained dataset is constructed by sampling of some critical variables relevant to system. The QGHNN is trained to learn the nonlinear relationship between device parameters and the dual objectives of readout (separation) fidelity and Grover success probability. Gradient-based optimization is then carried out directly in parameter space using the trained network, yielding operating points that simultaneously improve measurement distinguishability and Grover algorithm accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate that the readout separation fidelity exceeds 99.4%, while the Grover success probability reaches approximately 86%, and this is comparable with the accuracy achieved by IBM Q5 Tenerife processor. Finally, the optimized parameters are used to implement the quantum circuit layout in Qiskit Metal, and their validity is further confirmed through EPR-based certification.

articles.title: Constitutive Modeling Method for AM 316 Based on Johnson-Cook Guided PCA-MLP Residual Learning
articles.abstract: Accurate prediction of dynamic flow stress for additively manufactured (AM) 316L stainless steel under high temperatures and high strain rates is critical for service safety evaluation and forming process optimization. To overcome limited accuracy of conventional empirical constitutive models and weak generalization of purely data-driven models under small datasets, this work develops a Johnson–Cook guided PCA-MLP residual learning model (JC-PCA-MLP). Taking the Johnson–Cook model as the physical baseline, principal component analysis (PCA) reduces dimensions of residual stress between experimental measurements and JC predictions. A multilayer perceptron (MLP) predicts PCA coefficients of residuals to reconstruct full stress–strain curves. Validated on dynamic compression data of AM 316L stainless steel across various temperatures and high strain rates, unseen intermediate temperatures (272°C and 450°C) are used for testing. The model achieves average R² of 0.9306 and 0.9538, average absolute relative errors (AARE) of 1.97% and 1.63%, and minimum R² of 0.8779 and 0.8909 at 272°C and 450°C, respectively. Compared with the JC, MLP and PCA-MLP models, JC-PCA-MLP delivers better prediction accuracy and stability. This work offers an efficient physics-informed data-driven strategy for dynamic constitutive modeling of additively manufactured 316L stainless steel.

articles.title: Sliding Friction Pair with Different Roughness
articles.abstract: Surface roughness governs the real contact area at the asperity level. The high-speed motion pair is currently moving at a high speed for weapons. Considering rotation, a calculation process was conducted on the friction and wear between the sliding pair in a high-speed rotating machine using a plane of Ra6.3 and Ra3.2, indicating that Ra3.2 has advantages over Ra6.3 when it has a certain firing rate. The wear condition of the movement and bolt/guide rail in different states. In higher firing rate Gatling guns, the guide rail should be processed more finely and have a smaller roughness. Higher Ra values reduce the number and increase the height of load-bearing asperities, leading to elevated local contact pressure per micro-contact according to the Greenwood–Williamson model. This concentrated pressure, combined with frictional shear under high sliding velocity, produces intense flash temperatures (Blok’s theory) and promotes localized plastic yielding or ratcheting. Consequently, the protective oxide film is disrupted more frequently, exposing nascent metal and accelerating adhesive wear. The deeper valleys on rougher surfaces also trap wear debris, inducing third-body abrasion. These coupled mechanisms explain why the Ra6.3 specimen exhibits an 11.5% higher peak stress and approximately 1000C higher interface temperature compared to the smoother Ra3.2 counterpart. For general machine tools, those within the range of Ra1.6 and Ra12.5 are not discussed, because they are not common in high-speed kinematic pairs.

articles.title: Enhanced Supercapacitive Performance of PANI/CdCrO₃/GO Ternary Nanocomposite: A Comparative Study with GO/CdCrO₃ Superior Electrochemical Performance of the Ternary Electrode
articles.abstract: The advancement of high-performance supercapacitors relies strongly on the development of electrode materials capable of efficient charge storage and energy delivery. In the present study, CdCrO3 and its graphene oxide (GO) hybrid composite with PANI were prepared using a facile and economical hydrothermal method and an in situ chemical oxidative polymerization method for potential supercapacitor applications. The structural, chemical, and morphological assessment was investigated by XRD, ATR-FTIR, and SEM techniques. Electrochemical evaluation demonstrated a remarkable improvement after GO and PANI incorporation, with the PANI/CdCrO3/GO electrode achieving a specific capacitance of 1715 Fg⁻¹ at 2 A g⁻¹, compared with 802 F g⁻¹ for the Binery CdCrO3/GO electrode. This study demonstrates the fabrication of two electrode configurations, namely CdCrO3/GO Binary and PANI/CdCrO3/GO Ternary nanocomposites. Although both sconfigurations exhibit favorable electrochemical characteristics, the Ternary device provides considerably improved charge-storage performance and maintains more than 50% capacitance retention at 1 A g⁻¹. The Ternary electrode configuration delivers a maximum energy density of 184.4 Wh kg⁻¹ along at a higher power density of 1007 W kg⁻¹, while for Binary electrode an 86.2 Wh kg⁻¹ energy density, at power density of 995.4 W kg⁻¹. These characteristics demonstrate the excellent energy–power balance of the PANI/GO/CdCrO₃ based device. Furthermore, the electrode system exhibits remarkable long-term durability, retaining 80% of capacitance with 1000 charge/discharge cycles. Overall, the outstanding rate capability, energy-storage performance, and cycling stability make the PANI/CdCrO3/GO supercapacitor a promising candidate for practical solid-state energy-storage applications.
authors: Aqeel Ahmed Shah Aqeel Ahmed Shah
M. Ajmal Khan M. Ajmal Khan

articles.title: Anthropogenic warming shifted southwestern Europe into fire-weather conditions exceeding operational suppression thresholds
articles.abstract: Anthropogenic climate change is increasing wildfire hazard worldwide, however how this growing risk will impact suppression efforts remains poorly quantified. Existing attribution studies have largely focused on meteorological fire danger, without assessing whether warming shifts fire-weather conditions beyond operational thresholds at which wildfire suppression becomes progressively ineffective. Here we combine global kilometer-scale simulations, constrained by spectral nudging to reproduce observed large-scale atmospheric circulation under 1950-like climate (Counterfactual), current climate (Factual) and + 2 K climate states, with empirical relationships between the Fire Weather Index, potential fireline intensity and expected operational suppression categories to quantify how anthropogenic warming altered the August 2025 wildfire crisis in the northwestern Iberian Peninsula. August 2025 simultaneously recorded the highest fire weather index values and largest burned area of the 1985–2025 record across the study region. We find that, relative to a 1950-like climate, present-day warming increased the spatial extent and persistence of fire-weather conditions associated with extreme wildfire events that render suppression virtually impossible (> 10,000 kW m⁻¹), with the exposed area increasing by 0.47 Mha (3.9%), while a + 2°C warmer climate further increased it by 0.92 Mha (7.6%). Consequently, exposure of protected areas, population and the wildland–urban interface to well beyond suppression capacity fire-weather conditions increased substantially. Our findings demonstrate that anthropogenic climate change is not simply increasing wildfire hazard, but progressively increasing the likelihood of the extreme wildfire events that significantly reduce opportunities for effective suppression.

articles.title: Optimal Grid Connection Capacity of a Hybrid Renewable Microgrid: An Energy Management and Economic Optimisation Model
articles.abstract: The paper presents a developed model for determining the optimal power of connection to the electric grid, which limits the possibility of introducing additional electric energy from the general grid (import) and withdrawing excess electric energy (export) in order to minimise the levelized cost of the microgrid. The model takes into account the daily cost of producing electric energy at generating plants, the daily cost of storing energy at a battery energy storage system (BESS), the daily cash flow, which includes the daily costs of purchasing electric energy from the grid to the microgrid, income from selling electric energy from the microgrid to the grid, purchasing fuel for a backup generating plant, the daily costs of paying for lost load for consumers in the form of penalties, and the daily costs of connecting to electric grids. The optimisation model proposes an economic algorithm to determine the priority power source's output (backup gas generator or import) based on an operational comparison between the market price "day in advance" and the backup generator's production cost. For a hybrid network, the structure of which includes a solar power plant (PV) with a power of 60 kW, a wind power plant (WPP) of 20 kW, a reserve power generator (RES) of 40 kW, a four-hour BESS with a nominal power of 50 kW and a nominal capacity of 200 kWh, with different loads of critical and non-critical consumers ranging from 40 to 240 kW across six scenarios, the optimal power of connection to the electrical network is determined, which, while ensuring the balance of electrical energy, allows reducing the cost of the microgrid to 2.8%.

articles.title: Borealisation of an Arctic marine ecosystem during the Last Interglacial
articles.abstract: The Arctic is warming at a rate four times the global average, threatening and overturning marine ecosystems. Here, we present a shotgun metagenomic sedimentary ancient DNA record revealing major reorganisation of an Arctic ecosystem west of Svalbard in response to the transition into the Last Interglacial (LIG), a warm period between 128 and 116 thousand years ago and an analogue for future warming. We document invasion of temperate phytoplankton communities (i.e. ‘borealisation’) into the Arctic, evidenced by increased cosmopolitan Gephyrocapsa coccolithophores, which contrasted diatom-based glacial systems. This shift was preceded by the proliferation of a highly diverse phytoplankton community enriched in smaller eukaryotes and potentially harmful algal bloom taxa. Given the important role of phytoplankton composition in the drawdown of atmospheric carbon dioxide, we consider the impact of the observed changes on the biological carbon pump. Marine megafauna, including whales and fishes lacking strict Arctic distributions, also increased at the start of the interglacial, showing borealisation extended to higher trophic levels. Our LIG data indicate substantial increase of inflow of Atlantic water into the Arctic, i.e. Atlantification, likely transporting heat and salt along with Atlantic organisms, and potentially reducing the Arctic’s capacity to sequester atmospheric CO2 under warmer climate conditions.

articles.title: A microbial index of biotic integrity integrates hydrochemical and microbial signals for ecological assessment of rare-earth mining-affected surface waters
articles.abstract: Rare-earth mining imposes compound hydrochemical stress on adjacent surface waters, but biological tools that integrate these pressures for mine-water assessment remain scarce. We integrated hydrochemical measurements, 16S rRNA amplicon-based microbial-community profiling, predicted functional potentials, and a microbial index of biotic integrity (M-IBI) to assess surface waters in two ion-adsorption rare-earth mining areas in southern China. An environmental stress axis was independently derived from 11 hydrochemical variables and a pH-deviation penalty before microbial metrics were screened. Sites at the high-stress end showed acidification, altered ionic composition, elevated sulfate and nitrate nitrogen, and metal-related signals. Bacterial communities shifted consistently along this gradient: Bacteroidota, Planctomycetota, and Polynucleobacter were associated with lower-stress conditions, whereas Pandoraea and Thermomonas showed stronger stress-response signals. Five non-redundant microbial metrics were integrated into a regional relative M-IBI (0.1932–0.8178), which was strongly negatively associated with the independent hydrochemical stress axis (Spearman r = -0.927). Leave-one-metric-out and leave-one-sample-out analyses indicated that this relationship was not driven by a single metric or sample. The study provides a technically explicit framework for integrating mine-water hydrochemistry and microbial responses in ecological monitoring. The index is intended as a regional relative assessment tool and should be independently validated across seasons and mining-restoration settings.

articles.title: Mineralogical and Geochemical Controls on the Sustainable Beneficiation of Hydrothermal Quartz from Egyptian Eastern Desert for advanced Applications
articles.abstract: The rising global demand for high-purity quartz (HPQ) in advanced technologies, such as semiconductors, photovoltaics, and optical systems, necessitates the identification and beneficiation of new high-grade quartz sources. This study presents a comprehensive investigation of the Marwit El Sweiqat quartz deposit, located in the Eastern Desert of Egypt, with a focus on its mineralogical and geochemical characteristics, impurity profiles, and beneficiation potential. The quartz body, of hydrothermal origin, exhibits favorable properties including coarse crystallinity, low structural defects, and an initial SiO₂ content averaging 99.45 wt%. Petrographic and geochemical analyses identified critical impurities such as Fe₂O₃, Al₂O₃, muscovite, feldspars, and fluid inclusions which primarily concentrated along grain boundaries and microfractures. A suite of dry high-intensity magnetic separation (DHIMS) experiments was conducted using a Rare Earth Roll separator, and the process parameters were systematically optimized through response surface methodology (RSM) and central composite rotatable design (CCRD). The optimized conditions (splitter angle of 85° and belt speed of 200 rpm) achieved removal efficiencies of up to 98.85% for Fe₂O₃ and 98.05% for Al₂O₃, reducing impurity levels to

articles.title: A Structure-Based Machine Learning Framework for Polymer Solar Cells: Prediction, Interpretation, and Virtual Screening
articles.abstract: Polymer solar cells (PSCs) have attracted extensive attention due to their lightweight, flexibility, and solution-processability. However, the performance of PSCs arises from the intricate coupling of molecular structure, energy-level alignment, charge generation, transport, recombination, and morphology, posing a significant challenge for rational materials design. With the accumulation of experimental data and advances in polymer informatics, machine learning has emerged as a powerful tool for accelerating PSC research. In this work, we construct the largest experimental database of 5,797 binary bulk-heterojunction PSC devices reported from 2010 to 2025 and develop an interpretable machine learning framework that predicts device performance directly from donor and acceptor structures. Random forest models using Morgan fingerprints achieve a strong prediction of power conversion efficiency (PCE), with R = 0.85 and RMSE = 1.94%. Statistical and Shockley-Queisser limit analyses show that historical PCE improvements have been driven primarily by short-circuit current density, whereas further gains increasingly depend on open-circuit voltage. Fragment-level SHapley Additive exPlanations reveal distinct structural roles: Y6-derived acceptors with ADA’DA architectures and INCN-type end groups contribute strongly to PCE and photocurrent, while donor fragments mainly regulate voltage. Screening more than 2.2 million virtual donor and acceptor combinations further indicates that high-performance systems occupy a restricted chemical space dominated by optimized Y6-derived acceptors paired with halogenated benzodithiophene-based donors. These results demonstrate how experimentally grounded, interpretable machine learning can clarify structure-performance relationships and guide the rational design and screening of organic photovoltaic materials.

articles.title: Broadband Dual-Core Microstructured Optical Fiber for Dispersion Compensation in Long-Reach Data Center Interconnects
articles.abstract: Chromatic dispersion accumulation in standard single-mode fiber (SSMF) can limit the transmission performance of long-reach data-center interconnects, particularly in dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) systems. To address this issue, a broadband dispersion-compensating microstructured optical fiber with a weakly coupled dual-core structure is proposed. The cladding region of the broadband dispersion-compensating photonic crystal fiber (B-DCPCF) is composed of periodically arranged air holes with a triangular lattice structure. By enlarging the diameter of the first-ring air holes and reducing the diameter of the second-ring air holes, a weakly coupled dual-core structure is achieved, which enables broadband negative dispersion characteristics. Numerical simulations are performed to optimize the structural parameters of the proposed B-DCPCF. The optimized fiber exhibits a broadband negative dispersion range of − 1150 to − 2613 ps/(nm·km) across the S-, C-, and L-bands. In the C-band, the dispersion compensation multiple (DCM) reaches 135.17, while the confinement loss remains below 0.1 dB/km throughout the entire band. At 1550 nm, the dispersion slope and relative dispersion slope of the B-DCPCF are calculated to be approximately − 8.47 ps/(nm²·km) and 0.0035 nm⁻¹, respectively. Its relative dispersion slope closely matches that of SSMF. This agreement enables the simultaneous compensation of chromatic dispersion and dispersion slope. The high DCM also reduces the required compensation-fiber length and facilitates compact dispersion management. These characteristics indicate that the proposed B-DCPCF has potential for broadband dispersion compensation in long-reach dense wavelength division multiplexing data-center interconnects.

articles.title: Extensional Lithospheric Architecture Controls Mantle Carbon Dioxide Transfer into the Crust and Focuses Conductive Pathways to Iron Oxide Copper-Gold Mineral Systems
articles.abstract: Iron oxide-copper-gold (IOCG) systems are typically associated with large-scale hydrothermal circulation along long-lived structural pathways, however, the three-dimensional lithospheric architecture connecting deep fluid sources to upper-crustal mineralisation remains poorly understood. Here, we present 3D magnetotelluric (MT) imaging from over 1,300 broadband sites across the eastern Gawler Craton and Olympic Domain in South Australia. The model images a series of conductive lower-crustal zones and vertically extensive pathways, which are interpreted as the preserved electrical footprint of deep fluid flow. In the northern Olympic Domain, including IOCG deposits at Olympic Dam, Acropolis, and Vulcan, these conductors form a strong linkage from the lower to upper crust, spatially associated with major IOCG systems, gravity highs, and displaced magnetic anomalies. We interpret this architecture as evidence for focused CO₂-rich supercritical fluid ascent, graphite precipitation and repeated structural reactivation linked to Hiltaba Suite-Gawler Range Volcanics magmatism. In the southern Olympic Domain, including IOCG deposits at Oak Dam, Carrapateena, Emmie Bluff and Mount Gunson, deep conductors are present but do not exhibit the same clear connection to the upper-crust. These results suggest that IOCG prospectivity beneath cover is imaged not only by the presence of deep conductors but also by the continuity, geometry, and preservation of conductive fluid pathways between lower-crustal roots and upper-crustal mineral systems.

articles.title: Geometric Origin of Quantization on an Adiabatically Evolving Manifold
articles.abstract: We propose a geometric mechanism for the emergence of quantization within a classical electrodynamics formulated on an adiabatically evolving Finsler space-time manifold. We show that a transverse electromagnetic field propagating on a nonstationary metric possesses a geometric adiabatic invariant with the dimension of action. This invariant, determined by the local cosmological parameters H and q, coincides with Planck’s constant h, suggesting a geometric origin of the quantum of action.Starting from a unified variational principle, we derive the nonlinear field equations and the equations of motion of charged particles. In this framework, quantization appears not as an independent postulate but as a compatibility condition selecting stable periodic self-consistent solutions. As an example, the relativistic Sommerfeld spectrum of the hydrogen atom is recovered directly from the proposed geometric framework.The proposed approach provides a geometric connection between space-time dynamics and quantum phenomena, suggesting that quantization may arise from the properties of an evolving space-time rather than being introduced as a fundamental axiom.

articles.title: Vortex-like coherent structures organize intermittent particle transport across turbulence states in a magnetized plasma
articles.abstract: Intermittent radial particle transport in magnetized plasmas is associated with localized coherent activity, but it remains unclear whether a common event dynamics persists across distinct turbulence states. We use a circumferential Langmuir-probe array in the linear plasma device PANTA to track large-amplitude local-flux events while varying the Argon gas pressure.In the laboratory frame, the fluctuations range from a streamer-dominated state to weakly organized turbulence and nonlinear solitary-wave states. Nevertheless, the large-amplitude transport events propagate with a long-wavelength background mode.Transforming to the frame moving with this mode, that is, the Galilean transformation, reveals a localized, vortex-like structure in the floating potential and radial E× B velocity throughout the pressure scan.The large flux tail is described by a stretched exponential with estimated exponents mostly between 1.25 and 1.55; the across-condition median is consistent with the 1.5 exponent obtained from a theoretical prediction using the instanton calculus for nonlinear coherent vortex-like structures.Event lifetime τ scales approximately linearly with event-integrated absolute flux P, τpropto P¹.⁰⁸±⁰.⁰⁵, indicating that the transport rate, P/τ, depends only weakly on the event lifetime. These observations identify co-moving localized structures as a common organizer of intermittent transport across plasma turbulence states and provide an experimental test of a large-amplitude prediction.

articles.title: Uncertainty-Aware Dual-Attention Temporal Convolutional Networks for Remaining Useful Life Prediction
articles.abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is a critical component of predictive maintenance systems for safety-critical industrial applications such as aircraft engine monitoring. Existing deep learning approaches primarily focus on predictive accuracy while often neglecting interpretability and uncertainty estimation, limiting their practical applicability in real-world maintenance systems. This paper proposes an Uncertainty-Aware Dual-Attention Temporal Convolutional Network (UA-DA-TCN) framework for aircraft engine RUL prediction using the NASA C-MAPSS benchmark dataset. The proposed framework integrates multi-scale Temporal Convolutional Networks with channel attention and temporal attention mechanisms to improve temporal degradation modeling and feature interpretability. In addition, Monte Carlo Dropout (MC-Dropout) is employed during inference to estimate predictive uncertainty and provide confidence-aware predictions. Experimental evaluation across all four C-MAPSS subsets demonstrates strong predictive performance under varying operating conditions and fault modes. The proposed model achieves RMSE values of 13.58, 17.55, 13.91, and 19.96 on FD001--FD004, respectively, outperforming the published CATA-TCN baseline on the challenging FD004 subset. Furthermore, the framework provides sensor-level interpretability and uncertainty estimation without significantly increasing architectural complexity. The results demonstrate that combining temporal convolutional feature extraction, dual attention mechanisms, and uncertainty estimation provides a practical and trustworthy framework for predictive maintenance applications.

articles.title: Coherence-Rate Graphs and the Trainability of Quantum Neural Networks Under Noise
articles.abstract: Every noise channel acting on a quantum neural network leaves a structural signature in the way it decays the coherences of the circuit, and this paper shows that the signature can be read before any training takes place. For the noise families that dominate practical device models, the decay rates within a charge sector of an equivariant network assemble into a weighted graph with closed-form edge weights, and the trainability behaviour of the circuit is organised by this coherence-rate graph. We prove a sufficient protection theorem on the graph, certified by a purely combinatorial construction from the circuit connectivity, we validate a predictor of the depth at which correlated noise degrades each trainable parameter, and we derive exact product laws for the measured degradation. We also refute the natural conjecture that operator-level decay bounds the measured decay, exhibiting explicit counterexamples with large gaps. A deterministic population benchmark, cross-validated to ten digits against an independent implementation, supplies exact targets for the statistical analysis and clarifies the finite-ensemble variation in the deep-circuit comparisons.

articles.title: Robust Fractional-Order PID Control of a High-Frequency Aerospace DC–DC Converter under Parametric and Bus Disturbances
articles.abstract: Aerospace DC networks combine large bus-voltage ratios, fast load changes, tight stability margins, and severe restrictions on size and filtering. These features make the voltage-control problem more demanding than nominal tracking alone suggests. This paper develops a robust fractional-order proportional–integral–derivative (FOPID) design for a high-frequency synchronous buck stage representative of a 270 V-to-28 V avionics interface. The averaged model incorporates inductor copper loss, line perturbations, and load-current disturbances. Controller synthesis is carried out directly in the frequency domain over bounded variations of input voltage, inductance, capacitance, load, and parasitic resistance. The proposed fractional controller employs proportional, fractional-integral, and fractional-derivative actions, with the fractional orders treated as additional design parameters to shape the closed-loop response and robustness characteristics. The resulting FOPID controller is compared with an integer-order PID designed under the same plant model and uncertainty description. A finite-frequency multiplicativeuncertainty envelope is constructed from all 32 interval corners together with 500 reproducible interior samples. Both designs satisfy the corresponding sampled small-gain test, while the FOPID controller yields essentially zero nominal overshoot, a shorter settling time, and lower controller gain near the 500 kHz switching frequency. Disturbance tests reveal a more nuanced result: the fractional controller improves recovery time but does not minimize every peak deviation. The study therefore identifies where the additional fractional degrees of freedom provide practical benefit without claiming universal superiority. All numerical data shown in the figures are embedded in the LATEX source to ensure direct reproducibility.

articles.title: Fault-Tolerant Fractional Control and Active Reconfiguration of Redundant Interleaved DC–DC Converters for UAV and Avionic DC Networks
articles.abstract: Fault tolerance in airborne DC power conversion is not only a component-level reliability problem; it is also a transient-energy problem because a fault must be detected, classified, isolated, and compensated before the protected bus leaves its admissible voltage region. This paper develops a mathematically explicit fault-tolerant architecture for a three-active-plus-one-spare interleaved buck converter representative of a 270 V-to-28 V UAV/avionic DC interface. The proposed framework combines four layers that are commonly investigated separately: an averaged multiphase converter model, model-based open-circuit fault residuals, Kirchhoff-consistency sensor-fault discrimination, and a fractional-order PI bus-restoration strategy. An exact residual expression is derived for an open-circuit phase under the averaged model, establishing finite threshold crossing whenever the commanded duty is nonzero. A second residual, constructed from the capacitor current balance, distinguishes an actuator-side open-circuit fault from a single current-sensor bias under ideal noise-free conditions. A capacitor ride-through condition is also introduced to determine an explicit upper bound on the admissible detection and reconfiguration delay. For the fractional-order controller, the post-reconfiguration stability problem is reformulated through a commensurate-order representation, which enables a direct Matignonsector stability assessment for the selected fractional order. Numerical experiments are conducted using a fixed-step averaged model that incorporates phase-parameter mismatch, a switch opencircuit fault, a subsequent current-sensor bias, a load increase, and an input-bus sag. The faulted phase is detected after 0.08 ms, the spare phase is engaged at 0.20 ms after fault inception, and the sensor bias is classified after 0.06 ms. With the selected parameters, the fractional controller maintains the 28 V bus above 27.35 V under the compound fault scenario and reduces the post-fault voltage integral absolute error by approximately 21.6% relative to the integer-order PI benchmark considered in this study. A 16-corner parameter study retains the bus voltage above 27.28 V. These results are model-based rather than flight-hardware validation; accordingly, the paper distinguishes mathematical guarantees from simulation-based evidence and states the assumptions required for practical implementation.

articles.title: Sustainable and Low-Cost Approach for Effective Remediation of Nickel(II) Ions Using NaOH-Modified Tea Waste and Its Biochar
articles.abstract: Nickel contamination in natural water bodies has become a major environmental concern, causing undesirable issues in ecosystems, requiring the remediation of Ni(II) from contaminated aqueous systems. Although many approaches have been in practice, biosorption provides a sustainable and low-cost methodology as a viable alternative. In this respect, this study investigates the potential of NaOH-modified tea waste adsorbent (STWA) and NaOH-modified tea waste biochar (STWB) for the remediation of Ni(II) from contaminated aqueous solutions. Application of Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, thermogravimetric analysis and point of zero charge confirms favorable surface characteristics for Ni(II) adsorption. Optimum conditions of 0.60 g and 0.30 g dosages, 20 min shaking time and 10 min settling time lead to the extent of removal of Ni(II) from 10 mg L-1 solution by TW and its biochar at 76% and 65%, respectively, for ambient pH and temperature, which are increased up to 95% and 98%, respectively, by NaOH treatment. Investigation of kinetics confirms efficient and superior biosorption, while the Weber–Morris intra-particle diffusion (IPD) model indicates multi-stage adsorption governed by film diffusion and IPD. Isotherm modeling indicates that STWB follows the Langmuir model, with a maximum adsorption capacity (qm) of 15.17 mg g-1, whereas the Freundlich model is suitable for STWA, with qm of 24.64 mg g-1. It is further determined that competing ions reduce adsorption efficiency, with STWB showing better stability. Regeneration is possible with HNO₃, HCl and EDTA with > 90% desorption, confirming the sustainable removal of Ni(II).

articles.title: Hydrostratigraphic 3D subsurface grid modelling of the Northwest German Basin: combining surface-based structural with voxel-based hydrostratigraphic modelling
articles.abstract: Large-scale 3D subsurface models constitute, among others, the foundation for groundwater flow simulations and management, geothermal potential assessment, carbon capture and storage (CCS) initiatives, as well as site selection strategies for nuclear waste repositories. As part of a larger project dealing with numerical predictions of subglacial meltwater erosion during future glaciations, we present a flexible workflow that integrates surface-based structural modelling with voxel-based hydrostratigraphic grid modelling to spatially model the complex fill of the Northwest German Basin. The modelling workflow is applicable to other sedimentary basins with complex fills and heterogeneous data coverage. The workflow was applied to construct regional 3D subsurface grid models to 2,000 m depth in an area of up to 50,000 km². For the model construction, we harmonised heterogeneous data sources, including borehole data, geological cross-sections, and existing structural 3D models, and utilised Permian to Quaternary hydrostratigraphic units. This approach enabled efficient property interpolation and the representation of both extensive and spatially restricted lithofacies, such as those associated with salt rim synclines and tunnel valleys. Model validation shows that the Nearest-Neighbour interpolation can cope with unevenly distributed data when guided by the structural framework model, and that the models reproduce relevant stratigraphic heterogeneities even where data coverage is heterogeneous.

articles.title: Capillary-Condensation-Dominated Moisture Sorption in Triple-Ion Cross-Linked Composite Gels for Reusable and High-Capacity Humidity Regulation
articles.abstract: A series of P(AM-co-AANa)/CaCl2/LiCl composite gels were successfully prepared via a one-pot free radical copolymerization strategy, realizing a triple-ion synergistic moisture absorption and conduction system. FT-IR, SEM, and TG results confirmed the successful construction of a cross-linked porous network with excellent thermal stability. The integrated Ca2+, Li+, and Na⁺ ions endow the gel with distinct functional advantages: Na⁺ provides sufficient fundamental absorption sites, Li⁺ optimizes low-humidity adsorption kinetics, and Ca2⁺ strengthens network rigidity through coordination cross-linking and effectively restricts excessive gel swelling. The composite gel exhibits a typical Type Ⅲ adsorption isotherm, and its moisture absorption behavior is predominantly governed by capillary condensation. The PANA30-Ca160 gel demonstrates excellent regenerability and cyclic stability, achieving complete regeneration within 24 h at 60°C and maintaining 98.2% of its initial absorption capacity after five cycles. The optimized PANA30-Ca130-Li30 gel presents outstanding comprehensive humidity-control performance, delivering a high equilibrium absorption capacity of 2.61 g·g-1 at 30°C and 90% RH (4.7 times that of pure PAM), while retaining 0.16 g·g-1 absorption capacity even under 30% low RH. The gel dehydration behavior follows non-Fickian diffusion kinetics, and the water release rate constant k increases significantly from 1.318 × 10− 3 to 4.879 × 10− 3 with increasing temperature from 30 to 70°C. Benefiting from multi-ion synergistic regulation and structural optimization, the proposed composite gel effectively overcomes the inherent trade-offs among high absorption capacity, anti-deliquescence performance, adsorption kinetics, and cyclic stability of traditional desiccants. This work provides a promising high-performance material for advanced humidity regulation applications.

articles.title: Trust-Aware Deep Policy Routing for Tactical Vehicle Ad Hoc Networks under Joint Mobility and Routing-Plane Attacks
articles.abstract: Tactical vehicle mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs) must sustain mission traffic under two simultaneous stressors: mobility-induced topology churn and adversarial manipulation of the routing plane by captured nodes (blackhole, grayhole, and sink-hole behaviors). Classical reactive and proactive protocols accept advertised routing metrics at face value, and single-purpose trust extensions address only one stressor. We present AIRouteOpt, a trust-aware deep policy-routing framework that selects the next hop with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) from per-neighbor link quality, a recursively updated per-neighbor trust score, and a short history of routing events, injecting trust as a continuous reward-shaping term rather than a hard threshold. We prove that the trust estimator concentrates around each neighbor’s true forwarding probability, derive a monotonic-improvement bound that accounts for topology drift, and show that the soft-trust reward generalizes hard thresholding. This last result explains our central finding: the learned policy matches a well-tuned threshold rather than exceeding it. In a Monte Carlo study over 12 seeds at a 20% blackhole/sinkhole attack, trust-awareness is decisive. AIRouteOpt delivers 63.0% of packets versus 46.3% for trust-blind baselines, a 16.7-point gain (paired p < 0.001), while matching the best hand-tuned trust-AODV (63.9%) at the lowest control overhead and with no exclusion threshold. Removing trust drops delivery to 45.7%. The benefit is confined to metric-advertising attackers; against a stealthy grayhole it is marginal. Inference costs 0.035 ms per decision with 5191 parameters.

articles.title: Shot saturation and evidence limits in quantum-AI hardware benchmarks
articles.abstract: Quantum benchmarks for artificial intelligence require measurement budgets, target observables, and execution records to agree. We reanalyze archived signed-overlap, kernel, and quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) summaries from a cloud-hardware campaign, retaining incomplete runs and distinguishing measured entries from imposed values. For eight signed-overlap submissions, increasing shots per batch from 256 to 2048 changes reconstructed root-mean-square error from 0.1335 to 0.1292. At 2048 shots, squared offsets of the empirical batch means account for 98.2% of the reconstructed error. This decomposition is descriptive; it does not identify a physical noise mechanism. An incomplete kernel contains 18 measured off-diagonal entries out of 45; filling the others with zero changes its observed-entry mean from 0.2220 to 0.0888. A source-label conflict prevents a matched provider comparison. Across 43 Rigetti QAOA submissions, size-group mean edge-cut fractions range from 0.4782 to 0.5010, but heterogeneous parameters and absent raw histograms limit interpretation. Earlier learning and simulation results obtained with graphics processing units provide exploratory supplementary evidence.

articles.title: Assessment of Metal-Organic Framework Incorporated Thin Film Nanocomposite Membrane in Real Seawater Desalination Via Pressure Assisted Osmosis
articles.abstract: This study presents the fabrication, characterization, and real seawater desalination performance of a microporous aluminium fumarate metal–organic framework (Al-Fumarate MOF) incorporated thin film nanocomposite (TFN) membrane synthesized for pressure assisted osmosis (PAO) applications. The membranes were fabricated through interfacial polymerization on a polyethersulfone support layer having nonwoven fabric support. The MOF was characterized using SEM, BET analysis while its stability in salt medium was confirmed using XRD analysis. The membranes were characterized by ATR-IR, SEM, XPS, AFM, contact angle and mechanical strength analysis. The membrane showed significantly better intrinsic transport features with a water permeability of 3.8 ± 0.22 Lm−2h−1bar− 1, NaCl rejection of 98.9 ± 1.1%, and a low B/A ratio of 8.9 kPa compared with the control membrane and conventional forward osmosis membranes. Real seawater PAO testing with 2M NaCl as the draw solution showed reliable performance at hydraulic pressures between 0 and 2 bar. The membrane with 0.05wt% of MOF attained a superior permeability-selectivity balance with stabilized flux of 9.35 Lm−2h− 1. The improved desalination performance was ascribed to the hydrophilic microporous framework of Al-Fumarate MOF that boosted water transport, reduced internal concentration polarization and improved membrane structural stability indicating potential candidate for seawater PAO desalination in high salinity seawater settings.

articles.title: Light beam 'swims' upstream through a quantum fluid by violating Newton's third law
articles.abstract: Just as a leaf drifts along with a stream, objects in other moving fluids normally drift along with the flow. That is, unless they exert energy to move against it. Although it may be less intuitive, light waves or photons work similarly. To move against a stream of light, an object or particle, like a photon, must either have an external force acting on it or actively use energy to move upstream.

articles.title: Scaling of qubit coherence in quantum dot based Majorana chains: Rabi and Ramsey oscillations of Majorana qubits formed by four and six quantum dots
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.25223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a theoretical study of the Rabi and Ramsey coherence time of Majorana-based qubits formed by double N-site quantum-dot artificial Kitaev chains, following the recent experimental realization arXiv:2607.09511. We generalize the qubit to two chains of arbitrary length and compare the Rabi and Ramsey oscillations of the four-dot and six-dot qubits, simulated with realistic disorder for three sets of parameters: small and large superconducting gaps, and the experimental parameters. We find that, in the pristine limit, the Rabi oscillation is independent of the chain length, whereas the Ramsey oscillation of the six-dot qubit suffers from larger leakage, because the third site suppresses the unwanted energy splitting away from the sweet spot but at the same time makes the deliberate splitting difficult to achieve, which requires a larger detuning that could excite the bulk. In reality with disorder, neither coherence time improves universally with the chain length. The Rabi coherence is set by the competition of three dephasing channels, and the additional dots pay off only if the fluctuation of the interchain tunneling is suppressed; the Ramsey coherence is set by the fluctuation of the energy splitting during the σ_z rotation, which for the four-dot qubit is fixed by the sweet-spot disorder alone and does not depend on the mean splitting, whereas for the six-dot qubit the detuning that generates the splitting adds a fluctuation growing with the splitting itself, so the additional dots pay off only for small splittings. This implies that a longer chain is thus a better quantum memory but not necessarily a better qubit under manipulation. Although topological protection is expected in a longer Kitaev chain qubit, observing it in the current Rabi and Ramsey measurement protocols remains an experimental challenge.
