Surface wind transport explicitly evolves observable weather variables, while upper-air inference uses learnable horizontal diffusion to approximate the missing influence of unavailable upper-air variables. A parallel data-driven diffusion branch captures complementary motion patterns, and an adaptive router integrates the two forecasts for station-level multivariate forecasting. Experiments on Weather2K and MeteoNet show that StationPDE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, reducing MSE by about 9.6% on average compared with the strongest baseline. Code and implementation details are available at https://github.com/hnu-vis/StationPDE.

articles.title: Uncertainty and Business-Aware Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Semiconductor Manufacturing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.22160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing relies on tightly interconnected components, so early identification of the assets most likely to fail is essential to prevent a single breakdown from disrupting the entire production pipeline. Maintenance planning must therefore balance unexpected failures against prematurely interrupted operating life. We present a Predictive Maintenance (PdM) framework combining Deep Learning (DL) sequence models and Simoultaneous Quantile Regression (SQR) for uncertainty-aware Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation and risk-aware maintenance decisions. Several architectures are compared on ion-milling data from the 2018 PHM Data Challenge (PHM18), including architectures based on State Space Models (SSM), using prediction and business metrics: Unexpected Breaks (UB), Unexploited Lifetime (UL), and a cost-weighted objective. Diagonal State Spaces (S4D) delivers the best Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimates across quantiles and, relative to Preventive Maintenance (PvM) baselines, substantially lowers business cost by avoiding systematically early interventions. The results support uncertainty-aware, cost-sensitive maintenance planning in semiconductor production.

articles.title: Beyond Task Completion: Training Capable and Safe Computer-Use Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.22178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) have made rapid progress in completing complex tasks through graphical user interfaces, yet post-training centered on task success alone does not induce reliable safety behavior. A reliable CUA must condition its execution on risk: it should complete ordinary benign tasks, avoid environmental hazards and continue when a safe completion path remains, and refuse when the goal is harmful or no safe path exists. To learn this conditional policy, we develop Safety and Capability Optimization for Policy Execution (SCOPE), which jointly post-trains a CUA for task-execution capability and safety-aware decision making. To provide aligned training data for this joint objective, we further introduce SCOPE-Gen, an automated pipeline that synthesizes verifiable capability tasks and converts them into paired environment-risk variants while preserving their original goals. Using the resulting tasks, we construct SATraj-OS, a trajectory dataset comprising capability demonstrations, safe continuations, and explicit refusals. SCOPE first learns from all three trajectory types through supervised fine-tuning and then further improves task completion through online reinforcement learning. Starting from Qwen3.5-9B, SCOPE-RL achieves a 54.17% task success rate on OSWorld and a 64.30% attack-avoidance rate on OS-BLIND, yielding the best aggregate capability--safety score of 58.80% among the evaluated agents. Ablations reveal asymmetric but complementary roles for the two forms of safety supervision: refusal trajectories account for most of the attack-avoidance gain, whereas risk-handling trajectories preserve greater task utility at comparable attack-avoidance levels.

articles.title: Universal Observatory Graphs for Distributed Sky Coverage and Artificial Intelligence Based Interplanetary Routing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.22244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This research proposes the Universal Observatory Graph (UOG), an AI-driven framework for distributed astronomical observation across the Solar System. The proposed architecture models autonomous observatories located at the Sun planet L2 Lagrange points as nodes in a weighted graph, while communication links are represented as graph edges characterized by multi-objective physical and operational metrics, including interplanetary distance, communication latency, transmission power, and link reliability. The resulting graph provides a unified mathematical representation of a cooperative interplanetary observatory network. This proposal examines a six-observatory Solar System configuration comprising Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Instantaneous sky coverage is evaluated independently using a 200,000 direction Fibonacci sphere, a 2,000,000 direction fixed seed Monte Carlo calculation and deterministic spherical integration. All three methods yield complete network union coverage, approximately 0.43% complete six observatory intersection and approximately 24.96% mean pairwise Jaccard similarity under the adopted pointing model. Communication routing is subsequently formulated as a finite horizon Markov decision process and solved using tabular Q-learning. The reward balances node participation and a distance dependent reliability proxy against distance, light time latency and a distance squared transmission power proxy. The learned Earth-Saturn-Uranus-Neptune route is also the highest discounted return route among all 41 feasible simple paths under the four hop constraint. The framework provides a reproducible baseline for sequential coverage assessment and multi objective routing; time dependent ephemerides, mission specific visibility, calibrated link budgets and scalable graph policies remain future work.

articles.title: TWIG: A Time-Causal Wavelet Operator for Autoregressive Forecasting on Irregular Graphs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.22585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce TWIG (Time-Causal Wavelet Operator for Irregular Graphs), a graph-native neural operator for autoregressive surrogate modeling on static irregular graphs. TWIG transforms each node history into causal multiscale temporal features that separate recent variation from progressively slower memory components, then propagates these features through graph-wavelet operator blocks with gated pointwise channel mixing. The architecture is causal by construction and designed for closed-loop forecasting, where predictions are recursively reused as future inputs. We evaluate TWIG on three irregular-domain forecasting problems spanning regional diffusion, three-dimensional subsurface hydrology, and aerodynamic flow, with graphs ranging from 400 to 5,233 nodes and model capacities from approximately 70k to 10M parameters. TWIG achieves the lowest aggregate rollout errors on the subsurface-hydrology and regional-diffusion benchmarks and ranks second on the 10M-parameter aerodynamic-flow benchmark, behind the GPS Transformer. Across all three settings, TWIG consistently outperforms the corresponding non-time-causal Graph WNO baseline. These results demonstrate that TWIG provides an effective and scalable approach to stable autoregressive forecasting of dynamical fields on irregular graphs.

articles.title: LPINNs: First-Layer Gated Localization for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.22984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) use one shared representation over the computational domain, which can become difficult to optimize on long domains and for high-order operators. We study a minimal alternative: multiply the first hidden activation of an otherwise unchanged dense PINN by input-dependent localization functions, giving first-layer units receptive fields without partitioning the domain or adding interface losses. We screen 13 families of localization functions, in up to three parameterizations each, on a nonlinear harmonic oscillator (HO), a heat equation on a long spatial interval, and a manufactured four-dimensional (4D) fourth-order problem, with ten paired seeds throughout. Three configurations give large reductions in solution error at matched budgets: (i) Fixed Gaussian localization functions on the 2π HO domain cut mean solution RMSE from 4.8369×10⁻¹ to 8.83×10⁻³ at 3k epochs. (ii) The inverse-quadratic family with learnable centers and widths cuts it from 2.896×10⁻¹ to 3.06×10⁻² on the 8π heat domain at 10k epochs. (iii) Fixed bump localization functions cut it from 1.75947×10¹ to 2.260×10⁻¹ on the 4π 4D domain at 10k epochs. Every paired seed improves in these three comparisons. The screen also shows that the mechanism is not a free win: on HO only 2 of 13 families beat the baseline, and 10 of the remaining 11 are 9 to 23 times worse; on 4D four families are non-finite and five are more than three orders of magnitude worse than the baseline. The inverse-quadratic family is the only one that beats the baseline on all three equations. Overall, these results show that first-layer localization can provide measurable improvements to baseline PINNs on long-domain and high-order problems.

articles.title: K-TRAIL: Simulator-Guided Generative Design of EM/RF Circuits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.23183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inverse design of RF and electromagnetic (EM) circuits is challenging because the relationship between circuit layout and electrical response is non-unique, and full-wave simulation is computationally expensive. This paper presents K-TRAIL, a simulator-guided generative framework for automated EM/RF circuit synthesis. K-TRAIL combines diffusion-based layout generation with derivative-free ensemble Kalman guidance, allowing feedback from a black-box EM simulator to refine candidate layouts during generation without requiring adjoint sensitivities or differentiable solver models. The framework supports both synthesis from prescribed S-parameter responses and synthesis directly from RF performance constraints. Experiments on multi-layer RFIC structures show that simulator-guided generation improves agreement with target responses and can identify structurally distinct layouts that satisfy circuit-level design requirements. The proposed approach provides a practical path toward generative, verification-aware RF circuit design while retaining the flexibility to explore diverse layout topologies.

articles.title: Physics-residual machine learning predicts oxygen-evolution catalyst activity beyond the training range from sparse polarization measurements
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.23549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Screening oxygen-evolution catalysts on combinatorial libraries requires deciding which candidates receive the remaining measurements. The deciding activity lies beyond each candidate's measured potential window and often above every activity recorded during fitting. We predict it by physics-residual machine learning: the Tafel equation extrapolates the candidate's own measured current and slope, a learned residual attenuated with feature-space distance corrects the magnitude, and an applicability-domain score identifies predictions above the training range before measurement. In a separately fabricated 322-candidate library, 282 above the training maximum, two measurements per candidate gave a mean absolute error of 0.203 mA cm⁻² against 1.330 for the selected data-driven machine-learning model. Errors inside the training range remained comparable, and 35 labelled catalysts were enough to fit it. In two independent datasets the same construction lowered the overpotential error by 29 to 52%. Campaigns can therefore shorten each measurement and still rank the most active compositions.

articles.title: Cost-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Action Masking and Projection for Battery Energy Storage Dispatch under Suppressed-Spread Market Shifts
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.23590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Battery energy storage system (BESS) dispatch must preserve operational feasibility while declining price spreads reduce the margin available to pay for cycling. We study a proximal policy optimization (PPO) controller whose pre-selection physical action mask and emergency projection are separated from a causal, forecast-informed economic advisory. All forecast-dependent methods receive the same causal 24-step forecast and grid-side settlement. Across five PPO seeds, advice-on net profit is 30.59 and 18.04 USD per 336-hour T1 and T2 window, versus 36.77 and 22.94 USD for proxy-cost MPC; PPO remains below this reference in both periods. Advice raises T2 profit from 16.45 to 18.04 USD while reducing throughput, but is immaterial in T1. On disjoint weekly blocks, PPO is stable under daily, weekly, and blended seasonal forecasts, weakens under persistence, and remains below proxy-cost MPC. Paired diagnostics localize changes to the observed 5-10 USD/MWh regime with mixed SoC-dependent effects. An M0-M6 ablation shows that mask removal sends thousands of infeasible requests to projection, while removing both physical layers exposes ramp violations. The evidence separates economic screening from feasibility enforcement without claiming formal safety, lifecycle-optimal aging, or RL dominance.

articles.title: GenVoid: Uncertainty-Aware Learning of Subsurface Material Defects with an Experimentally Validated Physics-Informed Generative Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.23761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Internal voids are ubiquitous defects in manufactured structures, yet their characterization remains challenging because their geometry is hidden and can only be inferred indirectly from accessible measurements. Here we introduce GenVoid, a physics-informed generative model-based framework for identifying internal voids in complex two- and three-dimensional solids from surface displacement measurements alone. By incorporating the governing mechanics into a generative inference framework, GenVoid enables void identification across linear elastic, hyperelastic and plastic material behaviours and accommodates complex two- and three-dimensional structural geometries. Importantly, the framework explicitly accounts for uncertainty and noise in displacement measurements, producing probabilistic reconstructions of internal void geometry rather than a single deterministic estimate. We demonstrate the approach using high-fidelity synthetic datasets and experimentally measured displacement fields obtained from in-situ mechanical experiments, establishing its ability to infer hidden voids from realistic displacement measurements. To quantify the fundamental limits of such inference, we further introduce an observability measure that characterizes the sensitivity of boundary measurements to localized stiffness perturbations within the interior under an ensemble of applied loads. This framework provides a direct connection between defect location, sensor configuration and reconstruction fidelity, enabling systematic assessment of how the number and spatial distribution of boundary measurements govern void-identification accuracy. To this end, these results establish a physics-informed and uncertainty-aware approach for non-invasive characterization of hidden defects and provide a quantitative basis for designing measurement strategies for inverse problems in solid mechanics.

articles.title: The Neural Forcing for Three-Dimensional Incompressible Navier-Stokes finite time blowup
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.23934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a two-part neural framework for forced three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes flow. Part~I develops the computational forcing system. A physics-informed neural model generates structured external-force trajectories, candidates are optimized through differentiable PDE rollouts or PPO-Clip, and selected forcings are frozen and checked by independent fixed-force replay. Part~II provides the mathematical certification layer. It separates neural candidate discovery from continuum analysis, derives integrated reciprocal-vorticity criteria that imply Riccati-type growth and finite-time loss of smooth continuation, develops a validated computational-to-continuum transfer strategy, and establishes a conditional positive-probability closure for a nondegenerate neural output law. The proof is complete at the continuum level.

articles.title: Graph-to-Grid (G2G): Continuous-Coordinate Feature Painting for Soccer Pass Surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.24040v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dense pass surfaces give, for every pitch cell, whether a pass played there would arrive, whether the carrier would choose it, and what the possession would then be worth. The networks that draw them read the state as a raster of per-cell counts, losing where inside a cell each player stands. LiDAR detectors, bird's-eye-view perception and graph weather models move entity features onto a grid, binning each entity to a cell or learning the transfer. We evaluate the interpolated form: each player's features are scattered bilinearly onto the grid at the player's measured coordinates, so the surface loss trains the per-player encoder end to end. Those systems adopt an interface; this paper measures one. On 53,628 passes from the 2022 World Cup, painting improves selection likelihood over the same core fed rasters alone by about a quarter of a nat: in every match of an eight-fold cross-validation, with every arm tuned over five seeds, and after retraining on seven Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga matches from another provider. Thirteen pre-specified studies locate the gain: painting the nine raw player features with no encoder carries three quarters of it, and the learned encoder and message passing add a smaller, resolved increment. Painting also helps the original SoccerMap and a canonical U-Net, whereas offset channels, a finer raster, an attention painter and a raster-free decoder do not. Frozen across the provider boundary the likelihood advantage is lost; injected tracking error compresses it. These results concern observed-endpoint prediction, not calibrated evaluation of hypothetical passes.

articles.title: Conformal Robustness in Prediction-Driven Decision-Making
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.23170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern prediction-driven decision systems often rely on black-box predictors, but a point forecast alone does not provide the uncertainty scale required for robust downstream decision-making. We build a score-calibrated robustness framework that converts any fixed point predictor into a decision-relevant uncertainty representation through distribution-free conformal calibration. We use the conformal score, rather than a particular uncertainty set, as the primitive unit of robustness. The same score determines coverage-calibrated uncertainty sets for reliability-based robust optimization and normalizes target violations in a target-oriented formulation, Conformal Robust Satisficing. This formulation induces a conformal fragility measure that quantifies how rapidly performance deteriorates as the realized parameter departs from the forecast on the conformal score scale. For objective-uncertainty problems under standard convexity and duality conditions, we show that the reliability-based and target-oriented formulations parameterize the same score-calibrated robust decision frontier. This equivalence yields a data-driven mapping between reliability levels and acceptable targets and characterizes the marginal cost of robustness. Synthetic experiments validate the theoretical guarantees and illustrate the reliability-target correspondence. A real-data online-grocery case study demonstrates how the interface combines deep-learning demand forecasts with tractable inventory optimization, thereby improving reliability and reducing operational costs. Overall, our work shows that conformal scores endow fixed black-box predictors with an interpretable uncertainty scale for downstream decision-making while enabling reliability guarantees, acceptable-target selection, and fragility analysis within a unified framework.

articles.title: Bayesian Filtering in Physical Systems via Test-time Trained Flow Matching
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.23383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian filtering provides a principled framework for online state estimation under uncertainty, yet its application to systems with high-dimensional states and complicated posterior distributions remains challenging. Recent generative models, such as flow matching, have shown potential in Bayesian filtering. However, they still rely on particle-based representations of the posterior, which lose the rich information of the full distribution, or tackle a trajectory-level inverse problem that conflicts with the recursive structure of Bayesian filtering. To address this, we propose a new perspective of directly encoding the evolving distribution into flow matching model weights, namely, the Belief Flow Filter (BFF). It is a generative filtering framework that updates model weights via gradient descent at test time to track the posterior evolution. Thereby, BFF bypasses the scalability issue of particle representations or the flexibility limitation of Gaussian assumptions in conventional filters. We theoretically justify that the BFF design is structurally aligned with Bayesian filtering, and its training objective targets the recursive filtering operator. BFF is empirically verified across 5 different physical systems, including ones with chaotic dynamics and highly sparse, non-linear observations. The results show that BFF attains the best score in 8 of 9 metric-benchmark cells across the three standard 1D and 2D PDE benchmarks, and similarly leads on the extreme single-moving-sensor setting and on a real-world-grounded tokamak plasma estimation task, demonstrating its potential to accurately approximate the Bayesian filtering operator in high-dimensional probability space.

articles.title: Vector-Valued Distributional Reinforcement Learning Policy Evaluation: A Hilbert Space Embedding Approach
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.18952v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose Kernel Embedding Distributional Reinforcement Learning (KE-DRL) an offline method to estimate kernel mean embeddings of conditional multivariate return distributions from observed offline trajectories with continuous state-action inputs and vector-valued rewards. KE-DRL approximates the conditional embedding and estimates its a finite-dictionary representation coefficients through a maximum mean discrepancy Bellman criterion. For a regular class of return distributions, we show that a Matérn embedding and a Bellman-invariant Sobolev-moment class identifies the unique distributional Bellman fixed point and and derive a Hölder-type bound that controls Wasserstein error by the population embedding Bellman residual. For directly observed responses, we provide finite-sample and uniform error bounds for a regularized conditional mean embedding estimator. Simulation experiments evaluate pointwise embedding recovery against Monte Carlo benchmarks across multiple behavior-target policy pairs. An application to Expedia hotel-search data illustrates conditional multivariate return evaluation under two policies.

articles.title: GNet: A scalable and flexible Gaussian process network with nonparametric neurons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.10735v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We build GNet, a scalable and flexible Gaussian process network with nonparametric activation functions. The key computational contribution is to make estimation of GP activations computationally scalable without forming covariance matrices explicitly. We provide theoretical studies comparing function classes with a fixed architecture, and derive predictive risk bounds for GNets. Using essentially the same architecture and optimization settings, GNet shows competitive performance across a diverse range of test problems, including predicting nonlinear functions, nonparametric regression of real-world data, and predicting one-body direct correlation functions with high-dimensional inputs in classical density functional theory. The strong performance of GNet suggests that flexible nonparametric neurons can substantially reduce the number of trainable parameters while remaining computationally scalable.

articles.title: Does enforcing physics improve evapotranspiration downscaling? A controlled comparison of mass-conserving and direct deep-learning models for WaPOR
articles.abstract: Satellite evapotranspiration products underpin agricultural water accounting. Yet the field-scale (20 m) data irrigation needs exist for only a handful of sites, whereas coarse (≈ 300 m) products span the entire African continent. This motivates deep-learning downscaling of the continental product to field scale. Physics-informed networks that enforce hard conservation constraints are widely advocated, on the premise that they improve accuracy and transfer. Yet this premise is rarely tested in a controlled way. To our knowledge, this is the first controlled test of it for evapotranspiration downscaling. It is also the first to adapt image-restoration and geospatial foundation models to the task, and to transfer across contrasting African agro-climates. We downscale WaPOR actual evapotranspiration (ETa) from Level-1 (≈ 300 m) to Level-3 (20 m). Inputs, training, sites, and protocol are held fixed across ten African irrigation pilots. We compare three direct super-resolution models (a compact SwinIR transformer, a Prithvi Vision Transformer, and their ensemble) against a physics-compliant network (PRSN). Direct models explain 78–91% of L3 ETa variance and transfer zero-shot to unseen agro-climates. They roughly halve naive-upsampling error and beat an operational per-pixel baseline. A compact 1.8 M-parameter SwinIR matches the 300 M-parameter Prithvi foundation model. The physics-compliant models keep their guarantees but are less accurate at every site, by ≈ 6% to ≈ 47% in relative RMSE. Neither a Budyko nor a Penman–Monteith anchor closes the gap. Hard constraints therefore buy consistency, not accuracy. Direct super-resolution is the practical route to field-scale ETa across the whole of Africa.

articles.title: Experimental Investigation on the Mechanical Characterization and Impact Behavior of Shot-Peened Al7068 Hybrid Composites Reinforced with SiC and Si₃N₄
articles.abstract: This study investigates the effects of Silicon Nitride (Si₃N₄) and Silicon Carbide (SiC) particles on the mechanical properties of Al7068 alloy. It aims to evaluate the potential of hybrid composites to meet engineering needs, such as aerospace applications. The Al7068- Si₃N₄/SiC composite was fabricated using the stir casting technique, with varying percentages of micro-Si₃N₄ (0%, 1%, 0.5%, 0.5% & 1%) and micro SiC (0%, 1%, 1.5%, 2.5% & 2%) particles. Mechanical tests were conducted to determine the impact strength before and after shot peening of the developed hybrid composites. These mechanical properties of the developed Al7068 reinforced with Si₃N₄ & SiC micro particles show the high potential for resistance to impact failure. A microstructural analysis shows a uniform dispersion of Si₃N₄ and SiC reinforcement particles within both the as-cast material and the Al7068 metal matrix composites. Integrating Si₃N₄ & SiC micro particles can create a high-performance composite suitable for aerospace applications that require a combination of lightweight properties and enhanced tensile strength.

articles.title: Efficiency of vB_BvS_ZagBV02 Phage in Controlling Antiseptic-Tolerant Brevundimonas vesicularis
articles.abstract: Brevundimonas vesicularis has emerged as an opportunistic pathogen with reduced susceptibility to antiseptics, posing a challenge for infection control. This study investigated the genetic basis of antiseptic resistance and evaluated the lytic phage vB_BvS_ZagBV02 as a potential antibacterial agent. PCR confirmed the presence of the antiseptic-resistance gene (qacE) in B. vesicularis. Phage vB_BvS_ZagBV02 showed a siphovirus-like morphotype, with an icosahedral head measuring 57 nm and a tail 142.8 nm in length. The phage vB_BvS_ZagBV02 adsorbed to host cells within 15 min, completed its infection cycle within 45 min, and had a burst size of approximately 296 phage particles per infected cell. The phage remained stable at pH 3–9 and at temperatures up to 80°C, retained infectivity for 7 months at 4°C and under freezing conditions and remained viable for 4 months at 37°C. Host range analysis showed infection of another Brevundimonas strain but no activity against the other tested bacteria. In planktonic culture, the phage reduced the bacterial growth at all tested multiplicities of infection (MOIs), while on stainless steel surfaces complete elimination of antiseptic-tolerant B. vesicularis was achieved when combined with antiseptic treatment at MOI 1 and 10. Genome analysis showed that vB_BvS_ZagBV02 was assembled as a single contig of 42,502 bp with a GC content of 67.52% and contained 62 predicted coding sequences, with no tRNA genes, antimicrobial resistance genes, virulence-associated genes, or lysogeny-related genes. Comparative analyses using BLASTn, VIRIDIC, ViPTree, and tail protein phylogeny showed that vB_BvS_ZagBV02 is distinct from the selected reference phages and does not cluster closely with currently available genomes. These findings support the potential of vB_BvS_ZagBV02 as a phage-based approach for controlling antiseptic-tolerant B. vesicularis.

articles.title: Analysis of Stresses and Displacements in Two-Layer Inhomogeneous Hollow Cylinders Using the Complex Potential Method
articles.abstract: This study presents an analytical solution for the thermoelastic state of a long, two-layer hollow cylinder composed of inhomogeneous materials under mixed boundary conditions. By accounting for distinct thermoelastic properties and internal heat generation within layered structures, this research addresses a significant gap in the existing literature. The thermal field is determined by expressing the temperature function as a power series. Leveraging the classical and effective Kolosov--Muskhelishvili complex potential method, the thermoelastic problem is transformed into the complex domain. This approach simplifies the analysis of displacements and stresses induced by thermal loading. To ensure high analytical precision, the particular solution for the resulting mixed boundary-value problem is sought in the form of a Laurent series of a complex variable. The surfaces of the layers are assumed to be either thermally insulated or maintained at zero temperature. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that the internal stress field is significantly influenced by the intensity of the internal heat source. The derived formulas provide crucial insights into the distribution of thermal stresses and displacements in non-homogeneous layered structures. Given that these results pertain to complex thermal loading conditions, they hold great significance for high-performance engineering applications. Mathematics Subject Classification: 374B10, 74K25, 30E25, 74E05, 74S25

articles.title: Optimization of Milling Parameters for Hybrid Sisal-Cotton Fiber Reinforced Polymer Composites Using Taguchi Method
articles.abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable, lightweight, and high-performance components in the automotive sector has accelerated interest in natural fiber-reinforced polymer composites (NFCs). However, machining these materials poses formidable challenges due to their heterogeneous and anisotropic nature, frequently causing fiber pull-out, delamination, and matrix cracking that degrades surface quality. To address this issue, this study proposes an intelligent artificial neural network (ANN)-based framework integrated with genetic algorithm (GA) optimization and Taguchi methodologies to predict and optimize machining responses during CNC end milling of hybrid sisal-cotton fiber-reinforced epoxy composites. The hybrid composites were fabricated using the cost-effective hand lay-up method following targeted chemical mercerization with 5% NaOH for cotton yarns and 8% NaOH for sisal fibers for 1 hour. Laminates with 10 and 30 wt% fiber mass fractions and random, bidirectional, and unidirectional configurations were characterized through tensile, compressive, flexural, and Charpy impact tests. CNC milling experiments were subsequently conducted using a Taguchi L9 orthogonal array by varying spindle speed (1000–2000 rpm), feed rate (100–300 mm/min), and depth of cut (1.0–2.0 mm). Levenberg-Marquardt backpropagation ANN models were developed to predict material removal rate (MRR) and average surface roughness (Ra). Sample 1, configured with a 30 wt% fiber mass fraction and short (2 mm) random orientation, exhibited the highest tensile, compressive, flexural, and Charpy impact strengths of 62, 44, 336.91, and 0.738 N/mm², respectively. ANOVA revealed that feed rate was the dominant factor affecting MRR, contributing 65.85% (P = 0.036), whereas depth of cut predominantly influenced Ra, contributing 54.48% (P = 0.023), followed by spindle speed at 28.44% (P = 0.0438). Taguchi optimization identified 1000 rpm, 200 mm/min, and 1 mm as the optimal cutting conditions for surface smoothness, while validation demonstrated only 1.28% prediction error for Ra under optimized conditions. The proposed ANN-GA-Taguchi framework provides a robust and reliable approach for pre-machining simulation, process planning, and optimization, reducing dependence on costly and time-consuming physical trials and supporting sustainable manufacturing of hybrid NFCs.

articles.title: Multi-Time-Scale Coordinated Planning of Distribution Networks with High Penetration of Distributed Renewable Energy Considering Active–Reactive Power Coupled Flexibility and Voltage Risk
articles.abstract: High-penetration distributed renewable generation introduces bidirectional power flow, rapid net-load ramps, and spatially uneven voltage sensitivity in active distribution networks. To address these challenges, a multi-time-scale coordinated planning method is proposed by integrating active–reactive power coupling flexibility and voltage-risk control. The method decomposes net active and reactive load into fast, medium, and slow components, models inverter-based P–Q feasible regions, and embeds voltage conditional value at risk into investment and operation decisions. A WGAN-GP-based scenario generation framework is used to preserve wind, photovoltaic, and load uncertainties, and 27 representative scenarios are selected for planning. Case studies on a radial PG&E 69-bus distribution feeder show that the risk-aware scheme increases wind and PV capacities from 0.96 MW and 0.56 MW to 1.18 MW and 0.74 MW, respectively. Although annualized investment rises from 1.05 M to 1.39 M, total annualized cost decreases from 2.83 M to 2.316 M, achieving an 18.16% reduction. Renewable utilization improves from 88.3% to 98.35%, while curtailed energy and expected energy not supplied decrease by 85.2% and 92.4%. The results verify that coordinated P–Q flexibility can enhance renewable accommodation, reduce voltage-tail risk, and improve planning economy.

articles.title: Wireless Networks with Large Intelligent Surfaces: Partial CSI Reconstruction through SNR-Aware Deep Learning
articles.abstract: The growing demand for high data rates, widespread connectivity and intelligent network services in future wireless communication systems has accelerated the evolution from fifth-generation (5G) systems to sixth-generation (6G) networks. Large Intelligent Surface (LIS) has emerged as a key enabling technology for 6G. It is considered as a potential solution for increasing coverage, spectral efficiency and energy efficiency by intelligently controlling the wireless signal propagation environment. However, high-dimensional cascaded channels are created in LIS-based systems due to the large number of reflecting elements, which makes collecting accurate Channel State Information (CSI) or channel state information a challenging task. Conventional full-CSI detection methods incur excessive pilot overhead, computational complexity and sensing requirements, limiting their large-scale application. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an SNR-aware deep learning framework for partial CSI reconstruction in LIS-assisted wireless networks. Instead of relying on full channel observations, the proposed method reconstructs high-dimensional CSI from a limited number of measurements, thereby reducing sensing complexity and pilot overhead. From noisy partial observations, full channel information is recovered using a convolutional neural network (CNN) with residual learning. In addition, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) information is incorporated into this learning method to increase robustness to changing channel conditions. During training, a joint loss function is used to improve the reconstruction quality, combining reconstruction fidelity and measurement-domain consistency. According to thorough simulations conducted using the DeepMIMO dataset, the proposed framework can successfully reconstruct high-dimensional channels with much fewer observations than conventional methods. According to research results, this approach ensures an optimal balance between sensing complexity and spectral efficiency, maintains robustness of performance at different SNR settings, and reaches similar performance to ideal full-CSI systems. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework as a scalable and energy-efficient solution for realistic LIS-based 6G wireless networks.

articles.title: Discussion on the Curie point depths in south-western Cameroon Volcanic Line derived from aeromagnetic data and their geothermal implications for thermal-springs and hydrocarbon resources
articles.abstract: Magnetic interpretation over the southern Cameroon Volcanic Line revealed the possible existence of a geothermal energy resource. This study extends the analysis of Curie isotherm depth, geothermal gradient, and heat flow using high resolution aeromagnetic data. By applying the centroid method to the aeromagnetic dataset, we obtained insights into geothermal energy resources and tectonic activity of the study area. The results of this investigation revealed that the depth to the Curie isotherm in the studied area is approximately ~ 16.73 km, which a geothermal gradient of ~ 33.17°C.km− 1 and a heat flow of ~ 83 mW.m− 2 derived from the Curie isotherm depth obtained. The shallow Curie isotherm depth may result from tectonic activity associated with the Central African Shear Zone, a significant active fault running through the Cameroon Volcanic Line, coupled with frequent eruptions of Mount Cameroon. Numerous thermo-mineral springs have been discovered in this area, concentrated along the corridor of the Cameroon Volcanic Line, indicating that the shallow Curie isotherm depth may have generated clean geothermal energy by driving hot water upward to the surface through fractured igneous rock. Many hydrocarbon fields are located immediately above this area, and are concentrated within the two most productive basins, suggesting that the high heat flow and geothermal gradient may have played a crucial role in reaching the temperature threshold required for hydrocarbon maturation in sedimentary basins.

articles.title: Citrate-Regulated Fe(III)-Tannic Acid Assembly for Processable and Recoverable Self-Bonding Fiberboards
articles.abstract: Conventional fiberboards rely on synthetic resin adhesives that can limit material recovery and raise formaldehyde and volatile organic compound (VOC) concerns. Dynamic metal-polyphenol networks offer an adhesive-free route, but Fe(III)-tannic acid systems are difficult to process because strong coordination can trigger premature aggregation before the network reaches fiber interfaces. Here, we investigate a citrate-containing Fe(III)-tannic acid formulation for self-bonding fiberboards. KOH/TEMPO activation increased fiber carboxylate content from 0.202 to 0.657 mmol g⁻¹, and citrate maintained low-turbidity precursors at pH 2.4–2.8, whereas the no-citric-acid control aggregated strongly. Across density-matched P0, P1, P2, P2a, and P3 boards, Full boards reached 44.2 MPa modulus of rupture (MOR) and 1.200 MPa internal bond strength (IB), exceeding both No-CA controls (33.5 MPa and 0.830 MPa) and CA-only controls (35.0 MPa and 0.950 MPa). Full boards also reduced 24 h thickness swelling to 13.2%, compared with 20.8% for No-CA and 20.0% for CA-only boards. Full boards showed lower total volatile organic compound (TVOC) emissions than No-CA controls (126 vs 247 µg m⁻³) and lower 336 h Fe release in the leaching screen (0.810 vs 2.860 mg L⁻¹); both Fe(III)-tannic acid groups were below the commercial urea-formaldehyde high-density fiberboard (UF-HDF) comparator for formaldehyde in the same audit. Interfacial characterization and recovery tests defined mechanistic and recovery boundaries, while screening inventory data identified likely hotspots without making a comparative life-cycle assessment (LCA) claim. These results frame citrate-containing Fe(III)-tannic acid chemistry as a controllable assembly and disassembly strategy for recoverable self-bonding fiberboards.

articles.title: Blue Technology in Switchgear for Sustainable Power Transmission Systems: Dielectric, Switching, Life-Cycle and Techno-Economic Modelling of SF₆-Free Clean-Air and Vacuum Gas-Insulated Substations
articles.abstract: Sulphur hexafluoride (SF₆) has been the reference insulating and arc-quenching medium of high-voltage switchgear for six decades, but with a global warming potential of about 24 300 and an atmospheric residence time of the order of 3 200 years it is now the single largest direct greenhouse-gas liability of the transmission sector. "Blue" switchgear technology — vacuum interruption combined with clean-air (80% N₂ / 20% O₂) insulation — removes fluorinated gases from the substation entirely. This thesis develops an integrated engineering model of blue switchgear for sustainable power transmission and evaluates it against SF₆ and fluoronitrile (C₄-FN) alternatives for a 145 kV, 40 kA reference bay. A streamer-criterion dielectric model with Schwaiger field-utilisation and an empirical design-derating factor yields a clean-air design point of a 150 mm coaxial gap at 6.2 bar absolute for a 650 kV lightning impulse withstand level, against 95 mm at 4.4 bar for SF₆; the enclosure diameter grows from about 300 mm to 475 mm and the bay footprint by roughly 22%. A vacuum-arc recovery model shows a dielectric-recovery rate of approximately 18 kV/µs against a transient recovery voltage of 2.0 kV/µs, giving an interruption margin of about nine. A Rayleigh-number-based thermal model shows that the lower volumetric heat capacity of clean air requires a 28% larger conductor cross-section to hold the temperature rise below 65 K at 2 500 A. A cradle-to-grave life-cycle inventory gives 377 t CO₂-eq for the SF₆ bay against 92 t CO₂-eq for the blue bay, a 75.7% reduction, of which 77% of the SF₆ burden is gas leakage and end-of-life release. A discounted life-cycle cost model with a 9.5% capital premium gives a break-even at service year 19 and a net present advantage of 3.9% of capital cost at 40 years; sensitivity analysis shows that the business case is governed by capital premium, gas-handling and compliance cost, and discount rate, and only weakly by carbon price. A four-layer system architecture linking the primary plant, an IEC 61850 digital layer, an asset and carbon-accounting layer and the regulatory interface is proposed, together with a weighted multi-criteria sustainability index in which blue technology scores 0.89 against 0.73 for the fluoronitrile route and 0.54 for SF₆.

articles.title: A scalable framework for agricultural drought hazard mapping in data-scarce arid regions: Case study of Jiroft plain, Iran
articles.abstract: Agricultural drought is a major challenge in arid regions, especially where data from weather stations are limited. In such areas, remote sensing offers a useful way to monitor soil moisture at a regional scale. However, using remote sensing data to map agricultural drought hazard (ADH) is still not well developed, particularly in places with few ground observations. This study presents the first ADH assessment for the Jiroft plain, Iran — a dry region with limited hydro-meteorological data. We used MODIS NDVI and land surface temperature (LST) from 2007 to 2022, combined with in-situ soil moisture data at 1 km² resolution, to estimate surface soil moisture (0–30 cm). We then calculated the relative departure of soil moisture (RDSM) during eight severe drought events and used this as a basis for ADH mapping. We applied three machine learning models — support vector machine (SVM), regression trees, and multivariate discriminant analysis — to predict ADH based on ten environmental variables. Our results show that SVM performed best, with an AUC of 0.95. Plant available water capacity (PAWC), together with soil moisture, was found to be the most important factor in the model. The approach allows for spatially detailed ADH mapping even in data-scarce regions. We show how the model can be used to predict future drought events in the Jiroft plain. The study provides a practical method for drought risk assessment in arid areas where monitoring data are limited. The results can support early warning systems and help improve land use planning in similar regions around the world.

articles.title: Structural and Electronic Features of a Julolidine Schiff Base Revealed by X- ray Crystallography and DFT Calculations
articles.abstract: A new hydroxy substituted pyridoquinoline Schiff base, 9-[(4-hydroxy-phenylimino)-methyl]-2,3,6,7-tetrahydro-1H,5H-pyrido[3,2,1-ij]quinolin-8-ol was synthesized by condensation of 8-hydroxy-9-formyl-2,3,6,7-tetrahydro-1H,5H-pyrido[3,2,1-ij]quinoline with p-aminophenol in refluxing methanolic solution. The 1H NMR, UV–Visible spectroscopy, single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Hirshfeld surface analysis and density functional theory (DFT) calculations led to the establishment of the molecular structure. Intramolecular O–H···N hydrogen bond stabilises the nearly planar conformation in the molecule, the solid-state being in the enol–imine tautomer, as revealed by the single-crystal X-ray analysis. The crystal packing is directed by intermolecular hydrogen bonding, weak C–H···π and π–π interactions, which results in the construction of a strong supramolecular network. Hirshfeld surface analysis and two-dimensional fingerprint plots revealed that the most abundant H···H (58.1%) contacts follow, followed by the C···H/H···C (23.2%) and O···H/H···O (12.7%) contacts, which reveals the crucial role that hydrogen bonding and van der Waals forces play in the stabilization of the crystal. The enol and keto tautomers showed a characteristic π→π* transition in the 220–230 nm region and an n→π*/intramolecular charge-transfer band in the 340–370 nm region, which suggests that both have a high degree of π-conjugation and the delocalization of electronic energy is very efficient. Comparative DFT calculations were also carried out which showed that the charge transfer properties are improved in the keto form due to the significant changes in molecular geometry, distribution of frontier molecular orbital and the HOMO–LUMO energy gap between the two tautomers. The experimental and theoretical studies give a detailed insight into the structural, supramolecular and electronic properties of this fused pyridoquinoline Schiff base. Multiple donor sites, extended conjugated framework, and preferential intermolecular interactions make the compound an attractive compound for coordination chemistry, crystal engineering, fluorescence sensing, utilization in optoelectronic materials, nonlinear optics, and biologically active systems of heterocycles. The results of the present study highlight the significance of combining crystallographic and computational methods to understand the structure–activity relationships of functional Schiff base derivatives, thereby optimizing their structures for targeted applications to develop advanced molecular materials that find applications in the field of emerging technologies.

articles.title: Temperature-dependent reservoir computing with granular vortex magnetic tunnel junctions
articles.abstract: Granular vortex-based magnetic tunnel junctions (GV-MTJs) provide a promising hardware platform for physical reservoir computing by combining nonlinear magnetodynamics, intrinsic short-term memory, and device-level structural complexity. Here, we experimentally investigate the temperature-dependent reservoir-computing performance of individual GV-MTJs with 600 nm and 800 nm diameters. Unlike previous simulation-based studies, this work presents an extensive measurement-driven evaluation of granular free-layer dynamics under thermal stress and assesses their computational capability using the Free Spoken Digit Dataset. Input waveforms are applied through a field line, while the measured reservoir responses are transformed using Mel-scaled filterbanks and classified with compact convolutional neural networks, enabling application-level benchmarking of the device response. Across ambient temperatures from 20 °C to 90 °C, the GV-MTJ reservoirs maintain stable spoken-digit classification performance, with accuracy degradation below 3 percentage points. At 160 °C, however, performance decreases sharply, consistent with thermally induced degradation of vortex dynamics and a reduction in effective grain-induced dynamical diversity, as supported by signal-level analysis and structural observations. These results show that free-layer granularity, traditionally regarded as a source of device variability in MTJs, can be exploited as a computational resource for reservoir computing, while also identifying the temperature range over which this resource remains effective. Overall, this work demonstrates the operational robustness and thermal limitations of GV-MTJ reservoirs and provides design guidelines for granular spintronic reservoirs in future neuromorphic edge-computing systems.

articles.title: Fano Resonances in Plasmonic Gold Gratings within a Coupled-Oscillator and Diffraction Framework
articles.abstract: Plasmonic gold gratings supporting Fano resonances are promising candidates for sensing, filtering, and surface-enhanced spectroscopy, yet the lack of a rigorous analytical framework connecting their coupled-oscillator description to grating diffraction physics has made it difficult to design structures tailored to specific applications. Here, we establish this connection for gold gratings on a silica substrate under transverse magnetic illumination, and derive closed-form design criteria that predict spectral asymmetry, quality factor, and resonance contrast directly from grating geometry. We develop a two-oscillator model in which the continuum mode is driven directly by the external field and the discrete mode is excited through coupling, and show analytically that the Fano resonance emerges near the natural frequency of the discrete oscillator due to its sharp π phase transition, while the overall spectral envelope follows the continuum because of its stronger amplitude. Intermediate values of oscillator damping produce asymmetric Fano profiles, with the asymmetry type (dip–peak or peak– dip) governed by the coupling strength: for real coupling a dip–peak profile arises when the discrete oscillator frequency exceeds that of the continuum, while for imaginary coupling the condition is reversed. Applying this framework to gold gratings, we identify the propagating zero-order diffraction as the continuum channel and evanescent higher diffraction orders beyond the Rayleigh wavelength as the discrete resonance, which appears as surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) at the metal–air or metal–substrate interfaces. Field distributions confirm a π phase shift between SPPs excited at the Fano peak and dip. Parametric sweeps demonstrate that ribbon width selects the resonance regime (antireso-nance, asymmetric Fano, or Lorentzian) by controlling ohmic damping, while grating period and ribbon height independently tune quality factor and spectral contrast. These analytical design rules enable the inverse design of Fano-based plasmonic gratings with prescribed asymmetric optical responses, providing practical guidelines for engineering next-generation plasmonic sensors, narrowband filters, and surface-enhanced spectroscopy substrates.

articles.title: Brainana: an end-to-end preprocessing framework for macaque neuroimaging
articles.abstract: Macaque MRI bridges non-invasive systems neuroscience with cellular and circuit-level mechanisms, but preprocessing remains fragmented across tools that are difficult to integrate, adapt to non-human primate acquisitions, and deploy reproducibly. We present Brainana, an automated, BIDS-compatible preprocessing framework for macaque neuroimaging. Brainana integrates structural and functional preprocessing, cortical surface reconstruction, quality control, transform tracking, and atlas projection within a containerized package, with cloud access for users without local compute. It incorporates macaque-trained deep learning models for brain extraction and tissue segmentation, conformation to standardize variable acquisitions, and surface reconstruction optimizations for macaque neuroanatomy. Across 23 imaging sites, Brainana processed data spanning heterogeneous scanners, protocols, species, and resolutions, yielding accurate anatomical correspondence across 130 monkeys, reliable native-space cortical surfaces, localized task-evoked activations, and reproducible brain-wide resting-state correlation structure. Brainana enables reproducible, scalable, and accessible macaque MRI preprocessing that supports cross-study comparison and multimodal integration across spatial scales, from neurons to networks.

articles.title: Finite Observation and Inter-Perspectival Objectivity: An Inverse-Limit Framework for Compatible Physical Descriptions
articles.abstract: This paper develops an observer-centric framework for analyzing how common physical structure may be reconstructed from finite observational perspectives. The starting point is operational rather than metaphysical: every physically situated observer or measuring apparatus has bounded discrimination, finite retention, limited temporal resolution, and finite capacity to register distinctions. Each observational regime is represented by a state space 𝑋𝑖, with deterministic reductions represented by bonding maps. More general stochastic and quantum reductions are treated as compatible map extensions rather than as ordinary set-valued inverse systems. The central claim is methodological. Inter-perspectival objectivity is formulated relative to an observational network through three distinct questions: does a compatible reconstruction exist, is it unique (up to a stated equivalence), and which properties remain invariant across all admissible reconstructions? The paper distinguishes local feasibility, overlap compatibility, and global reconstructibility, and introduces obstruction certificates for localizing compatibility failure. A classical phase space example establishes the kinematic architecture, while a worked Peres Mermin contextuality application provides a nontrivial foundational benchmark. There the appropriate mathematical object is a limit of an overlap diagram: each context is locally consistent, but the complete family has no compatible global section. The manuscript compares this reconstruction perspective with ordinary coarse graining, relational descriptions, and sheaf-theoretic contextuality, and states explicit limitations and criteria for future empirical or explanatory success.

articles.title: Numerical Study of Formamidinium Lead Iodide Perovskite Solar Cells using Solar Cell Capacitance Simulator (SCAPS-1D) Software
articles.abstract: Perovskite-based solar cells (PSCs) have significantly influenced the photovoltaic industry by outperforming several established solar cell technologies, with power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) already exceeding 23%. Owing to the high costs associated with the experimental development and fabrication of solar cells, researchers have increasingly adopted numerical simulation approaches. Simulation-based optimization offers several advantages, as it is straightforward and cost-effective and enables the prediction of optimal parameters that contribute to the fabrication of solar cells with improved performance. Although PSCs continue to demonstrate promising potential as a viable solar technology, replacing conventional charge transporting layers (CTLs) with inorganic alternatives can enhance long-term device stability and cost-effectiveness. We propose a theoretical study aimed at analysing the performance of Formamidinium Lead Iodide (FAPbI3)-based PSCs using the SCAPS-1D simulation program. The solar cell is built with a novel and cost-effective planar n-i-p architecture that includes inorganic transport layers. The addition of a thin interface defect layer between the electron transport layer (ETL) and absorber layer significantly improved device performance. Furthermore, a systematic analysis of device parameters was performed, considering critical elements such as working temperature, ETL and absorber thickness, absorber defect density and interface defect layer (ILETL/At). Our optimal device configuration of FTO/SnO2/ILETL/At/FAPbI3/CuI/Ag resulted in an ideal device efficiency of around 25.81%. This research examines a cost-effective architectural design method that prioritizes device efficiency and sustainability.

articles.title: Smartphone Thermal Response to Concrete and Vegetated Surfaces: A Proof-of-Concept Pilot Study
articles.abstract: Urban heat is traditionally investigated from the outside in, through satellite imagery of surface patterns across an area, weather station observations of ambient air at a point, or surface-temperature measurements taken on the spot. This pilot study takes a different approach, asking what a heated surface does to a set of electronics being exposed to it, namely via ordinary smartphones as surface-coupled thermal probes. I am dubbing this method Active Thermal Mapping. For this proof-of-concept investigation, two smartphones with distinctly different internal thermal engineering — one with a vapor-cooling apparatus (Phone 1), and one without (Phone 2) — were placed directly on a concrete surface and on grassy ground, in turn and in two separate trials (one trial in the early afternoon, and one in the evening of 25 February 2026). Both devices registered a considerably higher warming effect on the concrete than on grass during the daytime trials (ΔT of + 9.9°C and + 11.4°C on concrete vs. +4.5°C and + 5.1°C on grass, for Phone 1 and Phone 2 respectively). In the evening, both devices registered a value warmer than their baseline on the concrete (+ 2.8°C and + 4.2°C) but cooler than their baseline on grass some ninety minutes later (− 3.3°C and − 2.9°C). The device without active cooling (Phone 2) had a higher thermal response in all four matched conditions than the vapor-cooled device (Phone 1). A normalized Smartphone Thermal Response Index (STRI) was also calculated for purposes of cross-trial comparison (Section 12). These eight paired data points represent an exploratory pilot rather than a controlled experiment: the two surfaces were not sampled simultaneously within a given day, only one trial was performed per condition per device, and a phone's internal sensor cannot serve as a valid proxy for surface temperature. The immediate priority for additional research (Section 15) is to perform repeated trials with simultaneous surface-temperature assessment and independent sampling, in order to properly calibrate a device's thermal response and evaluate it as a potential estimator for surface conditions.

articles.title: Experimentally Realistic SCAPS-1D Optimization of Carbon Electrode-based CsFAMAPbIBr Triple-cation Mixed-halide Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Cesium-formamidinium-methylammonium lead iodide-bromide (CsFAMAPbIBr) perovskite has gained attentions because its combine high efficiency potential with improved compositional stability. Carbon electrodes provide a low-cost alternative to noble-metal contacts in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), and can be applied using simple printing techniques. This study employs SCAPS-1D to systematically optimize an FTO/BaSnO3/CsFAMAPbIBr/Cu2O/C solar cell while retaining a carbon back electrode and experimentally attainable input parameters. The prototype device exhibited a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.91%, with VOC, JSC and FF of 1.24 V, 21.47 mA/cm2, and 74.79%, respectively. Systematic variation of layer thickness, carrier concentration, bulk and interface defect densities, and series and shunt resistances increased the PCE to 26.97%, with VOC, JSC and FF of 1.32 V, 23.90 mA/cm2, and 85.23%, respectively. Sensitivity evaluation identified absorber bulk defect density and shunt resistance as the major performance-limiting parameters, with sensitivities of 0.713 and 0.515, respectively. Temperature-dependent simulations showed a consistent PCE above 26% between 290 and 330 K. These results establish practical design priorities for efficient carbon-electrode triple-cation mixed-halide PSCs and provide an experimentally oriented strategy for translating numerical optimization toward device fabrication.

articles.title: Maximising Regenerative Energy Return from Dynamo-Motor Traction Drives in Solar PV-Powered Electric Vehicles for Long-Haul Operation with Strong Stability
articles.abstract: This thesis develops a design method for maximising the energy returned to the traction store of a solar photovoltaic (PV) powered electric vehicle by a dynamo-motor traction drive over a long-haul mission, while maintaining strong small-signal and large-signal stability of the on-board DC distribution network. The upper bound on that return is established first, by examining the widely repeated proposition of equal energy return against the first and second laws of thermodynamics. It is established analytically that a dynamo mechanically coupled to the traction load cannot, in isolation, return energy equal to the traction demand: the regenerative path is bounded by a round-trip efficiency of 74.8 per cent computed from the measured component chain, and it can act only upon the fraction of mission energy that is otherwise dissipated in braking. Equality is therefore admissible only when an external energy influx — here, the vehicle-integrated PV array — closes the deficit. A complete mathematical model is developed comprising longitudinal vehicle dynamics with grade, a dual-mode permanent-magnet machine model, a bidirectional power-conversion efficiency chain, a single-diode PV model with thermal derating, and a second-order equivalent-circuit battery model. A neutrality index is defined as the ratio of returned energy to traction energy, the recovery-maximising operating policy is derived, and the closed-form condition for unity index is obtained as the limiting case. Simulation of a 450 km hilly long-haul mission for a 3 500 kg vehicle with a 12.4 m² roof array in Abu Dhabi conditions yields a traction demand of 146.8 kWh, a regenerative return of 8.3 kWh and a solar harvest of 14.4 kWh, giving a neutrality index of 15.5 per cent. The equal-return condition is satisfied at a cruise speed of 10.8 km/h for the design array, or at 80 km/h only if the aperture area is increased beyond 91 m². Stability is assessed through an averaged small-signal state-space model of the 750 V DC link loaded by the traction inverter as a constant-power load. The undamped link is shown to lose stability at 64.3 kW, below the 95 kW peak traction rating; insertion of a virtual damping resistance of 0.62 Ω raises the critical power to 950 kW and secures a minimum damping ratio of 0.707, with a Lyapunov-based estimate of the region of attraction covering the full operating envelope. The recovery systems reduce specific energy consumption from 326.2 to 292.3 Wh/km and raise the arrival state of charge from 6.1 to 15.3 per cent, converting a mission that violates the depth-of-discharge limit into a feasible one. The work concludes that maximised recovery is a substantial and realisable design gain, whereas full energy neutrality is a bounded objective attainable only within a narrow envelope that is quantified here.

articles.title: Depth-wise super-resolution of a serial-sectioned low-carbon steel microstructure by a generative adversarial network trained on in-plane images
articles.abstract: In this study, a deep-learning super-resolution framework that restores the depth-wise resolution of the 3D microstructure of a low-carbon steel without the need of additional training data is presented. The 3D microstructure of a metallic material is generally obtained through serial sectioning followed by observation of the sample surface. This provides a full 3D image, but its resolution along the depth direction is low compared to that of the microscope-observed planes. Various deep learning methods have been developed to overcome this limitation, but they mostly require additional 3D microstructure datasets to train the networks. Here, an enhanced super-resolution generative adversarial network (ESRGAN) trained on low and high resolution pairs was employed to restore the depth-wise resolution of the microstructure. As the pairs were generated internally from the specimen's own surface images, the trained network was applied along the depth direction without any external dataset. Together with a conventional SRGAN, a super-resolution convolutional neural network (SRCNN) and three interpolation schemes, we compared the methods in terms of microstructural and statistical analysis, as well as structural similarity. Among the compared methods, the ESRGAN provided the most faithful reconstruction of the depth-wise microstructure.

articles.title: AI-Enabled Structural Health Monitoring with Piezoelectric Sensors
articles.abstract: Accurate and cost-effective detection and localization of structural damage are important goals in structural health monitoring (SHM), particularly for lightweight metallic structures that are vulnerable to fatigue cracks. Such cracks can reduce the strength and reliability of a structure before they are identified through conventional inspection methods. In this study, an finite-element FEM and machine learning-based approach is proposed for detecting and locating cracks in an aluminum beam using a surface-mounted piezoelectric (PZT) actuator and sensor[1]. A parametric finite element analysis was carried out using COMSOL Multiphysics, where a rectangular crack was progressively moved along the beam from 20 to 180 mm in 5 mm increments. The resulting floating electric potential was recorded at the four measurement points under transient conditions, producing more than 500 time-series responses. Two additional multi-crack configurations were also modeled to examine more complex damage scenarios, although these configurations were not included in the machine-learning dataset. From each transient response, six features were extracted at each measurement point: root-mean-square amplitude, peak amplitude, peak-to-peak amplitude, kurtosis, Hilbert-envelope arrival time, and dominant frequency. This resulted in a 24-dimensional feature vector for each response. A support vector machine (SVM) classifier was then trained to distinguish between healthy and cracked beam conditions. Grid search was used to select the most suitable kernel from linear and radial basis function (RBF) options. For crack localization, a Gaussian process regression (GPR) model with a Matern covariance kernel was trained using only the cracked-state data. The model achieved a mean absolute error of 25.09 mm and provided 95% prediction confidence intervals. Principal component analysis (PCA) was also used to visualize the distribution of the cracked-state features. In addition, the trained SVM classifier was applied sequentially along a simulated monitoring timeline to demonstrate how the probability of damage could evolve over time. However, the results should be interpreted as a proof of concept rather than as a validated damage-detection accuracy. In particular, the healthy-state data were synthetically generated by augmenting a single cracked-beam simulation instead of being obtained from an independent healthy-beam simulation. The study demonstrates the potential of combining piezoelectric sensing, FEM simulations, and machine learning for structural damage detection and crack localization.

articles.title: SatForensics: A Transformer-Based Multi-Modal Framework for Cyber-Attack Detection,Attribution, and Chain-of-Custody Forensics in Low-Earth-Orbit Satellite Communication Networks
articles.abstract: Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, such as Starlink and OneWeb, provide global broadband connectivity but introduce an expanded cyber-attack surface. Terrestrial intrusion detection and digital forensics tools do not account for LEO operating constraints, including Doppler-shifted telemetry, intermittent contact windows, and resource-constrained ground stations. This paper presents SatForensics, a Transformer-based multi-modal framework for cyber-attack detection, attacker attribution, and chain-of-custody evidence preservation in LEO satellite networks. SatForensics fuses three data modalities: satellite housekeeping telemetry, radio-frequency (RF) interference indicators, and GPS reflectometry (GPS-R) anomaly signatures. A multi-head self-attention encoder captures temporal dependencies across successive orbital passes. A dedicated attribution sub-network maps detected intrusions to five adversarial archetypes using learned attack embeddings. A hash-chained forensic ledger generates tamper-evident evidence logs with sub-millisecond overhead. We evaluate Sat-Forensics on three real-world datasets: SatNOGS telemetry observations, NASA CYGNSS GPS-R anomaly signals, and ITU-R reported RF interference records. SatForensics achieves a macro-averaged F1-score of 97.6% on attack detection, exceeding CNN, LSTM, and single-modality Transformer baselines by 2.9 to 17.1 percentage points. Attack attribution achieves a macro-F1 of 94.2% across five archetypes, while the forensic ledger adds 0.47 ms median latency per logged event.

articles.title: Asymptotically-Embedded Deep Learning for Unsteady Singularly Perturbed Convection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations
articles.abstract: Singularly perturbed convection-diffusion-reaction equations represent a class of partial differential equations (PDEs) ubiquitous in fluid dynamics, chemical kinetics, and semiconductor modeling. These problems are characterized by a small perturbation parameter ε, leading to the formation of sharp boundary and interior layers where the solution exhibits rapid variations. Classical numerical methods, such as Finite Element Methods (FEM), suffer from spurious oscillations on uniform meshes and typically require specialized, layer-adapted meshes (e.g., Shishkin or Bakhvalov meshes) to ensure convergence. Recently, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a promising mesh-free deep learning framework. However, standard PINNs suffer from spectral bias, a phenomenon where neural networks prioritize learning low-frequency components, failing to resolve the high-frequency features characteristic of exponential boundary layers. In this work, we propose an Asymptotically-Embedded Physics-Informed Neural Network (AE-PINN). By leveraging the asymptotic expansion of the exact solution, we construct a specialized feature space that injects the analytical structure of the boundary layers directly into the neural network’s input architecture. This effectively transforms the stiff optimization problem into a smooth parameter estimation task. We perform extensive numerical experiments on unsteady 2D nonlinear prob- lems in both convection-dominated and reaction-dominated regimes. Our results demonstrate that the AE-PINN achieves high accuracy and stability for perturbation parameters as small as ε = 10−2, capturing sharp gradients that standard deep learning models miss. Furthermore, we provide a comparative analysis with Weak Galerkin FEM, highlighting the advantages of the proposed mesh-free approach in terms of implementation simplicity and geometric flexibility.

articles.title: Towards ultra-scaled nanoelectronics using the zipper material system Bi₂O₂Se/Bi₂SeO₅
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.10786v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) materials could overcome the scaling bottleneck of nanoelectronics by enabling atomically thin channels, superior electrostatic control, and reduced short-channel effects. However, progress is limited by the lack of semiconductor–insulator interfaces being simultaneously scalable, stable, and reliable. Conventional 2D interfaces are often low quality or require transferring dissimilar materials, limiting reproducibility and scalability. We show that the zipper heterostructure formed by the high-mobility 2D semiconductor Bi 2 O 2 Se and its native high- κ oxide Bi 2 SeO 5 addresses these challenges, providing an atomically sharp, chemically matched interface with excellent electrostatics and promising scaling potential. We further present the first comprehensive multiscale assessment of Bi 2 O 2 Se/Bi 2 SeO 5 transistors targeting thermal stability, reliability, and scalability by linking atomic-scale structure and defects to device-level behavior across four transistor generations (top-gated, fin, and two gate-all-around architectures). Benchmarking against IRDS-2035 targets indicates that Bi 2 O 2 Se/Bi 2 SeO 5 devices could deliver high drive current with low gate leakage under aggressive scaling, potentially surpassing the targets in the upper-bound region of the sensitivity analysis. Finally, we identify oxygen-related oxide defects as the dominant origin of hysteresis consistent with a beneficial role of encapsulation and oxygen-rich annealing. Together, our findings support the potential of this zipper material system as a technologically-credible and manufacturing-relevant platform for future nanoelectronics.

articles.title: Spontaneous Parity Breaking in Quantum Antiferromagnets on the Triangular Lattice
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.05901v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Frustration on the triangular lattice has long been a source of intriguing and often debated phases in many-body systems. Although symmetry analysis has been employed, the role of the seemingly trivial parity symmetry has received little attention. In this work, we show that phases induced by frustration are systematically shaped by an implicit rule-of-thumb associated with spontaneous parity breaking in weak longitudinal field. This principle enables us to anticipate and rationalize the regimes and conditions under which nontrivial phases emerge. For the spin-S antiferromagnetic XXZ model, we demonstrate that a controversial parity-broken phase appears at intermediate values of S. In bilayer systems, enhanced frustration leads to additional phases, such as supersolids, whose properties can be classified by their characteristic parity features. Benefiting from our improved tensor network contraction techniques, we confirm these results through large-scale tensor-network calculations. This study offers an alternative viewpoint and a systematic approach for examining the interplay between spin, symmetry, and frustration in many-body systems.

articles.title: Predicting magnetism with first-principles AI
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.09093v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Computational discovery of magnetic materials remains challenging because magnetism arises from the competition between kinetic energy and Coulomb interaction that is often beyond the reach of standard electronic-structure methods. Here we tackle this challenge by directly solving the many-electron Schrödinger equation with neural-network variational Monte Carlo, which provides a highly expressive variational wavefunction for strongly correlated systems. Applying this technique to transition metal dichalcogenide moiré semicondutors, we predict itinerant ferromagnetism in WSe₂/WS₂ and an antiferromagnetic insulator in twisted Γ-valley homobilayer, using the same neural network without any physics input beyond the microscopic Hamiltonian. Crucially, both types of magnetic states are obtained from a single calculation within the S_z=0 sector, removing the need to compute and compare multiple S_z sectors. This significantly reduces computational cost and paves the way for faster and more reliable magnetic material design.

articles.title: Stress-Induced Ferroelectricity in Hafnium Oxide Core-Shell Nanoparticles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.09262v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In contrast to hafnia (HfO2) thin films, where the appearance of switchable ferroelectric polarization can be induced by strain or defect engineering, reliable methods for controlling ferroelectricity are absent in HfO2 nanoparticles. Direct experimental observations of ferroelectric hysteresis and ferroelectric domains in these nanoparticles are also absent. To the best of our knowledge, stress-induced ferroelectric states in the HfO2 nanoparticles have not been explored. In this work, we study the influence of chemical stress on phase diagrams, dielectric and polar properties of spherical HfO2 core-shell nanoparticles using a Landau-Ginzburg-Devonshire free energy functional that includes trilinear and biquadratic couplings involving polar, antipolar, and nonpolar order parameters. The ferroelectric phase exhibits reentrant behavior as a function of nanoparticle size, such that the spontaneous polarization exists only within a limited range of core radii R_c, namely R_cr^min

articles.title: Robust realization of spin-polarized specular Andreev reflection in V₂O-based altermagnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.12695v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We theoretically investigate charge transport in a junction between a conventional superconductor and a V₂O-based altermagnet exhibiting distinctive spin-split quasi-one-dimensional Fermi surfaces. The altermagnet is described by a microscopically motivated seven-basis-state model with six-orbital characters that incorporates sublattice degrees of freedom associated with both V and O sites. Based on calculations performed under various boundary conditions, we demonstrate the robust emergence of specular Andreev reflection with a distinctive spin polarization. Furthermore, we propose an efficient multiterminal setup to detect this specular Andreev reflection through nonlocal conductance measurements. Our results establish V₂O-based altermagnets as a promising platform for realizing spin-resolved Cooper pair splitting, which is essential for generating energy-entangled electron pairs.

articles.title: Toward Accurate RIXS Spectra at Heavy Element Edges: A Relativistic Four-Component and Exact Two-Component TDDFT Approach
