The solidified radius is set by planetary mass and core fraction, insensitive to the host star, irradiation, and initial thermal state. In contrast, volatile-rich super-Earths at and above about 5 Earth masses may not solidify: their thick outgassed atmospheres throttle the surface heat loss until the interior settles into a deep magma ocean, keeping the planet inflated and limiting the contraction to about half its volatile-poor value. Mantle contraction alone thus shapes the low-mass exoplanet transit population, motivating joint interpretation of atmospheric and geophysical signatures in upcoming exoplanet surveys.

articles.title: Resource and entanglement study of a hybrid qudit-qubit quantum algorithm for solving the integer programming problem
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.23243v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently, a hybrid qudit-qubit algorithm [1] was presented for solving the integer programming problem with a polynomial quantum advantage. In this work, we investigate the algorithm [1] to understand the role of qudits (d-dimensional quantum system) by conducting a comparative resource analysis with its qubit-only implementation and the classical simulability of the algorithm by exploring the entanglement structure. The resource analysis part is performed in terms of logical gate counts, and fault-tolerant physical resources, including non-Clifford gates. The hybrid qudit-qubit implementation has a more compact structure of the unitary operators as opposed to its qubit-only simulation which reduces the logical and fault-tolerant resource requirements. Two example problems, one with qutrits (d=3) and the other with ququint (d=5), when contrasted with their qubit-only implementation, within a simplified fault-tolerant resource model, showed sim 180 ×  and sim 2220× fewer total resource count, respectively. For the entanglement study, volume-law-like entropy growth and signatures of multi-partite entanglement is observed leading to increasing difficulty in the classical simulation of the algorithm. The algorithm generates synergistic tri-partite entanglement even for a quadratic problem, revealing that the algorithmic structure itself can generate higher-order entanglement in the system independent of the problem.

articles.title: A Discretely Entropy Conserving/Stable Flux Reconstruction Scheme via Hybridized Split Form Differential Operator and Generalized Entropy Projection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.24257v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper proposes a novel discretely entropy conserving/stable flux reconstruction (FR) scheme for nonlinear conservation laws. The scheme combines a hybridized split-form differential operator with a generalized entropy projection, enabling discrete entropy conservation for arbitrary nodal distributions and arbitrary correction functions without modifying the original quadrature weights. The formulation is built directly upon the classical FR framework and is shown to preserve conservation properties while achieving entropy conservation in the semi-discrete sense. Numerical experiments using the isentropic vortex problem confirm the theoretically predicted accuracy and demonstrate robust entropy behavior with entropy-dissipative interface fluxes.

articles.title: Parallel Optimization: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications,
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.24505v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This 30 years old book is posted for free download by the generosity of Oxford University Press that granted permission to allow access to future generations of young scientists. A printed copy can be purchased from the publisher. The authors received for this book "The 1999 INFORMS Computing Society Prize for Research Excellence in the Interface Between Operations Research and Computer Science" from the Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS). For a book review by Janos D. Pinter go to: Journal of Global Optimization, 16: 107-108, 2000.

articles.title: An Exact Operator Formulation of Statistical Quasiparticle Theory for Nonlinear System-Bath Coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.24603v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an operator formulation of statistical quasiparticle theory for open quantum systems with nonlinear system-bath coupling, extending beyond the linear coupling setting of the standard Gaussian influence functional formulation. For Gaussian baths, the statistical quasiparticles, termed dissipatons, are explicitly constructed as collective operators in the thermofield bath space. Our construction provides a microscopic operator basis for the dissipaton algebra and generates hierarchical equations of motion directly from the Liouville equation. Nonlinear interactions are incorporated through a recursive generalized Wick's theorem, enabling automatic generation of hierarchical equations for polynomial couplings. The resulting framework connects explicit bath operator representations to nonperturbative, non-Markovian dynamics and unifies the treatment of linear and nonlinear system-bath interactions.

articles.title: SolarFlowRefiner: Refinement-Aware Flow Matching for Surface Solar Radiation Downscaling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.22126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-resolution surface solar radiation (SSR) is important for solar forecasting and grid operation. However, physically consistent reanalysis products are too coarse to resolve localized cloud-driven variability. In this paper, we study a multisource downscaling task that reconstructs high-resolution SolarCube SSR fields from coarse ERA5 radiative variables and co-registered satellite channels. The task is challenging because a single ERA5 grid cell may contain both sunlit and cloud-shadowed regions. As a result, the missing high-resolution correction can be spatially sharp and inherently ambiguous. One-stage predictors often oversmooth these structures. Post-hoc refinement also introduces a stage-wise mismatch: the generator is optimized independently, even though its output determines the refiner's initial state. We introduce SolarFlowRefiner, a refinement-aware flow-matching framework for SSR downscaling. A conditional FlowMatch generator first predicts a normalized correction to an upsampled ERA5 baseline. The refiner is then trained on prediction-conditioned states between the current FlowMatch output and the target residual. This exposes the refiner to the structured errors produced by the generator. The refinement objective is also backpropagated through the FlowMatch sampler, allowing generation and correction to be jointly optimized for the final reconstruction. Experiments on a day-blocked ERA5--SolarCube benchmark show consistent improvements over standalone generation and post-hoc refinement. More broadly, SolarFlowRefiner provides a general strategy for coupling generative predictors with iterative correctors.

articles.title: CleanScore: Black-Box Benchmark Audits with Negative Controls and Sensitivity Bounds
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.22183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public benchmark scores may reflect skill, prior exposure to the questions, or both, and for most models the training data are unknown. We present CleanScore, a black-box audit using scored outputs only. Each benchmark question becomes a parent item with one public form and two independently written fresh forms preserving its numbers, facts and answer. The audit reports an interval for the public-form advantage rather than a verdict, and a private negative-control bank with an explicit transport radius separates exposure from ordinary form mismatch. A registered controlled-exposure experiment detects planted exposure and stays quiet under fresh-form exposure. A registered audit of five open models on 200 GSM8K and 200 ARC-Challenge items finds no exposure-consistent advantage, bounding surface-form inflation below five points. Registered positive controls then bound what such a null can mean. Leaking an item raises accuracy on paraphrases the model never saw almost as much as on the leaked wording, leaving 52% to 110% of the effect invisible to a paraphrase audit. On ARC a planted 49-point advantage shows an observable gap of -0.020, and about 20 points survive rewriting stem and options, across four training seeds. A surface-form null bounds far less than the phrase contamination audit implies.

articles.title: Strategy Accumulation and Guided Execution for Automated LLM Fine-Tuning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.22257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Producing task-specific large language models requires discovering effective training strategies through experimentation. Automated fine-tuning systems have made this experimentation feasible with far less manual effort. However, these systems are stateless: each search discards its discovered strategies, dataset insights, and hyperparameter findings once it ends. Every new task must then repeat this costly search from a cold start. To address this, we propose Strategy Accumulation and Guided Execution (SAGE), a two-stage framework that makes automated fine-tuning search cumulative. In the first stage, a multi-agent pipeline performs Monte Carlo Tree Search-based exploration. A parallel Distillation Agent extracts task-specific exploration records and confidence-scored cross-task insights, which together constitute a structured experience repository. In the second stage, SAGE retrieves relevant experience from this repository and selects what applies to guide training on the new task. We evaluate SAGE on nine unseen tasks spanning both single- and cross-category settings. In single-round execution, SAGE's accumulated experience raises the average relative improvement over baseline from 3.2% to 15.6%, a 12.4-percentage-point gain over the same pipeline without it. These results show that persistent strategy experience provides effective guidance for automated fine-tuning on unseen tasks.

articles.title: Resist, Update, Reject: Preference Optimization Installs a Prior-Dependent Reliability Switch
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.22359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An aligned model asked to hold its answer against a manipulative source must still update on a reliable one and reject an unreliable one: resistance, reliable-update, and unreliable-source rejection are one three-way contract, not three independent behaviors. We show the objective most anti-sycophancy work optimizes is non-identifying with respect to source reliability: because no preference label depends on whether a source is actually reliable, any scalar mixture of the arms traces a single deference dial, and no point separates two same-template testimonies differing only in stated reliability. This fixation↔gullibility frontier is a property of the objective, not any model. We make reliability identifiable through data: a threshold benchmark where a source asserts the opposite answer while stating its reliability r, and the correct action is to flip iff r exceeds the model's prior strength p. Preference optimization over balanced coverage installs a prior-dependent reliability switch: across three seeds on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct the threshold r^star rises monotonically with the prior, decision accuracy reaches 0.84 with a monotone flip curve (Spearman 0.56), and the policy generalizes to unseen reliability values and a held-out notation, following stated reliability over role prestige. Three controls localize the cause: an unmatched variant installs the switch equally (0.80), a second preference optimizer (IPO) installs it just as well (0.86), whereas supervised imitation does not (0.50), so the cause is preference optimization over reliability-labeled coverage, not pairing, loss, or imitation. A confirmatory battery replicates the switch on a fresh test draw, bounds it honestly (it keys on reliability stated in the testimony, not a separately audited record), and transfers it to Llama-3.1-8B. The frontier is empirical, not a theorem.

articles.title: Testing the Construct Validity of a Functional Valence Axis in LLM Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.22850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contrastive activation directions are often interpreted from what they decode or how strongly they steer behavior. But what evidence is sufficient to identify the construct represented by such a direction, rather than a correlated feature of the contrast used to extract it? We study this question for a good--bad outcome direction in a maze task, using controlled interventions that separate the realised outcome from the informational history through which it became known. Across multiple LLM checkpoints, directions fitted on one explicit outcome encoding transfer well to another, indicating that the readout is not tied to surface form. In contrast, when the same realised outcome is reached through announced and unannounced histories, transfer degrades substantially: even after both histories receive the same explicit outcome, the post-event readout remains strongly conditioned on the earlier announcement. In a matched maze-RL run, the post-RL direction becomes substantially more predictive of reference-MDP remaining return and the policy becomes more dependent on it at the tested sites, while this history dependence persists. These results support a functional, value-related interpretation of the direction, but not its identification with a history-invariant scalar valence state.

articles.title: Optimizers for Diffusion Models: A Controlled Benchmark
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.23055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete diffusion models now match autoregressive language models on several benchmarks, while the question of how best to train them has received far less attention: the optimizer is inherited from one paper to the next and never compared. New optimizers, meanwhile, are validated almost exclusively on autoregressive pretraining, a different objective on a different loss surface. We present a controlled optimizer benchmark across four diffusion formulations, to our knowledge the first for discrete diffusion: seven optimizers (AdamW, Lion, Muon, SOAP, MARS, MARS-M, Schedule-Free) on masked diffusion (text8), uniform diffusion (QM9, and LM1B through the Gaussian duality) and Gaussian diffusion on images (CelebA-64), each on a task with published reference values. Every optimizer receives the same search protocol, and every winner is retrained at the full budget with three seeds. AdamW is a strong default but not always the right choice: it is beaten by a resolved margin on two of the four tasks, and the winner changes with the formulation, so the optimizer deserves the same care as the rest of the training recipe. Notably, methods validated on autoregressive language model pretraining transfer well: Muon, MARS-M and SOAP each beat the tuned AdamW on at least one diffusion formulation. The benchmark, all runs and every figure are reproducible end to end from the released code at https://github.com/armanbolatov/diffusion-baselines.

articles.title: Matched-Input Estimates Differ in Sign Across Architectures: Auditing EEG Foundation Models on Motor Imagery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.23924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pretrained EEG foundation models are increasingly proposed as general-purpose encoders for brain-computer interfaces, yet recent benchmarks disagree about when their representations transfer to downstream tasks. We audit LaBraM and CBraMod on motor imagery under a validation-locked protocol in which preprocessing, architecture, optimization, freeze depth, checkpoint, temperature, and method selection are determined using training-session data only. On four-class BCI Competition IV-2a, every supervised comparator evaluated here outperforms every foundation-model configuration, including validation-selected fine-tuning. We then examine a key confound: foundation models and task-specific decoders are normally evaluated using different input pipelines. Retraining three supervised architectures on the broadband arrays consumed by the foundation models produces matched-input accuracy differences of opposite sign across architectures: broadband input improves ATCNet by 0.078 accuracy while reducing EEG Conformer accuracy by 0.088. None of the three individual matched-input terms is significant after multiple-comparison correction at n = 9, so we treat the sign variation descriptively rather than as a formal architecture-by-pipeline interaction. These observed sign differences suggest that a single comparator may not provide an architecture-invariant decomposition of a pretrained-versus-supervised performance gap. The four-class deficit also does not reproduce uniformly across motor-imagery datasets: on two-class BNCI2014-004 we cannot detect the same separation between fine-tuned CBraMod and the supervised comparators. Finally, validation-fitted temperature scaling returns foundation-model calibration error to the supervised range despite substantially lower four-class accuracy.

articles.title: Mind or Message? Auditing Theory of Mind in Multi-Agent Social Simulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.24146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language model agents are increasingly used to simulate social interaction, and the resulting transcripts read as though the agents understand one another. We ask whether that appearance rests on a model of the partner's mind or on the surface record of what the partner said. We build a social simulation in which both questions have exact answers: 40 multi-issue negotiations whose hidden preference weights and whose full Pareto frontier are known by construction. Two model families negotiate across 160 dyads, every transcript is frozen before any measurement, and 2880 counterfactual probes then hold the evidence byte identical while moving one factor at a time: the reader's own stake, the partner's tone, an identity label, and the order of recursion. The agents are socially fluent and economically poor. They reach agreement in 96.2% of dyads with 0 protocol failures, yet only 0.7% of deals land on the Pareto frontier, they leave 20.5% of the available joint value unclaimed, and they miss the one issue on which their interests are perfectly aligned in 76.6% of deals; on the frontier and on that aligned issue, a package drawn at random from the set both sides would accept does as well. The probes locate the failure. Swapping only the reader's own payoff sheet, while the partner's words and offers stay identical, moves the inferred top priority by 15.0 percentage points, which is egocentric projection rather than inference, while a tone rewrite moves it by 5.3 percentage points and an identity label by 0.0. Most tellingly, an agent predicts what its partner believes about it 72.5% of the time while that partner's belief is itself correct only 51.2% of the time: the agents track the conversation far better than they track the mind behind it.

articles.title: Sparse Regression Distilled from a Single Robust Fit
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.23937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robust linear fits can resist response contamination yet remain too dense or unstable for useful global explanations. We propose penalized distillation, which fits a smoothly clipped absolute deviation (SCAD) estimator to a robust initial estimator's empirical fitted surface along a safeguarded coordinate-descent path and evaluates candidate states separately for fidelity, parsimony, perturbation stability, and held-out prediction. The new results attach to the states the algorithm actually computes. Conditional on a fixed uncontaminated design, deterministic bounds transfer response-replacement boundedness from the initial fit to every retained path state. Turning to fixed dimension, we characterize the oracle-support branch by its empirical-Gram projection and influence function, give conditions for covariance-weighted least-squares approximation equivalence, and establish a path-conditional generalized information criterion. By contrast, at large dimension-to-sample ratios the full-coordinate robust fit collapses without warning, and screening restores the construction. Under a sure-screening framework, the robustness bound and the support and selection guarantees transfer to the screened fit. Simulations separate robustness transfer from support recovery, efficiency, and computation across the dimension-to-sample ratio, with p up to 240, and the signal density, which isolates what the sparse stage adds once the screen over-selects. In a duplicate-grouped superconductivity study, the distilled estimator remains predictively stable under prespecified training-response shifts but retains 66.8--68.8 of 81 slopes. Stronger sparsification reduces the model to 12.6--14.0 slopes only at visible fidelity and prediction cost. Distillation therefore preserves predictive stability on these data without substantiating a compact coordinate-level explanation.

articles.title: Selective Inference for CART with Binary Outcomes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.24949v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Binary classification trees select subgroups using the same outcomes later used to assess their differences. We develop finite-sample conditional tests of a common success probability within a parent selected by deterministic Gini CART. The construction retains all eligible cutpoints and conditions on the selected split, its ancestor path, the parent success total, and outside outcomes. The resulting uniform label fiber gives an exact count distribution, while a reversible parallel Monte Carlo construction yields super-uniform inclusive and exactly uniform tie-randomized p-values for any prespecified finite run budget. Within a two-child constant-risk model, the selected count law is an exponential family with information equal to its conditional count variance. We separate information loss from computational limitations and exhibit a selected fiber disconnected under single-label swaps. Simulations with 200 or 400 observations, ten independent or correlated predictors, and trees of depth three show conservative inclusive tests and nontrivial power for large risk differences. At 400 observations and a generating risk difference of 0.4, randomized rejection conditional on reaching the prespecified third-level target is 51--71%, while selection followed by rejection occurs in 11--21% of datasets. Smaller signals remain difficult to detect, and a representative fivefold increase in computation gives little power improvement. The guarantee concerns parent homogeneity, or equality of two constant child risks, and does not cover equality of heterogeneous regional averages.

articles.title: Skittles: A Multicolor Flow Cytometric Workflow for High-Throughput Characterization of Micro- and Nano-plastics
articles.abstract: Micro- and nano-plastics (MNPs), polymer particles less than 5 mm in dimension, are abundant and globally pervasive anthropogenic pollutants. However, their true abundance in natural systems remains poorly constrained by the lack of high-throughput, standardized analytical methods for their characterization. Here, we present Skittles, a multicolor flow cytometric workflow for the high-throughput characterization of MNPs in liquid suspension that simultaneously provides fluorescence-based discrimination, particle enumeration, and SSC-calibrated PS-equivalent size distributions. The workflow was optimized and analytically validated using laboratory reference standards and environmental samples, demonstrating high precision (CVs typically <4%), quantitative recovery (mean 103%), and strong agreement with epifluorescence microscopy (R² = 0.99), while polymer classifications were independently corroborated using Raman spectroscopy. Application of Skittles to heterogeneous laboratory and environmental samples demonstrated its ability to characterize particle populations spanning multiple polymer types, morphologies, and sizes, including fragments, clumps, and fibers. Together, these results establish Skittles as a high-throughput analytical workflow for micro- and nano-plastic characterization in aquatic environments.

articles.title: Theoretical Research on Zeolite-Supported In-situ Grown LDO for Fluoride Removal in High-Salinity Wastewater by Memory Reconstruction
articles.abstract: Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) possess a tunable layered crystal structure, excellent anion exchange capacity, and a unique high-temperature memory reconstruction effect, showing promising application prospects in the treatment of inorganic anion pollution in water bodies. However, pure LDH powders suffer from inherent engineering application limitations, including easy agglomeration of nanosheets, low solid-liquid separation efficiency, and poor adsorption selectivity for fluoride ions in high-salinity systems. In this study, acidified clinoptilolite was adopted as a rigid support carrier. A nitrate-intercalated MgAl-LDH precursor was in-situ grown on the zeolite surface via a co-precipitation method under a nitrogen atmosphere isolated from carbon dioxide, and a zeolite-based LDO core-shell composite adsorbent was fabricated by controlled calcination at 400–450°C. The full preparation process, including zeolite acidification pretreatment, in-situ LDH coating, and calcination-induced LDO transformation, was systematically elaborated. Key preparation parameters, such as calcination temperature, atmospheric environment, and types of interlayer anions, were optimized. Combined with BET characterization and static adsorption experimental data, the evolution law of the material’s microstructure was analyzed, and the multiple synergistic adsorption mechanism of zeolite-based LDO for fluoride removal from high-salinity wastewater relying on the memory effect was revealed. The adsorption experimental results demonstrate that the specific surface area of the prepared zeolite-based LDO reaches 136.42 m²/g, which is significantly higher than that of pure LDO (68.75 m²/g). Under the conditions of an initial fluoride concentration of 50 mg/L, pH value of 6, and coexisting high salts (0.1 mol/L NaCl and 0.05 mol/L Na₂SO₄), the maximum saturated adsorption capacity of zeolite-based LDO is up to 127.23 mg/g, which is 4.1 times that of single acidified zeolite (31.06 mg/g). Moreover, 82.6% of the initial adsorption capacity can be retained after five regeneration cycles. The composite adsorbent features low raw material cost and excellent recyclability, which is suitable for the advanced purification treatment of industrial high-salinity fluoride-containing wastewater. This work can provide comprehensive theoretical support and technical references for the industrial development and engineering application of zeolite-based LDO adsorption materials.

articles.title: Testing Frontier LLMs on Indian Statutory Interpretation: The Indian Construction Canon Benchmarking (ICCB) -Pilot Benchmark
articles.abstract: Statutory interpretation is the foundational cognitive task of legal reasoning and yet it remains largely untested in large language model (LLM) evaluation. Existing benchmarks privilege outcome prediction within English common-law settings, leaving the interpretive substrate of legal reasoning unmeasured and jurisdiction-specific doctrinal traditions unexamined. No benchmark to date evaluates whether frontier models correctly identify and apply the canons of construction that structurally govern statutory interpretation in the Indian legal systems. This paper introduces ICCB-Pilot, an expert-rubric benchmark of 40 items drawn from Indian Supreme Court and High Court judgments spanning ten canons of statutory construction. Four frontier models: Claude Opus 4–7, GPT-5.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Llama 3.3- 70B Instruct, were evaluated across two prompt conditions (zero-shot open and canon-primed), generating 320 scored outputs. A five-dimension rubric assessed canon identification (D1), doctrinal accuracy (D2), application fidelity (D3), outcome correctness (D4), and reasoning quality (D5), with inter-rater reliability reported via Cohen's κ. Our principal findings are threefold: (i) all models score substantially higher on D4 than on D1; and (ii) canon-priming produces marked gains on D1 but negligible gains on D4, indicating that outcome approximation is largely insensitive to correct canon selection. The systematic dissociation between D4 and D1 scores is consistent with surface pattern-matching rather than rule-governed interpretive reasoning. These findings suggest that jurisprudential fidelity in LLMs cannot be inferred from accuracy metrics alone, and support mandatory doctrinal evaluation as a precondition for deploying LLMs in statutory interpretation tasks within Indian legal practice.

articles.title: Near-tip elastoplastic fracture mechanics of amorphous silica at small scale
articles.abstract: Amorphous silica is widely used as an insulating layer in semiconductor and solar cell fabrication, where fracture behavior at the nanometer scale directly governs manufacturing precision and device reliability. Nanometer-scale exfoliation of amorphous silica requires a clear understanding of the crack growth mechanics. Fracture studies of amorphous silica have traditionally relied on linear elastic fracture mechanics. However, the recent establishment of plasticity near the crack tip at the atomistic scale calls for revisiting this assumption. In this present work, an elastoplastic fracture mechanics framework is utilized at the atomistic scale using molecular statics simulations. Local elastoplastic stress fields ahead of the crack tip are calculated from atomistic strain energy densities and finite strains at local atomistic sites. Further, a discretized, domain-integral formulation of the J-integral is derived using a linear weight function. It has been demonstrated that even when the integral domain encloses the near-tip elastoplastic zone at the critical state just before crack propagation begins, the path independence of the critical J-integral holds. The resulting critical J-integral has been validated against multiple independent methods: a global energy release rate calculation, crack tip opening displacement estimates from both 90° blunt-tip and direct methods. This fracture toughness has also been shown to translate to the continuum scale through an elastoplastic finite element analysis using the Ramberg-Osgood model. The methodology demonstrated in the present work is general in nature and maybe extended to any amorphous material.

articles.title: Do we carry the false belief that LLMs have a theory of mind?
articles.abstract: Recent work shows that Large Language Models (LLMs) match and even exceed human-level performance across a battery of Theory of Mind (ToM) assessments. This has led to speculation that LLMs possess ToM capabilities. In this study, we test this claim by using the Unexpected Transfer task (i.e., the Sally-Anne test) to assess five up-to-date LLMs. The results indicate that while each model cumulatively performed above chance, they regularly defaulted to using less costly heuristics in place of dynamically tracking mental states. Most task failures resulted from an inability to integrate causality and “common-sense” pragmatic inferences into their reasoning processes. These findings suggest that LLMs have yet to develop robust ToM capabilities, calling for a systematic review of the present association between LLMs and ToM.

articles.title: Replay-Safe Decision Provenance for Mutable Geospatial Contexts: Version-Bound Receipts and Complete Change Frontiers
articles.abstract: A historical spatial decision can change when replay silently substitutes a newer geometry, policy, or evaluator, even if the evidence is immutable. We define replay-safe decision provenance with separate as-issued, current-context, and counterfactual semantics. A receipt binds evidence, a declared interpretation context, and the issued decision; later reclassification produces a separate certificate. For a three-tier point-to-polygon classifier, we characterize label changes exactly as the union of symmetric differences of two offset regions. A conservative grid-coordinate filter reduces exact geometric evaluation while retaining a linear scan of the history. Evaluation uses 90 synthetic mutation trials of 100,000 events, six single-seed scaling configurations up to one million events, five timing repetitions per path, and baselines that reuse stored old labels. Selective replay returns exactly the full-replay change set in all trials. Across nine scenarios, median candidate reduction over five seeds ranges from 99.47% to 99.83% for uniform histories and from 29.84% to 29.96% for a boundary-concentrated mixture. A minimal content-addressed verifier passes 19 functional checks, including missing or substituted artifacts and separation of issued from counterfactual results. A logical commitment ablation detects all five dependency substitutions only when all five are bound. These results support conditional replay integrity and distribution-dependent recomputation savings; they do not establish physical-location truth, production ledger enforcement, or completeness beyond the declared evaluator interface.

articles.title: Detector-Calibration Failures in Pattern-Based LLM Refusal Classification: Discovery, Generalization, and a Confirmed False-Positive Pattern Across Models
articles.abstract: Pattern-based refusal detection in LLM safety pipelines introduces its own error surface, rarely reported alongside the safety numbers it produces. We report a three-phase investigation into one such detector's calibration history. Phase 1 finds an apparent non-determinism result on Claude Haiku was substantially a detector artifact, corrected by fixing two concrete defects. Phase 2 replicates the fix across six models and finds it generalizes but clusters cleanly by provider, while also introducing confirmed false positives concentrated in specific prompt shapes. Phase 3 closes the resulting audit across the remaining models and categories, finding the pattern recurs once more, and reports explicitly which parts of the audit grid have no data to examine at all rather than implying broad coverage. The fix is real and generalizable in aggregate, but its per-verdict correctness requires manual audit at every scale -- verifiable here, as every result traces to an archived dataset available on request.

articles.title: Marginal Mean Weighting Through Stratification for Time-Varying Multivalued Treatments: A Monte Carlo Comparison with Inverse-Probability-Weighted Marginal Structural Models
articles.abstract: Marginal structural models are commonly estimated using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) to address time-varying confounding, but direct inversion of estimated treatment probabilities can produce unstable weights. Marginal mean weighting through stratification (MMWS) provides an alternative weight-construction strategy that has been extended to longitudinal multivalued treatments but has received little comparative evaluation. We compared sequential MMWS with multinomial IPTW in a Monte Carlo simulation varying sample size, confounding strength, treatment-confounder feedback, number and prevalence of treatment levels, treatment-model misspecification, and positivity. Both methods used identical fitted treatment models, isolating differences in weight construction. MMWS had lower root mean squared error than IPTW for every treatment contrast across all scenarios, with particularly large advantages under treatment-model misspecification, although it generally incurred modestly greater bias. Under positivity stress, MMWS retained lower root mean squared error but exhibited substantially greater bias and poorer confidence-interval coverage, while exclusions and cumulative-weight restarts revealed increasing support limitations as treatment complexity increased. These findings suggest that MMWS can provide a more stable and robust alternative to conventional IPTW when treatment-level overlap is adequate, but does not eliminate the positivity challenges inherent in complex longitudinal multivalued treatments.

articles.title: Effects of Physical Fatigue on Muscle Activities and Running Kinetics in Individuals with both Obesity and Pronated Feet
articles.abstract: Background and Purpose Despite the known changes in ground reaction forces (GRFs) components in individuals with overweight and obesity, the effects of running-induced fatigue on GRFs and lower-limb electromyographic (EMG) activity remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the impact of running-related fatigue on GRF components and lower-limb muscle activity in individuals with obesity and pronated feet during running.Methods Thirty-one male participants were divided into two groups: a normal weight/normal foot group (body mass index [BMI] < 25 kg/m²; navicular drop: 4–10 mm) and an obesity/pronated foot group (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²; navicular drop > 10 mm). Participants ran barefoot along an 18‑m runway at a controlled speed of 3.3 m/s (± 5%) before and after completing a fatigue protocol. GRF components were collected using a force plate, and EMG activity of selected lower-limb muscles was recorded using a surface electromyography system.Results Following fatigue, several GRF components increased significantly in both groups. Overall muscle activity decreased after fatigue; however, gluteus medius activity during the early stance phase was significantly affected (P = 0.004, d = 1.161). Specifically, gluteus medius activity increased in the normal weight/normal foot group but did not increase in the obesity/pronated foot group (P = 0.001, d = 0.959).Interpretation: These findings suggest that running-related fatigue increases GRF components and reduces lower-limb muscle activity. Importantly, individuals with obesity and pronated feet exhibit insufficient compensatory increases in gluteus medius activity during fatigue, which may compromise pelvic stability and increase the risk of running-related musculoskeletal injury.

articles.title: Congruent functional patterns conceal contrasting environmental drivers of aboveground and belowground community assembly across Europe
articles.abstract: Above- and belowground plant organs interface with fundamentally different environments and have evolved under distinct selective regimes. This raises the possibility of divergent community-level responses along environmental gradients between these two compartments, an unresolved question with important implications for predicting ecosystem responses to global change. Using 29,223 European vegetation plots, 2,981 aboveground and an unprecedented 612 belowground species traits, we quantified functional variability and composition for both compartments and assessed their associations with climate, geo-edaphic features, human pressure, and vegetation structure. Spatial patterns of functional structure were broadly similar between compartments, but environmental control was asymmetric: while functional composition was comparably well explained in both compartments (R² up to 66% aboveground, 59% belowground), environmental drivers explained far more functional variability aboveground (34–37%) than belowground (5–10%). Climate was the dominant driver overall, but soil properties and terrain roughness were equally or more important belowground, particularly for fine-root diversity and economics. Environmental relationships were consistently stronger in forests than in open vegetation, suggesting that vegetation context modulates environmental filtering across compartments. These findings reveal that spatial congruence can conceal contrasting assembly processes, meaning that predictions of ecosystem responses to global change based on aboveground functional patterns alone will systematically misrepresent belowground dynamics.

articles.title: FireInSite: an Accessible, Integrated Fire Behaviour Prediction System for the UK and Ireland
articles.abstract: Accessible tools to support wildfire management are lacking for humid temperate regions. We developed FireInSite as a user-oriented system for predicting fire behaviour for major fire-prone fuels at any location in the UK and Ireland. Extensive fuel moisture, flammability, and seasonally varying energy content data underpin FireInSite’s integrated fuel moisture, heat content, and fuel modules. The user-friendly interface requires no user input to generate fire behaviour predictions, other than selecting a location of interest or using the automatic geolocated selection. It does so by characterising the state of the fuels of interest at any point in the season in respect to a location's climatology and weather as novel modules and then directing the relationships between these modules into a fire behaviour prediction model based on the Rothermel family of equations. As well as hourly forecasts, hindcasts of fire behaviour are also available back to 1970 and weather and fuel moisture forecasts can be compared to historical conditions. FireInSite therefore enables assessment of fire risk, effects of fuel load reduction, or planning for fire prevention and suppression. FireInSite has been used by Fire and Rescue Services and land managers in the UK and Ireland since 2025, and community response and validation have demonstrated the skill of FireInSite as a decision support tool. FireInSite’s capabilities therefore provide previously lacking support for the UK, Ireland, and comparable humid temperate regions, enabling them to better prepare for and mitigate their accelerating wildfire risk.

articles.title: A Discrete Combinatorial Yamabe Flow Operator for Grayscale Image Structure Analysis: Curvature, Flow, and Conformal Enhancement
articles.abstract: We introduce and characterize a new discrete geometric emphimage operator: a grayscale image is lifted to a piecewise-linear graph surface over a triangulated pixel grid and evolved by a emphcombinatorial Yamabe flow, a per-vertex conformal rescaling that drives the discrete Gaussian curvature of the image surface toward a prescribed target field. The primary contribution of this paper is this operator and its theory, not a denoising or enhancement algorithm: we prove a curvature--singularity duality theorem showing that straight intensity edges are intrinsically flat and produce zero curvature response, so that curvature concentrates exactly at genuinely two-dimensional singularities (corners, junctions, blobs), and a monotone-energy theorem giving a Lyapunov certificate for the flow, with full proofs, and we discuss explicitly which assumptions of the classical discrete-conformal-geometry results we rely on and how (and whether) they transfer to an image-induced metric. Corner detection, structure-preserving smoothing and structure-selective sharpening are then presented as three illustrative instantiations of the same operator, each evaluated quantitatively: a corner-detection benchmark with exact synthetic ground truth (matching the Harris detector), a denoising benchmark against five established baselines including BM3D on eight standard test images, and an objective no-reference sharpness-metric evaluation of the enhancement flow. We report all of these results honestly, including where they are unfavourable: the flattening-flow denoiser is measurably better than the noisy input but trails BM3D and non-local means substantially, and we discuss why, rather than treating denoising as a competitive claim. We are explicit about a hard constraint of this study: standard large-scale benchmarks (BSD500, Kodak24, CBSD68, Set12, HPatches) were not reachable from our computing environment, so evaluation is limited to synthetic primitives, eight diverse standard test images, and one synthetic corner-detection scene; we flag this as the paper's main open limitation rather than obscuring it, and we discuss exactly what a full evaluation on those datasets would require. All code is publicly available on GitHub (link in Code Availability) and provided as supplementary material. medskipnoindentKeywords: discrete differential geometry, combinatorial Yamabe flow, discrete Gauss--Bonnet, image curvature, conformal image processing, structure-preserving smoothing

articles.title: Growing-season Arctic carbon fluxes are changing relatively faster in tundra than in boreal ecosystems
articles.abstract: Rapid Arctic warming is altering ecosystem functioning and challenging the view of the terrestrial Arctic as a sustained carbon sink. Drawing on independent evidence from warming experiments, satellite observations, data-driven eddy-covariance-based flux products, and atmospheric inversions, we assess growing-season carbon dioxide (CO2) fluxes across the terrestrial Arctic (60N-90N) between 2001 and 2020. We find that tundra ecosystems exhibit larger relative increases in gross primary productivity (median 7-8%) than boreal regions (median 4-5%), which is also reflected in larger relative increases in solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (median 9% versus 5%) and an overall strengthening of carbon uptake (median of 9-11% versus 3-5%) between the two decades. Despite differences among datasets, their agreement on broad-scale patterns suggests that Arctic warming is reshaping tundra carbon dynamics faster than those of boreal ecosystems.

articles.title: Development of Sustainable Water-Based Functional Coatings for Enhanced Surface Performance
articles.abstract: To keep the surface functionality needed for applications while decreasing the environmental impact of solvents, water-based coating systems are a promising path. The environmental profile of a coating, however, is not only dependent on whether it is made with an aqueous formulation, but also on the end-of-life impacts, on the durability, on the processing needs, on the functional additives and on the sustainability of the raw materials used. The present study aims at designing sustainable water-based functional coatings and testing their surface, mechanical, hydrophobic and protective characteristics. Compositions of coatings were developed with a waterborne matrix containing sustainable and functional additives, and were applied to [substrate] and cured under [curing conditions]. The coatings obtained were characterised by the techniques of [contact angle, adhesion, hardness/abrasion, surface morphology, corrosion/protective performance]. Experimental results indicated that [insert principal finding, quantitative result obtained: [insert key quantitative result] with [insert property] versus [reference/control coating]. The developed formulation also demonstrated [insert finding (mechanical, hydrophobic, protective)]; it also retained [insert durability/performance outcome]. In general, the results showed that the developed water-based coating [did not/did] provide better environment-friendly properties and the functional surface properties, which is implicated to the sustainable coating development and application.

articles.title: Physical Sufficiency and Predictive Identifiability in Amino-Acid Transfer-Energy Representations
articles.abstract: A molecular representation can preserve every recorded physical response yet fail to determine predictions throughout a validation protocol. We develop an observer-conditioned reduction framework that separates these two preservation requirements and supplies explicit failure certificates. On the canonical twenty-residue Wimley–White octanol record, a five-coordinate physical representation 𝑞2 is injective and inclusion-minimal within its declared primitive family. Its affine design has rank six and cospark two: every single-residue deletion preserves rank, but deleting cysteine and methionine removes the sulfur direction. Thus finite physical sufficiency coexists with failure of nested leave-one-out predictive identifiability. Exact fiber-loss certificates quantify physical refinement, while sixteen alternative minimal injective encodings rule out uniqueness from injectivity alone. The protocol-specific rank gate reduces 262 low-capacity predictive states to 131; none preserves the complete 𝑞2 state within the tested descriptor grammar. Fully nested 𝑄2 values are 0.825, 0.529, 0.586 and 0.213 for octanol transfer, membrane-interface transfer, translocon insertion and the Moon–Fleming scale. Algorithm-matched permutation evidence remains conditional on the retrospectively fixed pipeline. Shared predictive alignment survives a joint-profile-preserving permutation test, without identifying a unique common geometry. An external structure-only FreeSolv demonstration reproduces validation-induced rank loss. Chemotype holdouts delimit extrapolation, and prospective noncanonical validation remains open. Scientific Contribution Physical sufficiency and predictive identifiability require different equivalence relations. The contribution is their integration into an auditable reduction protocol, with a direct finite counterexample to their equivalence. Established projection, thermodynamic-cycle, graph-cycle and sparse-linear-algebra identities supply the certificates; novelty is not assigned to these identities in isolation.

articles.title: Electrochemical Preparation of UCl3 -LiCl-KCl Molten Salt in a Frit-Separated Cell
articles.abstract: Electrorefining in pyroprocessing requires (:3-10:wt.%:UCl3) in the(::LiCl-KCl) molten salt, but current preparation routes rely on (:CdCl₂) or corrosive chlorinating gases. Here, (:UCl₃-LiCl-KCl) molten salt was prepared electrochemically at 773 K in a frit-separated cell. The route drives the following reaction (:U+3LiCl:→UCl3+3Li): metallic uranium is dissolved anodically to supply (:U³⁺) and the Li is generated at the cathode. The suitability of Cd and Bi as the liquid-metal cathode to capture Li was evaluated first. Bi proved better suited than Cd and was adopted for the subsequent runs. Impedance spectroscopy showed that conduction across the frit added 7.1 Ω, increasing the ohmic loss while providing the separation needed to suppress U³⁺ crossover from anode to cathode. Over ten consecutive runs at 0.5 and 1.0 A, the UCl3 concentration in the anode compartment increased almost linearly to 12.45 and 12.57 wt.%, with comparable apparent current efficiencies of 95.5% and 96.4%. Because UCl3 is generated electrochemically in situ, this route offers several advantages: it requires no chlorinating reagent, introduces no additional metallic impurity, and allows the UCl3 concentration to be set directly by the charge passed.

articles.title: Modulating Effects of Amino Acids on Low-Temperature Plasma-Induced DNA Damage
articles.abstract: Low-temperature plasma (LTP) generates reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) and can lower the pH, both of which can damage DNA in aqueous solution. Here we examined how amino acids modulate LTP-induced DNA damage. Plasmid DNA, with or without phosphate buffer (PB), was irradiated with a helium plasma jet, and strand breaks were quantified by gel electrophoresis. With PB holding the pH near neutral, the single-strand break (SSB) yield fell to (5.1 ± 1.0) × 10⁻⁹ SSB·Da⁻¹·s⁻¹. Without PB, the solution pH decreased and the yield was (19.4 ± 2.1) × 10⁻⁹ SSB·Da⁻¹·s⁻¹, indicating that acidification contributes to the damage. Tryptophan, tyrosine, and methionine at 10–300 µM protected DNA increasingly with concentration, both with and without PB. Because the protection persisted when PB held the pH constant, it was not primarily due to pH buffering. A competitive coumarin assay showed that dimethyl sulfoxide, a radical scavenger, reduced the fraction of plasma-generated hydroxyl radicals (•OH) available to react with coumarin. No significant difference was observed among the three amino acids, consistent with their similar rate constants for reactions with •OH. LTP-induced DNA damage thus arises from both RONS and acidification, and amino acids at µM concentrations reduce the RONS-driven component, most likely through radical scavenging.

articles.title: Configuration Design and Experimental Verification of Flow Field in Electrochemical Machining of Blisk Profiles
articles.abstract: Electrochemical machining (ECM) is widely applied in aerospace and other industries, and has become one of the core technologies for blisk manufacturing. Flow field stability is a key factor affecting the machining stability and surface quality of ECM. In view of the structural characteristics and machining difficulties of blisk blade surfaces, four three-dimensional flow modes with additional electrolyte flow at the leading and trailing edges were designed, and finite element simulations were conducted for these four flow modes. The results show that the flow mode with an additional electrolyte inlet length of 12 mm achieves better performance, with higher electrolyte velocity and more uniform flow field distribution. In addition, cathode deformation caused by pressure difference was also analyzed to evaluate the rationality of the flow field under the four flow modes. Verification experiments were carried out, and the experimental results are consistent with the simulation results. With the optimized flow field model, the machining process is stable and high surface quality can be obtained.

articles.title: Cooperative NHC/LA Catalysis for Stereoselective Strain-Release Difunctionalization of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes to 1,1,3,3-Tetrasubstituted Cyclobutanes
articles.abstract: The stereoselective synthesis of densely substituted cyclobutanes has emerged as an important frontier in contemporary molecular synthesis, owing to their value as three-dimensional building blocks and bioisosteric motifs. Here we report a cooperative N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)/Lewis acid catalytic strategy for strain-release difunctionalization of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) with α,β-unsaturated aldehydes, affording 1,1,3,3-tetrasubstituted cyclobutanes in up to 94% yield with excellent syn-diastereoselectivity across a broad substrate scope. Most reactions reach completion within 15 min at room temperature. Mechanistic studies, including isolation of a 2-oxabicyclo[2.1.1]hexane intermediate and its subsequent conversion to the cyclobutane product under the catalytic conditions, establish its involvement in the reaction pathway. The data support Lewis acid-assisted C–O σ-bond cleavage followed by NHC-mediated ring opening and rearrangement. This transformation reveals an unconventional mode of NHC reactivity in strain-release chemistry and demonstrates how cooperative NHC/Lewis acid catalysis can redirect the reactivity of strained oxygenated bicyclic intermediates.

articles.title: q-Mittag–Leffler Resolvents for Nonlinear Caputo q-Fractional Equations: Well-Posedness, Stability, and the q → 1− Classical Limit
articles.abstract: This work studies a nonlinear semilinear Caputo q-fractional problem on a finite q-time horizon. The analysis is based on the associated resolvent operator and the q-Mittag–Leffler function. Under suitable q-dependent assumptions, existence and uniqueness of solutions are established through a contraction argument. Continuous dependence is obtained using a fractional Gronwall-type estimate, while a Lyapunov approach provides a stability result. Numerical experiments for linear and nonlinear relaxation models confirm the theoretical convergence toward the classical fractional case as q approaches one. The results emphasize the role of the q-Mittag–Leffler function as a natural resolvent structure and clarify the connection between quantum and classical fractional dynamics. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: 26A33; 33D05; 39A13; 34A08.

articles.title: Nonlinear Nabla Caputo q-Fractional Difference Equations on Quantum Time Scales: Well-Posedness, Order Preservation, and the Classical q → 1− Limit
articles.abstract: This work develops a nonlinear initial-value framework for Caputo-type q-fractional dynamics on the quantum time scale. The analysis is carried out through an equivalent Jackson–Volterra formulation, which allows us to establish existence, uniqueness, and continuous dependence of solutions under suitable contraction assumptions. The positivity of the fractional q-integral is then used to derive an order-preservation principle for nonlinear terms that are nondecreasing in the state variable. We also examine the connection between the quantum model and its classical fractional counterpart as q approaches one. Numerical examples involving linear and nonlinear relaxation problems support the theoretical results and illustrate the convergence behavior of the proposed framework. The study extends earlier linear q-Mittag–Leffler constructions to a nonlinear setting and provides a unified perspective on well-posedness, order structure, and the classical-limit behavior of q-fractional systems. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: 26A33; 39A12; 39A70; 34A08.

articles.title: Short-Range Modulated Electron Lattice and d-Wave Superconductivity in Cuprates: A Phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau Framework
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.03368v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A short-range charge modulation near 0.3 reciprocal lattice units along the Cu-O bond is present in every hole-doped cuprate family. Resonant x-ray scattering now shows that superconductivity does two opposite things to it at once: below Tc the modulation weakens yet becomes more phase coherent. We trace this split to symmetry: the modulation's envelope carries lattice momentum, which leaves a d-wave condensate exactly two ways to couple to it at quartic order, through the modulation's amplitude or through its phase. The first moves amplitude, coherence, and superfluid stiffness together; the second buys coherence at the expense of stiffness, so the two are separately measurable. We call this Ginzburg-Landau framework the modulated electron lattice (MEL). Classical Monte Carlo on 120x120 lattices with quenched disorder places the x-ray observation, read as a single component, at competing amplitude coupling and cooperative phase coupling, where the model gives no stiffness gain. But the measured intensity sums bond-centred and site-centred components. A two-component simulation gives the same pair of bulk signatures, intensity down and coherence up, both with a stiffness loss and with a stiffness gain, depending on the strength of the bond channel. Bulk data therefore cannot say whether this charge order stiffens the superconductor or softens it. What settles the question is the bond-channel amplitude, which form-factor-resolved scattering and phase-resolved tunnelling measure. The response follows the local pairing amplitude, so its onset need not be sharp at Tc. We also compute vortex pinning in the modulated landscape and obtain an in-plane penetration depth of about 124 nm once the transition temperature fixes the energy scale. This version corrects the first: its linear envelope coupling was symmetry-forbidden, and all numerical results are new.

articles.title: Theoretical Prediction of Optimal T_c and Fermi Pockets in Nickelate Superconductors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.06083v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-pressure bilayer La₃₋ₓSmₓNi₂O₇₋δ (LSNO) reaches a record T_c=96 K, triggering wide discussion on the T_c ceiling of nickelate superconductors. We show monoclinic and tetragonal LSNO share the same octahedral quantum-well motif governing T_c with YBa₂Cu₃O₇₋δ (YBCO). Using the Planckian quantum-well scaling T_c = Λ/ξ² (ξ: lattice-modulated quantum-well depth), we obtain T_c=93.4 K and 97.1 K for monoclinic and tetragonal LSNO, matching experimental values 92 K and 96 K. Despite distinct stoichiometry and global symmetry (P2₁/m for LSNO, Pmmm for orthorhombic YBCO), both systems have nearly identical ξ (3.6629 angstrom vs. 3.6720 angstrom) and consistent T_c responses. Further calculations yield a universal T_c limit sim100 K for rare-earth nickelates, irrespective of stacking sequences. We examine four nickelate multilayer stacking variants: 2222 (pure bilayer), 1212 (alternating single-bilayer), 2323 (bilayer-trilayer), and 1313 (single-trilayer). Mirror symmetry breaking of coupled twin quantum wells, unique to bilayer nickelates, dictates γ Fermi pocket formation and ambient-pressure superconductivity. We further prove Fermi surfaces constitute a hologram of quantum-well electrons, establishing intrinsic links between quantum-well symmetry breaking, Fermi pocket structural evolution, and superconducting properties.

articles.title: Trion liquid and its photoemission signatures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.02323v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the formation of a trion liquid in doped low-dimensional semiconductors with strong electron-hole interactions and analyze its signatures in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). We show that this strongly correlated state of matter forms naturally in the vicinity of the phase boundary between a normal band insulator and an excitonic insulator upon doping. By studying the photoemission spectrum, we show that a partially occupied trion band gives rise to an in-gap feature in the ARPES spectrum with vanishing spectral weight at the Fermi energy. We demonstrate our findings using a 1D microscopic model employing exact, unbiased, matrix product state (MPS)-based calculations.

articles.title: Topological Defects in Amorphous Solids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.07061v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Topological defects (TDs) are crucial for understanding important physical properties of crystalline materials including mechanical failure, ion transport, and two-dimensional melting. This concept has not translated to disordered materials like glasses because these solids have no obvious reference structure that can be used to define TDs. As a result, key properties related to those listed above have typically been modeled using purely phenomenological approaches. Recent studies have demonstrated that certain observables commonly associated with TDs can also be identified in disordered solids indicating that topological concepts may be as crucial in amorphous solids as in crystals. This hints that TDs may offer a first-principles framework for understanding their mechanical response and complex spatiotemporal dynamics. In this Perspective, we review recent theoretical, numerical, and experimental studies that have exploited topological concepts to rationalize mechanical properties of amorphous solids. We also highlight pressing open questions and some promising directions for future research in the field.

articles.title: Quantum geometry phenomena in condensed matter systems
articles.abstract: Author(s): Anyuan Gao, Naoto Nagaosa, Ni Ni, and Su-Yang Xu The observation by Berry that adiabatic transport around a closed loop leads to a phase in addition to that determined by the energy spectrum lies at the heart of topology in solids. Such geometrical effects have measurable physical consequences, notably quantum Hall physics in the absence of an external magnetic field—all of which are encapsulated by the quantum geometric tensor. The imaginary part of this tensor is the Berry curvature, and the real part encodes the distance between nearby wave functions and hence is referred to as the quantum metric. In recent years, the quantum geometric tensor has proven central to novel many-body effects in quantum matter, including superconductivity in flat-band systems, third-order nonlinear Hall effects, and second-harmonic nonlinear Hall effects, to name a few. This review catalogs these advances with an eye toward showing how new many-body effects arise from quantum geometry. [Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 035005] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026
