Aggregated to Modified ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, all three clustered spatially (Moran's I 0.507–0.674; all p<0.001), concentrating in the Bronx and Upper Manhattan, and all three were positively correlated with neighborhood poverty (r=0.35–0.66). In spatial lag models, hydrant requests were independently associated with Hispanic population share, power outage requests with all sociodemographic predictors examined, and ventilation requests with poverty. In exploratory secondary analyses, ventilation requests corresponded most closely with heat-illness EMS dispatch rates, while cooling center density showed weak or no association with any category. Heat-related 311 requests appear to index distinct dimensions of heat burden, including informal cooling, infrastructure strain, and housing conditions, and may complement conventional heat metrics in targeting urban heat interventions.

articles.title: Towards Quantum Decision Intelligence: A Four-Qubit Architecture for Venture Capital's Non-Linear Dilemmas on a 156-Qubit IBM Heron Processor
articles.abstract: Early-stage venture screening requires navigating non-linear compensatory trade-offs that linear scoring models struggle to capture. We propose HQDIS, a parsimonious 4-qubit Variational Quantum Circuit (13 parameters) for a stylized version of this problem, conceptually motivated by a published study of Canadian venture investors (Bachher, Díaz de León, and Guild, 1999). Calibration uses a synthetic N = 45 benchmark (Benchmark A) authored by the researchers, not real historical decisions. We introduce a monotonic angular-scaling protocol (π/4) that provably prevents a phase-inversion aliasing failure in a common feature map. Under Repeated Stratified 5-Fold Cross-Validation (100 repeated resampling runs over the same 45 cases, not 100 independent samples), HQDIS attains 80.33% (± 2.72%, 95% CI) accuracy, statistically indistinguishable from Random Forest and Gradient Boosting (Nadeau–Bengio p > 0.7); Logistic Regression attains a nominally higher 91.56% (p = 0.133, d=-0.77), a gap our tests lack power to confirm at N = 45. Ablation shows a nominal 7-point gap and a medium effect size (d ≈ 0.51) between the full circuit and variants lacking ansatz entanglement, but the formal paired test does not reach significance (p ≈ 0.32) at this sample size. We execute Benchmark A on IBM's 156-qubit Heron processor (ibm_fez), obtaining 93.33% hardware accuracy and 97.78% concordance with simulation (κ = 0.9552; r = 0.9943) — a measure of hardware-simulation fidelity, not predictive validity. A counterfactual sweep on one boundary case demonstrates a reproducible auditability mechanism. In a second, explicitly synthetic benchmark (Benchmark B) built to favor non-linear rules, Logistic Regression significantly outperformed HQDIS in accuracy (paired p = 0.025) across 10 seeds, while HQDIS showed a non-significant nominal AUC-ROC advantage (paired p = 0.141); Random Forest significantly exceeded HQDIS on both metrics. We report this mixed result in full. We discuss the resulting, circumscribed implications for quantum decision-support architectures and report Benchmark A's synthetic construction as a central scope limitation.

articles.title: Design-Based Study of an Invisible Field Tool for Endangered Languages
articles.abstract: This study examines the design and field impact of an Excel-VBA based validation tool, developed to serve as an auxiliary utility on the Mozilla Common Voice platform for two endangered Circassian languages, Adyghe (ady) and Kabardian (kbd). Both languages were institutionalized with distinct Cyrillic standards between 1936 and 1938 (Topçu, 2006). Diasporic distribution, complex dialectal structures, and low literacy rates make crowdsourced data collection processes particularly sensitive (Leivada et al., 2019). Framed within Design-Based Research, the tool was developed through seven iterative versions (v1.0.0–v2.1.0, April 2025–August 2026). It combines sentence topic classification, palochka (U+04C0, U+04CF) validation, variant-based automatic grouping, statistics, and ady↔tr/kbd↔tr transliteration features into a single graphical user interface. The findings reveal that the workflow—which previously required specific IT knowledge—was simplified to make it accessible for non-experts, thereby positively affecting participant morale. Both communities showed resistance to Latin transliteration; this finding demonstrates that community orthography preferences in language technology design can outweigh technical functionality. The study argues that the layer of "invisible field tools" in endangered language technologies is critical for participant sustainability and data quality.

articles.title: Microstructure homogeneity control of GH4706 superalloy turbine disc prepared by integral hot forming
articles.abstract: Coarse mixed grains originating from strain-deficient regions during one-step integral hot forming compromise the properties of ultra-large GH4706 superalloy turbine disks. Different from conventional tuning methods centered on temperature and strain rate, this study proposes a homogeneity-oriented control strategy that incorporates an optimized pre-forging step, wherein die geometry is utilized as the primary regulation approach to redistribute the overall strain. This study combines multi-field, multi-scale finite element simulation with Taguchi experimental design and signal-to-noise ratio analysis to realize co-optimization of the overall average grain size (AVG) and its standard deviation (SD). A dual quantification framework integrating analysis of variance (ANOVA) and Sobol sensitivity analysis is adopted, in which the ANOVA contribution rates are validated by first-order Sobol indices calculated via Monte Carlo simulation. The results indicate that pre-forging die geometry is the dominant influencing factor, with a total contribution of 67.0% (concave radius: 36.4%, underfilling height: 21.3%, die angle: 9.3%), followed by strain rate with a contribution of 29.9%. By contrast, deformation temperature only contributes 3.1% within the pre-screened range of 1110–1140 ℃. Accordingly, it is concluded that the geometric tolerance of pre-forging dies should be strictly controlled, while the deformation temperature window can be appropriately relaxed. Under the optimal parameter combination, the grain size at all 12 cross-section verification points is less than 40 µm, the standard deviation of grain size is less than 4 µm, and coarse mixed grains with a size exceeding 40 µm are substantially eliminated. Production verification conducted on a scaled forging with a diameter of 660 mm confirms that uniformly recrystallized microstructures are obtained at all six sampling positions, and the dynamic recrystallization (DRX) fraction at the hub end exceeds 70%. This study provides a validated and cost-effective design foundation for the full-scale integral hot forging of ultra-large turbine disks.

articles.title: Tissue-specific responses of largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides) to acute hyperosmotic stress: an integrated assessment across serum, gill, and liver
articles.abstract: Micropterus salmoides, a major freshwater commercial fish in China, shows adaptability to saline–alkali water. This study systematically evaluated its behavioral responses, tissue adaptability, biomarker changes, and regulatory mechanisms under hyperosmotic conditions (salinity 14.0‰). The 96-h LC50 for salinity was 13.63‰, and mortality was positively correlated with increasing salinity. Short-term hyperosmotic stress significantly impaired locomotor ability, reducing total swimming distance and average speed while increasing immobility time. Under hyperosmotic conditions, severe damage was observed in gill and liver tissues, including curling and fusion of gill filaments, epithelial hyperplasia and desquamation, as well as liver cell disorganization, vacuolization, and inflammatory infiltration. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed disruption of circular microvilli on the gill surface and abnormal mucous cell secretion. In early stress, compared with the freshwater control group, antioxidant markers (SOD, CAT, GSH-PX) in serum, gills, and liver were significantly suppressed, while malondialdehyde levels rose. Key energy metabolism markers (TC, TG, COR), immune markers (ACP, ALP), and osmotic markers (Na⁺/K⁺-ATP, Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺-ATP) all increased initially before gradually declining. IBRv2 analysis showed that biomarker disturbances emerged in serum and gills at 12 h, with subsequent shifts in energy metabolism and immune indicators at 24 h. At high-salinity group, osmoregulatory genes (atp1a2a, slc9a3, cftr) and pro-inflammatory factors (cox-2, il-6, tnf-α) were significantly upregulated in gill tissue. In the liver, glucose metabolism genes (hk, pk, gk) and lipid metabolism genes (fabp7a, acca, ppara) all showed an initial increase followed by a decrease. These results indicate that the tissue response of largemouth bass in hyperosmotic environments exhibits a time-dependent pattern, with tissue damage causing oxidative stress, metabolic disruption, immune suppression, and ion imbalance.

articles.title: A Minimization Approach for the Design of TIR Collimators with Freeform Surfaces
articles.abstract: Inverse optical design methods have been widely developed for systems consisting solely of refractive or reflective elements, whereas catadioptric systems, which combine both, remain less explored from a mathematical perspective. In this article, we present an inverse design approach that iteratively updates an initial optical design to minimize the Wasserstein distance between the light distribution it produces and a prescribed target distribution. We demonstrate the method on a total internal reflection (TIR) collimator. Due to its rotational symmetry and the use of a point source, the problem admits a two-dimensional formulation while yielding a three-dimensional design. In this setting, the refractive and reflective ray paths can be treated independently, which allows the resulting minimization problem to be solved efficiently using a gradient-descent method. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed approach accurately reconstructs the desired target intensity distribution and the associated freeform optical surfaces. The presented methodology provides a first step toward the design of more general lens–reflector systems.

articles.title: Changing patterns of heat waves and population exposure in India, 1980-2024
articles.abstract: India's intensifying heat waves pose significant risks, yet conventional indices overlook two critical hazard dimensions: nocturnal heat stress that impairs physiological recovery and antecedent drought conditions that amplify surface heating. We present the Entropy Weighted Heat Wave Peril Index (E-HWPI), a novel six-component composite index quantifying heat wave hazard across all 36 Indian states and union territories at 0.25° resolution using India Meteorological Department gridded data (1980–2024). E-HWPI integrates four classical heat wave parameters-peak magnitude, cross-event severity, annual frequency, and mean spell duration-with two innovations: Nocturnal Heat Stress (NoctHS), tracking minimum temperature anomalies during spells, and Compound Drought Heat Index (CompDHI), capturing antecedent monsoon rainfall deficits. Shannon entropy weighting with a five percent minimum floor assigns objective, data-driven component weights. Our March-June focus reflects documented physical mechanisms for heat wave development and drought-heat interactions. Trend analysis reveals weak long-term intensification (Mann-Kendall tau = 0.065, p = 0.538). CompDHI exhibits the strongest temporal signal, with minimal correlation (r < 0.25) to classical components, confirming it captures independent drought-compound information. NoctHS correlates strongly with daytime metrics (r approx. 0.83–0.92), indicating physiological distinctness despite statistical overlap; the five percent floor preserves its nocturnal recovery contribution despite low entropy-assigned weight. Five states reach Extreme risk status: Haryana (0.2026), Uttar Pradesh (0.2016), Rajasthan (0.2001), Punjab (0.1892), and Madhya Pradesh (0.1757). Annual population exposure peaks at 294 million person-events in 2010. E-HWPI provides a reproducible, spatially explicit evidence base for differentiated heat governance across India.

articles.title: Structural, Optical and Electrical Insights into Biosynthesised CaO Nanoparticles using Lemon Peel Powder Extract
articles.abstract: Calcium Oxide nanoparticles (CaO NPs) were synthesised using Lemon Peel Powder Extract (LPE) (LPE-CaO NPs) through ultrasonic-assisted coprecipitation. The XRD pattern reveals the formation of crystalline LPE-CaO NPs with an FCC crystal structure, space group is F m-3 m, and the average crystallite size is 67.9977 nm. UV-Visible spectroscopy showed the maximum absorbance peaks at 264 nm for LPE, while the characteristic absorption at 300 nm in biosynthesised LPE-CaO NPs, indicates the CaO NPs formation. The photoluminescence (PL) study shows an intense emission peak centred at ~ 380 nm, which is consistent with the direct band gap (~ 3.181 eV) obtained from Tauc plot analysis. The FTIR peak at 522 cm− 1, attributed to the Ca-O stretching vibrations, supports the formation of CaO NPs, while FTIR peaks of LPE at 1224 cm− 1 and 1026 cm− 1 were attributed to the C-O and C-O-C stretching vibrations, acting as reducing and capping agents in the synthesis of CaO NPs. FESEM images show nearly spherical morphology, and the average particle size of LPE-CaO NPs is 87.88 ± 19.47 nm. Electrical impedance, electric modulus, and electrical conductivity have been examined at the frequency (f) (100 Hz-1 MHz) in the temperature range (303 K-383 K). The impedance decreases with increasing temperature, indicating a negative temperature coefficient of resistance (NTCR) in LPE-CaO NPs. The relaxation peaks in electric modulus analysis shift to higher frequencies with increasing temperature, indicating a decrease in relaxation time and confirming a thermally activated relaxation process. The activation energies obtained from electrical impedance (EaZ = 0.0741 eV) and electric modulus (EaM = 0.073 eV) are closely in agreement, supporting thermally activated relaxation behaviour in LPE-CaO NPs. Therefore, these findings establish LPE-CaO NPs as a promising material for applications involving thermally activated electrical responses.

articles.title: Carbonation-Based Recycling of Concrete Wash Water for Pollution Control and CO 2 Sequestration
articles.abstract: This study proposes an integrated cleaner-production route that combines accelerated CO₂ mineralization with wastewater recycling for the treatment of concrete wash water (CWW) from ready-mixed concrete production. CWW was carbonated through gas-liquid mixing to produce carbonated concrete wash water (CCWW), which was subsequently reused as mixing water for cement mortar. The results showed that, compared with the potable-water reference group, the use of CCWW reduced the drying shrinkage by 52.9%, increased the compressive strength by 13.0%, and decreased the flowability by 12.6%. In addition, quantitative substitution tests indicated that when the replacement ratio of mixing water by CCWW was lower than 50%, the relevant performance requirements could still be satisfied. Furthermore, optimization of the solid/liquid ratio, CO₂ flow rate, and cooling-water temperature by response surface methodology increased the CO₂ absorption rate by 14.1%, reaching 18.6 g/min. These findings demonstrate that accelerated carbonation of CWW provides a feasible route for simultaneous wastewater reutilization and CO₂ sequestration.

articles.title: Quantifying Environmental and Demographic Stochasticity in Population Viability Analysis: The Case of Rissa tridactyla
articles.abstract: Mathematical models that incorporate stochasticity are essential for understanding population dynamics and assessing extinction risk in fluctuating environments. In this study, we investigate the extinction risk of the Black-legged Kittiwake (Rissa tridactyla) using deterministic and stochastic population growth models. Population data obtained from the Global Population Dynamics Database (GPDD) were fitted using exponential, Gompertz and logistic growth models, with model selection based on the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). The logistic model provided the best description of the observed population dynamics and was subsequently extended to incorporate demographic and environmental stochasticity through stochastic differential equations. Model parameters were estimated using maximum likelihood estimation, which identified demographic stochasticity as the dominant source of population variability. Future population trajectories were projected using Monte Carlo simulations, yielding an estimated 53.1% probability of quasi-extinction within the next 30 years. Confidence and prediction intervals demonstrated good agreement between model predictions and observed data, supporting the reliability of the proposed framework. These findings emphasize the importance of incorporating stochastic processes into population viability analyses and provide valuable quantitative insights for assessing extinction risk and informing conservation strategies for vulnerable seabird populations.

articles.title: When Continental Powers Rise at Sea: China’s Maritime Balancing Escalation
articles.abstract: Why do continental powers sometimes move beyond asymmetric sea denial and undertake costly competition in the core functions of maritime power? Classical geopolitical theory expects land powers to remain constrained by continental security burdens and therefore to favor limited, cost-effective naval strategies. This article challenges that expectation by developing the concept of maritime balancing escalation. It argues that escalation becomes more likely when landward security burdens ease, the power gap with the dominant maritime rival narrows enough to make sustained naval competition feasible, maritime pressure intensifies, and ruling elites give greater priority to sea power. China provides a theory-building case. For decades, Beijing balanced U.S. maritime superiority mainly through shore-supported denial capabilities. Since the early 2010s, it has retained those capabilities while adding carrier aviation, large surface combatants, amphibious forces, and far-seas support. The article shows when continental constraints become less binding and maritime balancing shifts toward broader functional competition.

articles.title: Plasma-coupled electrothermal ultrahigh-temperature graphitization of non‑graphitizable hard carbons via heterogeneous edge-seeded layer growth
articles.abstract: Graphitization is inherently limited by solid‑state carbon self‑diffusion, whose activation energy (682 kJ mol−1) ranks among the highest recorded for elemental solids, underpinning the 70‑year dichotomy between graphitizable soft and non‑graphitizable hard carbons. Industrial production currently relies on multi‑day annealing of fossil‑derived coke in Acheson furnaces. Here we report a plasma‑coupled electrothermal ultrahigh-temperature synthesis (PCES) strategy that couples bulk Joule heating and localized interfacial plasma excitation in a two‑stage sequence, achieving spatially uniform temperatures above 3500 K within seconds to directly surmount the carbon diffusion barrier. Ex-situ electron microscopy and ReaxFF simulations reveal a heterogeneous edge-seeded layer growth mechanism: reactive carbon species at particle interfaces condense epitaxially onto nascent sp2 nuclei, bypassing sluggish bulk rearrangement and avoiding turbostratic disorder. We achieve 98 % graphitization of renewable hard carbon precursors, yielding Bernal‑stacked graphite with performance matching commercial battery‑grade graphite. A modular hexagonal reactor design decouples heating kinetics from scale, supporting projected ton-per-day output at about 60% lower energy than Acheson furnaces.

articles.title: Power-Optimal Covariate Adjustment for Switchback Experiments
articles.abstract: In switchback experiments with unequal cluster sizes, outcome dispersion across randomization units inflates estimator variance and limits statistical power. Standard control-using-prediction-as-covariate (CUPAC) adjustment may be suboptimal for variance reduction in this setting, because in its basic form it targets overall predictive accuracy and does not distinguish between the components of variance that vary across the randomization units of switchback experiments and those that vary across individual observations, even though these components contribute unequally to estimator variance. We propose a power-optimal variance reduction methodology via CUPAC that balances prediction of the noise between and within randomization units to achieve maximum statistical power. The methodology utilizes the framework for decomposition of the variance of the treatment-effect estimator for switchback experiments, and adapts both the outcome prediction and the analysis-time residualization to minimize the treatment-effect variance. We develop the theoretical framework for the power-optimal CUPAC and validate it in a Monte Carlo simulation study using gradient-boosted trees.

articles.title: Buffalo Grazing Effects on the Physical–Mechanical Quality and Load-Bearing Capacity of Hydromorphic Riparian Soils in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest
articles.abstract: Background and Aims Buffalo production is an economically relevant alternative in Brazilian livestock systems, particularly in São Paulo State. However, intensifying this activity in hydromorphic soils of Atlantic Forest floodplains may accelerate compaction and structural degradation. This study evaluated the impact of semi-extensive grazing (SEG), intensive grazing for 20 years (IG20), and intensive grazing for 1 year (IG1), compared with native vegetation (NV), on soil erodibility, laboratory penetration resistance (LPR), load-bearing capacity (LBC), and compressibility in hydromorphic soils. Methods Soil samples were collected from four land-use systems at 0.0–0.2 and 0.2–0.4 m depths. Soil erodibility was determined using the K factor of the Universal Soil Loss Equation. LPR was evaluated under two soil water contents, while LBC and compressibility were assessed through uniaxial compression tests under five moisture conditions. Data were analyzed by analysis of variance and Scott-Knott test (p < 0.05), and precompression stress was evaluated by regression as a function of soil moisture. Results Soil erodibility varied among systems and depths, with IG20 showing the highest values and being the only treatment classified as highly erodible in the subsurface layer. LPR increased under drier conditions, whereas LBC decreased with increasing soil moisture. NV showed the highest LBC, while IG20 exhibited greater sensitivity to moisture changes and increased structural vulnerability. Conclusion Soil moisture strongly controls the mechanical behavior of hydromorphic soils, while grazing management influences their susceptibility to compaction and erosion. Combining physical-mechanical indicators with erodibility assessments can support sustainable management of floodplain environments.

articles.abstract: Author(s): Atul Kedia, Jeffrey M. Berryman, Jonathan Cabrera Garcia, Jutta E. Escher, Oliver C. Gorton, Erika M. Holmbeck, Gail C. McLaughlin, Cole D. Pruitt, Andre Sieverding, and Rebecca Surman Where do the heavy elements in our universe come from, and how accurately can we model their creation? Accurately predicting the abundances of elements produced in the weak rapid neutron-capture ( r - process) requires rigorous quantification of nuclear reaction uncertainties far from stability. This work utilizes cross sections with uncertainty-quantified optical potential and considers both independent (uncorrelated) rate variations and rate variations fully correlated via the underlying optical potential. While fully correlated variations alter the covariance structure among elemental yields, they do not automatically reduce the overall uncertainty envelope. By identifying specific neutron capture rates that have the most leverage on the r -process element production, this work provides a roadmap for experimental and theoretical efforts to constrain key nuclear reaction rates. articles.title: Double step nuclear polarization decay under level anticrossing conditions
articles.abstract: Proton spin polarization decay has been measured in paranitrotoluene crystalline powder after a nonadiabatic magnetic field switch from a high polarization field into a low field. At certain magnetic fields, when 14 N– 1 H level anticrossing conditions are satisfied mediated by dipole–dipole interactions, a double step proton polarization decay has been observed. A first step taking place typically in the millisecond range due to polarization transfer is followed by relaxation in the range of tens of seconds. The experiment has been carried out using a homebuilt field cycling relaxometer allowing for sufficiently fast field switching. The observed two step decay is analyzed analytically in terms of the Liouville–von Neumann equation.

articles.title: Nonlocal dielectric response and screening in ionic liquids
articles.abstract: The dielectric response of room-temperature ionic liquids (RTILs) plays a central role in charge screening within these strongly correlated ionic fluids and thereby governs ion transport, electrochemical kinetics, solubility, and related electrochemical phenomena. Here, we present a comprehensive study of the nonlocal, wavenumber-dependent dielectric response function χk in representative RTILs using all-atom molecular dynamics simulations. We identified distinct features of this function χk, including a smeared solvation-induced peak of χk at ∼0.8 Å−1 and, notably, a higher wavenumber (∼2.25 Å−1) overscreening resonance-like peak underpinned by correlated anion-dominated collective structures. The latter points to a screening contribution that is distinct from simple solvation-layer ordering and is reminiscent of finite-wavevector screening features reported earlier in molten salts. To rationalize these features, we introduce a minimal phenomenological spectral representation containing a long-wavelength conducting background, a structural mode, and an additional anion-dominated resonance branch. We further connect the nonlocal dielectric response to screened potentials and solvation of simple ions in RTILs. A smeared Born-sphere representation of the charge density of such ions suppresses overscreening response and gives ion solvation energies in ionic liquids that are comparable to, but generally weaker than, hydration energies in water. These results provide a molecular picture of nonlocal screening in RTILs and highlight that dielectric response in such liquids is governed by several coupled structural modes rather than by a single screening length.

articles.title: Two-color light steers electrons through graphene's transient topological state
articles.abstract: The electronic properties of materials are typically determined by their structure under normal, undisturbed conditions, when they are in a state known as equilibrium. articles.title: Isolation and Characterization of a Clinically-Derived Staphylococcus epidermidis HE23: Revealing Its Antibiotic Resistome and Metabolic Potential
articles.abstract: Neonatal incubators may serve as environmental reservoirs for antimicrobial-resistant bacteria in neonatal intensive care units. In this study, Staphylococcus epidermidis HE23 was isolated from a high-touch surface of a neonatal incubator and characterized using whole-genome sequencing, comparative genomics, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and metabolomic analysis. Hybrid assembly of Illumina and Nanopore sequencing reads generated a complete genome consisting of a circular chromosome (2,542,743 bp) and two plasmids (50,114 bp and 9,031 bp). Genomic analysis identified nine antibiotic resistance genes, including the chromosomal β-lactam resistance determinants blaZ and mecA and the plasmid-borne mupirocin resistance gene mupA. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing further confirmed resistance to multiple antibiotics, including β-lactams and quinolones. Genes associated with resistance to cationic antimicrobial peptides were also identified, suggesting potential mechanisms that may facilitate persistence under antimicrobial pressure. Metabolomic profiling detected several secondary metabolites, including putatively annotated cinobufagin and harmaline. Comparative genomic analysis further revealed conserved and strain-specific genomic features of HE23. The coexistence of chromosomal resistance determinants and plasmid-associated mupA highlights the potential of incubator-associated S. epidermidis to act as a reservoir of antimicrobial resistance in neonatal intensive care environments. These findings support strengthened microbial surveillance and targeted infection-control strategies for neonatal incubators.

articles.title: An Integrated Geospatial Framework for Spatio-Temporal Monitoring of Surface Albedo, Thermal and Vegetation Dynamics in Amrapali Coal-Mine Overburden, Eastern India
articles.abstract: Monitoring coal-mine rehabilitation primarily relies on single vegetation indices, which reflect greenness but overlook surface transitions that precede vegetation growth, and are rarely integrated into a reproducible spatio-temporal workflow. Surface albedo is a promising yet underutilized metric for early-stage reclamation, but integrated multi-indicator assessments remain sparse. This study addresses this gap for the Amrapali opencast coal-mine overburden in Chatra, Jharkhand, establishing a pre-restoration baseline (2013–2026). Annual composites of surface albedo, land surface temperature (LST) and NDVI were derived from Landsat imagery across a 10 km buffer, and land use/land cover (LULC) change was quantified (2015–2025). Trends were assessed with OLS regression, the Mann–Kendall test and Sen's slope, and relationships with Pearson and Spearman correlations. Surface albedo showed a significant declining trend (Mann–Kendall p = 0.004; Sen's slope = − 0.00137 yr⁻¹; R² = 0.60), the clearest signal of landscape change, consistent with progressive darkening of the stabilizing overburden. NDVI showed no significant trend but high variability (CV = 13.4%), and LST remained stable despite an approximately 3.7-fold mine expansion. A significant inverse NDVI–LST relationship (Spearman ρ = −0.55, p = 0.043) confirmed vegetation cooling, whereas weak albedo–LST and NDVI–albedo associations indicate that surface material changes, not canopy greenness, governed the albedo decline. LULC analysis documented contraction of open land ( ~ − 39%) and vegetation ( ~ − 16%) alongside mine, built-up and agricultural expansion. By fusing albedo, LST, NDVI and LULC in a spatially-explicit, multi-temporal framework built on openly available data, this study identifies albedo as a sensitive early-stage indicator and contributes a transparent, transferable geospatial workflow and baseline for evaluating future restoration.

articles.title: Laser experiments recreate solar flare physics and reveal consistent magnetic reconnection rates
articles.abstract: Magnetic reconnection is a process that occurs when the magnetic fields of a conductive plasma quickly rearrange and release massive amounts of stored magnetic energy. It is widely thought to be the underlying mechanism behind cosmic events such as solar flares and substorms in Earth's magnetosphere.

articles.title: High-throughput Discovery of Magnetic Rare Earth Transition Metal Alloys
articles.abstract: We present an accelerated materials discovery framework that combines diffusion-based crystal structure generation with hierarchical screening to identify new rare-earth–transition-metal magnets simultaneously achieving high magnetization and thermodynamic stability. Using this workflow, we systematically explored over 3000 binary (R-T) and ternary (R-T-T ′) compositions spanning R ∈ Y, Sm, T ∈ Fe, Co, Ni, and T ′ ∈ Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Cu, Zn, and filtered approximately 240,000 generated crystal structures through machine-learning interatomic potential prescreening and spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) validation. We identify 300+ low-energy magnetic candidates within 0.1 eV/atom above the convex hull at the DFT level, including 5 thermodynamically stable phases. The highest saturation magnetization reaches ∼1.8 T in Fe-rich binary and ternary phases (SmFe 12 , YFe 12 , YFe 18 Ti and Sm 2 Fe 16 Mn). Symmetry analysis reveals that the majority of ternary candidates are subgroup derivatives of known binary prototypes through Wyckoff site splitting that accommodates T ′ substitution. Site-resolved magnetic moment analysis further shows that Mn aligns ferromagnetically with the Fe sublattice with minimal magnetization loss, whereas Cr couples antiferromagnetically, providing systematic guidance for dopant selection. These findings demonstrate a generalizable strategy for targeted magnetic materials discovery and suggest that extending generative searches to larger unit cells (>20 atoms) with higher Fe fractions is a promising route toward stable phases with saturation magnetization exceeding 1.8 T.

articles.title: Enhancing V2X Communication Security Using an MTCNN-LSTM-Based Multilevel Trust Evaluation Framework
articles.abstract: In the evolution of V2X infrastructure deployment, vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication necessitates authentication, privacy, and dependability. Securing the V2X networks and charging issues is critical and more challenging due to the extensive infrastructure. This direction enables trust-based transactions between electric vehicles and the smart grid to fulfill energy consumption. This paper reveals the closed-loop V2X security and energy allocation system that integrates real-time multi-attack detection, dynamic trust evaluation, and battery optimization in an intelligent transportation system. In the proposed MTCNN-LSTM model, which incorporates multilevel trust and CNN-LSTM, we achieve 94.75% accuracy, 94.83% weighted F1-score, and 99.3% attack detection rate across four attack types (none, sybil, DDoS, and both). Trust based on nine telemetry features(security score, feedback score, behavior score, message frequency, message received, energy consumed, SoC, security score difference, energy consumed rate) It also optimizes the battery consumption during the attack, ensuring that the system can maintain functionality by detecting energy wastage based on the MTCNN-LSTM model, energy waste: 550 kWh at 30 % attack out of the supply by smart grid 2000 kWh for the given dataset "Electric Vehicle Trip Energy Consumption Data” in the simulation based on real data, class-weighted training and multi-speed validation to ensuring secure, resilient and sustainable energy in smart grid enabled V2X network.

articles.title: Electrode Geometry-Controlled Quantum Transport in Au–Pentane–Au Molecular Junctions: A DFT–NEGF and Machine Learning Study
articles.abstract: Molecular electronics offers a route toward continued device miniaturization, but reliable control of charge transport at the molecular scale requires a detailed understanding of the metal–molecule interface. In particular, the role of electrode geometry in determining transport behaviour remains less systematically explored than molecular structure and contact chemistry. Here, we investigate the influence of atomic-scale electrode geometry on the structural, electronic, quantum-transport, thermoelectric, and noise properties of Au–pentane–Au molecular junctions using a combined density functional theory–non-equilibrium Green's function (DFT–NEGF) and machine learning framework. Six representative electrode configurations—Flat Au(111), Pyramidal, Single Apex, Multi-Atom Tip, Nanowire, and Rough Surface—were structurally optimized and systematically compared while maintaining the same pentane molecular backbone and Au–S contact chemistry. The calculations reveal pronounced geometry-dependent variations in Au–S bonding, coordination number, contact area, molecular tilt, charge transfer, electronic-state alignment, and molecule–electrode coupling. These structural and electronic changes directly control quantum transport, with the calculated conductance decreasing from 0.92 G₀ for Flat Au(111) to 0.56 G₀ for the Single Apex configuration. Transmission, current–voltage characteristics, charge redistribution, and interface dipole analysis consistently demonstrate that highly coordinated and extended contacts provide stronger electronic coupling and more efficient transmission pathways. Thermoelectric calculations reveal an opposing trend: lower-coordination contacts exhibit enhanced Seebeck coefficients because of stronger energy dependence of transmission near the Fermi level, whereas the Flat Au(111) junction provides the highest calculated power factor and ZT ≈ 0.68. Shot noise, Fano factor, low-frequency noise, and Hooge-parameter analysis further demonstrate increasing transport fluctuations as electrode coordination decreases. To accelerate transport prediction, a dataset of 1500 configurations were constructed from structural and electronic descriptors extracted from the DFT–NEGF calculations. Among the tested models, XGBoost achieved the highest predictive performance, with a testing R2 of 0.988, RMSE of 0.010 G₀, and MAE of 0.007 G₀. Feature-importance analysis identified Au–S bond length, HOMO–LUMO gap, coupling strength, DOS at the Fermi level, and Au 5d PDOS as the dominant predictors. The trained model successfully predicted conductance for previously unseen electrode configurations, demonstrating its potential for rapid screening of molecular junction structures.

articles.title: Physicists extend the search for quantum black holes at the LHC
articles.abstract: Physicists at UC Santa Barbara have extended the search for evidence of microscopic black holes produced at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN). The formation of these tiny, fleeting objects at the LHC represents one way theorists have sought to resolve anomalies in our understanding of the basic structure of spacetime, while the method used to look for them demonstrates a new way of searching for new particles.

articles.title: An extremely stable quantum gas offers a new lens on strongly interacting systems
articles.abstract: Molecular gases are a new form of artificial quantum matter. However, when these molecules collide, they are often lost extremely rapidly. Researchers from Radboud University and Columbia University have been able to suppress this collisional loss, paving the way for strongly interacting quantum matter. This new artificial quantum matter allows researchers to study quantum behavior relevant to electrons in real materials. Their results are published in Science.

articles.title: The Darma Valley at the Himalayan Trijunction: Community, Territoriality, and Security Dynamics in the Borderland of India, China and Nepal
articles.abstract: Darma Valley is a high-altitude region in the Dharchula tehsil of Pithoragarh district, Uttarakhand, of the Rang or Darmiya Bhotiya community. Although small, the valley is structurally significant in the interface region along the borders of India, China, and Nepal, and it remains relatively understudied. Darma was one of only six passes officially designated for trade and pilgrimage under the Sino-Indian Agreement of 1954 between the Tibet Region of China and India. The centuries-old trans-Himalayan trading economy that sustained the valley became unviable after the Indo-Tibetan border was closed following the war of 1962, and the region was transformed into a heavily militarised border, guarded by the Indo-Tibetan Border Police. Based on the archival treaty material, colonial-era gazetteers, ethnographic scholarship, and government and news sources ranging from 1816 to 2026, this paper places the valley in the context of the larger frontier complex of Dharchula, located adjacent to the contested Trijunctions of Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhara, where multiple interpretations of the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli continue to be a burden on India-Nepal relations with a certain studied ambiguity being displayed by China. In a borderland and securitisation approach the valley is explored as a miniature representation of the governance of the frontier in the Himalayas, where demographic retention, cultural continuity, pilgrimage tourism and infrastructure competition are as crucial in the definition of sovereignty as military presence, as shown in India's Vibrant Villages Programme or China's Xiaokang border village model. The analysis provides a geographically informed example of how human security and agency of the borderlands can be established in high-altitude border areas with contested claims.

articles.title: Thermal Performance and Drying Characteristics of a Solar Assisted Refractance Window Dryer Based on CFD Simulation and Experimental Validation
articles.abstract: Drying is among the most energy-intensive operations in food processing, necessitating the development of technologies that balance energy efficiency with product quality preservation. Refractance Window Drying (RWD) has emerged as a promising fourth-generation drying technique for heat-sensitive materials. This study presents the design, development, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis of a solar-assisted RWD system, complemented by experimental validation. A three-dimensional transient CFD model was developed to investigate coupled heat transfer and airflow characteristics within the drying chamber. Simulation results revealed uniform airflow distribution and stable operating temperatures of approximately 60°C across the drying surface, providing favorable conditions for temperature-sensitive agricultural products. Experimental investigations were conducted using a solar-assisted continuous RWD setup at hot water temperatures of 82, 86, 90, 94, and 98°C with belt speeds of 0.8, 1.1, 1.4, 1.7, and 2.0 m/min. Three system configurations were evaluated: conventional RWD (CRWD), Hybrid RWD System 1 (HRWD 1), and Hybrid RWD System 2 (HRWD 2). The hybrid configurations demonstrated significant performance improvements, with drying time reductions of 18% for HRWD 1 and 37% for HRWD 2 across all operating conditions. The highest moisture removal rate of 22 g/min was achieved at 98°C and 0.8 m/min in HRWD 2, compared to 13.2 g/min for CRWD under identical conditions. The numerical predictions were validated against experimental data, demonstrating a maximum temperature deviation of approximately 5°C. The results confirm that CFD modeling combined with experimental validation is an effective tool for optimizing solar-assisted RWD systems, thereby improving drying uniformity, enhancing energy efficiency, and preserving product quality compared with conventional drying technologies. The developed approach contributes to Sustainable Development Goal 7 through the utilization of renewable solar energy and to Sustainable Development Goal 12 through improved resource-efficient food processing, while its application for agricultural product preservation has potential relevance to SDG 2 by helping reduce post-harvest food losses.

articles.title: Polarization-coupled complete operators in sliding ferroelectric semiconductors for native in-memory attention computing
articles.abstract: Attention computing, central to Transformer-based generative AI, calls for native in-memory hardware with linear and nonlinear operators intrinsically coupled. Current compute-in-memory (CIM), however, remains tailored to linear algebra, lacking integrated nonlinear operators. Here, we demonstrate complete-operator hardware that intrinsically couples both operator types in situ via ferroelectric polarization. Our device integrates a vertical ferroelectric tunnel junction for linear multiply-accumulate operations and a lateral ferroelectric semiconductor field-effect transistor for exponential functions in sliding-ferroelectric semiconductor ReS2. Tuning lateral transport length and vertical barrier thickness yields designable exponential operators with tunable sensitivity and operating range. A fabricated (9×3)×9 array realizes the first in-memory hardware execution of full Transformer attention primitives, including intrinsic Softmax, with device-level 600-ps latency and 320-aJ/operation energy. A closed-loop hardware prototype enables real-time text generation, with experimentally calibrated simulations supporting neural-signal-to-language scalability. This work embeds the missing nonlinearity directly into memory, advancing CIM toward complete, native hardware for generative AI.

articles.title: Development and Evaluation of Target-Specific Machine-Learning Scoring Functions for Monoamine Oxidase B
articles.abstract: Target-specific machine-learning scoring functions (MLSFs) have improved virtual screening for several targets, but their performance depends heavily on benchmark design and modeling choices. Here, we develop and evaluate target-specific MLSFs for human monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B), systematically comparing three modeling decisions: classification versus regression, structure-based (PLEC) versus combined structure- and ligand-based (PLEC + Morgan fingerprint) featurization, and untuned versus hyperparameter-tuned models. Generic scoring function performance was first established on the DUD-E benchmark, then re-evaluated on an independent test set composed exclusively of experimentally confirmed inactive compounds to control for property-matched decoy bias. On DUD-E, RF-Score-VS achieved the highest early enrichment among generic scoring functions (NEF1% = 0.789), but declined to NEF1% = 0.061 on the true-inactive test set — indistinguishable from the native Smina docking score and close to the random baseline (NEF1% = 0.024). Target-specific models trained on 2,328 actives and 121,764 DeepCoy-generated decoys consistently outperformed their classification counterparts: regression exceeded classification for all five algorithms tested. Combining Morgan fingerprints with PLEC features improved performance in five of ten baseline algorithm–task combinations. The best-performing model was tuned XGB regression with combined features (NEF1% = 0.245), exceeding the best generic scoring function on the same test set (CNN-Score, NEF1% = 0.082) by approximately threefold. Hyperparameter optimization did not reliably improve early-recognition performance, and a structural similarity analysis showed that the 25 test actives with above-threshold training-set similarity were retrieved at a substantially higher rate than the remaining 92 (28.0% vs. 5.4% for XGB; 28.0% vs. 2.2% for SVM), indicating that a meaningful share of early-recognition performance reflects structural analogy to known actives rather than generalization to novel chemical space. These findings argue for carefully designed benchmarks, explicit bias controls, and prospective validation in future target-specific MLSF studies.

articles.title: A new bridge for quantum networks: Physicists convert microwaves to light using 2D magnets
articles.abstract: Physicists at The City College of New York have demonstrated a new way to transfer microwave signals onto light using magnetic waves inside a layered semiconductor. The work establishes a materials platform for building interfaces that could one day link quantum computers through optical networks. The research, titled "Microwave-to-optical transduction using magnon–exciton coupling," was led by the Laboratory for Nano and Micro Photonics (LaNMP) at CCNY, headed by physics professor Vinod M. Menon. It appears in the journal Nature Materials.

articles.title: New benchmark puts quantum computers to the test and reveals their limitations
articles.abstract: Quantum computers are no longer theoretical concepts. Today, they are being developed to tackle a range of complex problems, including exploring financial risk, modeling complex molecules and optimizing massive logistics networks. However, until now, there has been no way to benchmark the computational power of different systems on the same scale to see how they compare.

articles.title: Energy-Constrained Joint Power and Hierarchical Beam Optimization for mmWave IoT Networks
articles.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) Internet of Things (IoT) networks rely on hierarchical beam alignment to overcome severe path loss, yet the associated sounding overhead and energy consumption pose significant challenges for low-power devices. This paper investigates joint optimization of transmit power allocation and hierarchical beam resolution under a total energy constraint for two-stage beam alignment. A tractable optimization framework is developed by modeling the alignment success probability using a calibrated analytical function that preserves the non-linear dependencies on transmit power, beam resolution, and line-of-sight (LoS) dominance under Rician fading. This analytical function is designed to be smooth and numerically stable, enabling efficient constrained optimization while avoiding analytically intractable order-statistics formulations. The resulting joint beam--power optimization problem is solved using a lightweight numerical Newton--Lagrange procedure suitable for real-time operation on resource-constrained IoT nodes. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate that the proposed framework successfully captures the essential performance trends and achieves substantial energy savings and improved alignment reliability compared with fixed or heuristic allocation strategies. The results provide practical insight into energy--resolution trade-offs in hierarchical beam alignment for mmWave IoT systems.

articles.title: G-Mamba: A Mechanism-Guided Graph State Space Network for Multi-Objective Prediction in Tyrosine Fermentation Process
articles.abstract: Key core parameters in microbial fermentation processes typically rely on offline chemical analyses characterized by prolonged time delays, which fail to meet the imperatives of real-time, precision process control. Although existing data-driven modeling approaches have been deployed, they still suffer from the dual limitations of excessive computational overhead and a lack of mechanistic guidance when simultaneously capturing temporal evolution trends and complex, nonlinear spatial couplings among variables. To address these challenges, this paper proposes G-Mamba, a gray-box multi-objective prediction network that integrates prior mechanistic knowledge with the selective state space model. Structurally, the core of the model incorporates a bidirectional Mamba architecture to accurately capture the long-sequence temporal dynamics of fermentation processes while maintaining linear computational complexity. Concurrently, a topological adjacency matrix is explicitly formulated by incorporating prior knowledge of cellular metabolic pathways and operational control logic, which operates in tandem with an adaptive adjacency matrix and a graph convolutional network (GCN) to model both explicit kinetics and dynamic latent spatial couplings among variables. Furthermore, a lightweight gated fusion mechanism is designed to adaptively merge deep temporal and spatial features, effectively decoupling inter-variable metabolic competition and synergy. We conducted biomass and product concentration prediction experiments using a multi-batch dataset from an Escherichia coli tyrosine fermentation process. The experimental results demonstrate that G-Mamba consistently outperforms mainstream baseline models across both point prediction and sequence forecasting tasks under various input lengths, exhibiting significant synergistic performance enhancements in multi-objective forecasting scenarios while maintaining superior computational efficiency.

articles.title: A Quantum Information Preserving Photonic Switch for Scalable Quantum Networks
articles.abstract: Current quantum networks are largely constrained to static, point-to-point links, which lack the scalability and resource efficiency required for distributed quantum computing, quantum sensing, and the emerging quantum internet. A critical barrier to progress is the absence of a switching technology capable of routing fragile quantum states without inducing decoherence or distinguishability. Here, we propose the Universal Quantum Switch architecture, a foundational building block allowing non-blocking, encoding-agnostic routing of quantum information, as well as seamless modality conversion between disparate quantum platforms. An integrated photonic prototype in thin-film lithium niobate is developed for polarization entanglement, allowing a reconfiguration rate up to 1 GHz. We experimentally demonstrate robust electro-optic switching of arbitrary entangled states at 1 MHz with an average fidelity of 96% and a purity of 1, which satisfies the requirement of dynamic distributed quantum error correction between arbitrary quantum computing nodes, to the best of our knowledge, for the first time. Complementing these experimental results, we project the architecture's scalability, showing dimension-independent decoherence, and provide a scalable, interoperable building block for heterogeneous quantum network fabrics.

articles.title: A Comprehensive performance evaluation framework for machine learning-based oil, gas and water leak detection systems
articles.abstract: The structural integrity of such pipeline infrastructure is of prime importance for oil, gas, and water industries, but designing an optimal Leak Detection System (LDS) remains a complex challenge due to trade-offs between sensitivity, computational costs, and hardware reliability. In this paper, a critical review and synthesis of recent developments in LDS methodologies are presented, considering the shift from deterministic models of fluid dynamics using mass balance equations to sophisticated data-driven models using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Machine Learning classifiers. Significantly, this review extends beyond algorithmic evaluation to consider the neglected dimension of IoT hardware reliability and edge computing constraints. Recognizing that current evaluation metrics are fragmented across these fields, this study proposes a new Unified Performance Evaluation Framework. Unlike conventional evaluation metrics that consider accuracy only for leak detection systems, this framework combines physical flow dynamics, algorithmic efficiency, and hardware reliability in a unified scoring mechanism. To validate the proposed framework, a case study of a hybrid IoT gas leak detection node for residential kitchens is conducted. The case study results demonstrate that the framework captures critical multi-dimensional performance attributes often overlooked by traditional assessments, including a detection accuracy of 96%, a false alarm rate of only 3%, an ultra-low energy consumption of 50 mJ per detection, a 9.7 years estimated battery lifetime, and a response latency of 15.6 seconds dominated by physical sensor response rather than computational overhead. This paper is a significant contribution for researchers and industry practitioners in designing hybrid leak detection systems that guarantee robust performance for diverse fluid media.

articles.title: Stacked 2D materials reveal room-temperature multiferroicity and voltage-controlled magnetism
articles.abstract: Multiferroics are materials that simultaneously exhibit two or more ferroic orders—stable arrangements of physical properties that can be switched using an external stimulus. These materials could be highly advantageous for the development of various technologies, including non-volatile, low-power memory devices, spintronic devices, miniaturized electronics, neuromorphic hardware, sensors and magnetoelectric devices.

articles.title: Machine-Learning Exploration of Defect Topologies and Thermodynamic Stability in Graphene with Atomic Vacancies
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomic vacancies and vacancy aggregates control the thermodynamic stability and the functional response of graphene, yet the configurational space spanned by many vacancies at variable concentration and separation is too large to be mapped exhaustively by first-principles methods. Here, we map and rationalize this stability landscape by combining semiempirical atomistic thermodynamics, interpretable machine learning, and symbolic regression. Several hundred defective supercells, built from a 72-atom cell by varying the vacancy concentration and the inter-vacancy distance up to the fourth neighbor, were relaxed with the PM7 Hamiltonian in MOPAC, and the heat of formation was adopted as the stability metric. Each structure was encoded with the Dynamic Collision Fingerprint, a translationally and rotationally invariant descriptor that maps the local topology onto transport-like statistics of virtual probe particles. A gradient boosted decision tree model, optimized by Bayesian hyperparameter search, reproduces the heat of formation of an independent test set with a root mean squared error of approximately 23.5~kcal/mol and no evidence of overfitting, and a SHAP analysis identifies the defect concentration and the inter-vacancy distance as the two variables that dominate the stability. Symbolic regression then condenses the learned mapping into a compact closed-form expression that reproduces the heat of formation with a coefficient of determination of R² = 0.9966, a mean absolute error of 15.51~kcal/mol, and a root mean squared error of 24.18~kcal/mol. The workflow turns a high-dimensional structure--stability problem into an interpretable analytical law, providing a transferable route to rational defect engineering in two-dimensional materials.
authors: José R. da M. Lima Filho

articles.title: Comprehensive First-Principles Investigation of the Structural, Mechanical, Electronic, and Optical Properties of Homoelemental Phase T-GaN Monolayer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The exploration of non-hexagonal two-dimensional topologies has opened new possibilities for tailoring the properties of group III-V monolayers beyond those accessible through conventional honeycomb phases. In this context, we have investigated the structural, mechanical, electronic, and optical properties of T-GaN, a two-dimensional tetragonal gallium nitride monolayer composed of alternating four- and eight-membered rings featuring coexisting homoelemental (Ga-Ga, N-N) and heteropolar (Ga-N) bonds, using density functional theory (DFT) within the generalized gradient approximation (GGA/PBE) and the hybrid HSE06 functional. The dynamical stability of T-GaN was confirmed by phonon dispersion calculations, which revealed the absence of imaginary frequencies throughout the Brillouin zone, and was further supported by ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. The mechanical characterization reveals a pronounced in-plane anisotropy, with critical strains of approximately 16.5% and 7.0% along the x- and y-directions, respectively. The electronic band structure analysis indicates that T-GaN is a nonmagnetic semiconductor with an indirect band gap of 0.35~eV (PBE) and 1.15~eV (HSE06), with the valence band maximum dominated by nitrogen 2p orbitals and the conduction band minimum governed by gallium 4s and 4p states. The optical response was evaluated along three crystallographic directions, exhibiting considerable anisotropy in the absorption coefficient, refractive index, and reflectivity. These findings provide new insights into the physical properties of tetragonal group III-V monolayers and suggest that T-GaN may serve as a promising candidate for anisotropic nanoelectronic and optoelectronic applications.

articles.title: Bad metallicity in the semi-quantum regime of the Hubbard model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bad metals exhibit approximately T-linear dc resistivity beyond the Ioffe--Regel limit. That this behavior occurs in systems with radically different ground states suggests it is a generic manifestation of strong local correlations. We test this hypothesis in the infinite-U Hubbard model with small hole densities using exact diagonalization to compute thermodynamic and transport properties of finite clusters. Upon cooling, we find an intermediate temperature range, an electronic analogue of the ``semi-quantum regime'' of liquid helium, in which quantum effects produce a roughly T-independent compressibility, yet the resistivity is T-linear and exceeds the Ioffe--Regel limit. Entry into this regime is accompanied by the formation of quasi-local ferromagnetic ``spin cages'' around doped holes, regions that facilitate local quantum motion embedded in a fluctuating spin background, analogous to the transient crystalline cages thought to control incoherent transport in semi-quantum liquid helium. Remarkably, despite the simplicity of the model, the bad metal behavior found here resembles that seen in various material platforms.

articles.title: Non-Abelian Anyon Condensation: a Path-Integral Monte Carlo Approach
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transitions out of non-Abelian topological order are difficult to describe in microscopic quantum models with numerical methods that remain tractable at large scales. We develop a sign-free path-integral framework for Kitaev quantum doubles mathcal D(G) by organizing single-link perturbations in terms of non-invertible electric and magnetic 1-form symmetries that proliferate distinct anyon species. For any finite group G, an exact matterization isometry introduces vertex degrees of freedom and maps the link-only model onto a G gauge--Higgs theory. Furthermore, the 1-form symmetries of the fixed point allow us to define generalized Fredenhagen--Marcu order parameters that become finite when the corresponding anyons condense. For G = S₃, quantum Monte Carlo simulations show that proliferating a non-Abelian electric anyon drives a first-order transition in which all nontrivial electric anyons condense. In the purely magnetic limit, the model reduces to a (2+1)D pure G gauge theory; for G=S₃, it exhibits a first-order confinement transition, diagnosed by the onset of a Wilson-loop area law and the restoration of an emergent magnetic 1-form symmetry. These results provide a unified numerical framework for non-Abelian anyon condensation, confinement, and generalized symmetry breaking.

articles.title: Valley-Helical Superconductivity Driven by Repulsion and Quantum Geometry: Applications to Time-Reversal Symmetric Rhombohedral Graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the recent experimental signatures of chiral superconductivity in valley-polarized graphene- and transition-metal-dichalcogenide-based systems, we investigate the possibility of chiral pairing in the absence of valley polarization or time-reversal symmetry breaking. For systems with opposite Berry curvature in the two valleys, we find that overscreened repulsion (i.e., the Kohn-Luttinger mechanism) can indeed induce pairing of opposite chiralities in each valley, producing a valley-helical state. Moreover, the valley-helical state can outcompete more conventional intervalley paired states at intermediate coupling, despite only the latter having a weak-coupling instability. Using a realistic model of time-reversal-symmetric rhombohedral graphene, we find extended ranges of fillings and displacement fields with dominant valley-helical superconductivity. This occurs for all layer numbers considered here, 4≤ N≤ 8. We show that the valley-helical states can display topologically projected edge modes, unusual magnetic responses, and intertwined Kekulé-like bond-order; features that can be used to distinguish them from more conventional superconductors.

articles.title: Momentum-dependent precessional and nutational spin pumping in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ultrafast magnetic inertial dynamics on subpicosecond timescales generate an additional high-frequency terahertz nutational resonance. Here, we investigate momentum-resolved spin pumping in a two-dimensional honeycomb antiferromagnet by incorporating spin inertia into the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. Using a microscopic two-sublattice model with J₁-J₂-J₃ exchange interactions, we calculate the precessional and nutational magnon spectra and their corresponding intra- and inter-sublattice spin pumping contributions throughout the Brillouin zone. For parameters representative of MnPS₃, we find a pronounced complementary momentum dependence of the two spin pumping channels: the precessional current is strongly suppressed around the Γ point (0.01%) and increases towards the Brillouin zone boundary (100% at K and 87% at M), whereas the nutational current is largest near Γ (100%) and decreases towards the boundary (68% at K and 69% at M). This contrasting momentum dependence provides a means of distinguishing spin nutation from conventional precessional motion. We further demonstrate that the nutational spin pumping current is strongly controlled by the inertial relaxation time η, in contrast to the comparatively weak η dependence of the precessional current. In the small-η regime, our analytical results show that the intra-sublattice nutational spin pumping current exhibits a leading-order dependence of 1/η³. The spin pumping response can also be tuned through the exchange interaction strengths and magnetic moment. Our further results on the magnetic field dependence of spin pumping reveal that the ratio of nutational spin pumping current increases with magnetic field strength, whereas the corresponding precessional counterpart decreases.

articles.title: Unified Transport and Susceptibility Analysis of a Thin BSCCO Film: From Local Pairing to Global Phase Coherence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The superconducting transition in thin high-T_c films can be significantly broadened by disorder, spatial inhomogeneity, and phase fluctuations. Here, we study the transition in a 30-nm-thick sputter-grown Bi₂Sr₂CaCu₂O₈₊δ (BSCCO) film through electrical-transport and ac-susceptibility measurements. The resistive transition is examined using a Gaussian distribution of local T_c values and the Ambegaokar--Halperin model, describing spatial variations in superconductivity and thermally activated phase dynamics, respectively. To relate the transport and magnetic responses, we extend the Choy--Stoneham susceptibility model by introducing the superconducting fraction extracted from transport and a temperature-dependent connectivity factor representing the gradual development of Josephson coupling among superconducting regions. The results identify separate temperature regimes corresponding to the onset of local superconductivity, expansion of the superconducting fraction, development of magnetic screening, and establishment of global phase coherence. The transition therefore proceeds progressively, from locally superconducting regions to a connected, phase-coherent state. This analysis provides a common framework for relating spatial inhomogeneity, dissipative phase dynamics, and magnetic screening in inhomogeneous superconducting films.

articles.title: Encapsulation epitaxy of air-stable monolayer superconducting films for quantum circuits and qubits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) superconductors are an emerging platform for strongly correlated physics and quantum information science. Their reduced dimensionality, atomically flat interfaces, and high crystallinity are attractive for realizing compact lumped-element devices in superconducting circuits. However, synthesizing large-area, monolayer 2D superconductors remains challenging because of their susceptibility to oxidation. Here, we report an "encapsulation epitaxy" mechanism that enables the growth of large-area, air-stable, monolayer superconducting NbSe2 films and explore their use in superconducting quantum circuits. A 2D encapsulation layer, such as graphene or hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), pre-deposited on a 3D substrate (e.g., SiO2 or Si3N4), serves both as a template for epitaxial growth of monolayer NbSe2 (1L-NbSe2) underneath it and as a protective cover. This approach produces uniform, large-area (>1-inch) 1L-NbSe2 with greatly enhanced ambient stability, enabling device fabrication in air. The resulting 1L-graphene/NbSe2 heterostructures exhibit robust superconductivity (Tc ~ 1 K) and enhanced charge density wave order (TCDW ~ 177 K), indicative of high material quality. We further integrate 1L-NbSe2 into superconducting circuits using oxidation-free transfer and superconducting edge-contact techniques. The 1L-NbSe2 exhibits a measured kinetic inductance LK ~ 0.7 nH/square, making it suitable for quantum circuits requiring high-kinetic-inductance elements. Encapsulation epitaxy thus provides a route to air-stable 2D superconductors and van der Waals heterostructures, with potential for wafer-scale, monolithic fabrication of superconducting quantum circuitry.

articles.title: Pressure-dependent melting and crystallization of B2-NiAl from neural-network molecular dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate pressure-dependent melting of ordered B2-NiAl using neural-network molecular dynamics with a Deep Potential interatomic model. Melting temperatures are determined from two-phase solid-liquid coexistence simulations over a broad pressure range, yielding the melting curve Tₘ(P). Relative to available experimental and previous molecular-dynamics results, the present calculations predict a stronger increase of the melting temperature with pressure at elevated compression. To assess the thermodynamic consistency of the calculated melting line, we evaluate the enthalpy and volume changes upon melting and compare the Clapeyron slope with the derivative of the fitted Tₘ(P) curve. The two estimates are in good agreement over most of the investigated pressure range, supporting the internal consistency of the coexistence results. To probe the character of melting, we perform a layer-resolved composition analysis of the coexistence configurations and find that the coexisting liquid remains essentially equiatomic at all studied pressures, with deviations of the aluminum fraction from the stoichiometric value not exceeding 5×10⁻³. This provides direct atomistic evidence that melting of B2-NiAl remains congruent within the present model. Together, these results establish a thermodynamically consistent pressure-dependent melting description of B2-NiAl and clarify the character of its melting under compression.

articles.title: Displacement field stabilizes even-denominator and partonic fractional quantum Hall states in the N=2 Landau levels of Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene (BLG), in which a graphene layer is stacked atop another and laterally shifted by a lattice constant, offers remarkable tunability in its single-particle states under applied magnetic and displacement fields. Owing to this tunability, recent transport and scanning tunneling microscopy experiments in the presence of a perpendicular magnetic field and finite interlayer displacement fields have observed even-denominator fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states at half-filling in the first excited, namely, N=2, Landau level (LL) of BLG. In contrast, at zero displacement field, a gapless composite fermion Fermi liquid (CFFL) is realized at half-filling of the N=2 LL. Motivated by these experiments, we compute the phase diagram as a function of the displacement field in the half-filled N=2 LL of BLG by studying the competition between the CFFL and the Moore-Read state---a candidate even-denominator FQH state---by calculating their thermodynamic energies in this setting. We find that the modified effective Coulomb interaction, induced by changes in the single-particle states with increasing displacement field, softens the inter-electronic repulsion at short distances, thereby stabilizing the Moore-Read state over the CFFL in the N=2 LL of BLG. We also study the nature of FQH states at fillings 2/5, 3/7, 4/9, and 6/13 in the N=2 LL of BLG. Our results suggest that, with increasing displacement field, the Jain composite-fermion states at 3/7, 4/9, and 6/13 transition into states with distinct topological order that are well-captured by parton wave functions.

articles.title: Multiferroic Quantum Dot in an Artificial van der Waals Heterostructure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum dots (QDs) provide a versatile platform for engineering quantum-confined electronic states with functionalities relevant for optoelectronics, spintronics, and quantum technologies. While substantial progress has been achieved in coupling confined states to spin, valley, topological, or ferroelectric degrees of freedom, the realization of a multiferroic QD in which quantum confinement simultaneously intertwines with magnetism and ferroelectricity remains elusive. Here, we engineer a multiferroic QD in an artificial van der Waals heterostructure grown by molecular beam epitaxy under ultra-high-vacuum conditions. The heterostructure consists of ferroelectric SnTe nanoislands deposited on the layered magnet CrBr₂ supported on highly oriented pyrolytic graphite. Combining scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy with ab initio calculations and low-energy tight-binding models, we demonstrate the emergence of spin-polarized discretized electronic states confined within the SnTe islands. Remarkably, the spectroscopic response of the QD strongly depends on the ferroelectric domain configuration of the SnTe nanoislands, demonstrating an interplay between quantum confinement, magnetic exchange, and ferroelectric order at the atomic scale. Our results establish engineered van der Waals heterostructures as a platform for multiferroic quantum confinement and open new routes toward electrically tunable quantum spintronic devices.

articles.title: ALIGNN 2.0: A Unified Line-Graph Neural Network Framework for Materials Screening, Force Fields, Inverse Design, Spectroscopy, and Microscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph neural networks are central to materials property prediction and machine-learning interatomic potentials, yet their reliance on specialized graph libraries hampers portability and reproducibility, and property and force-field models have historically required separate graph pipelines. We present ALIGNN 2.0, a dependency-free, pure-PyTorch reimplementation of the Atomistic Line Graph Neural Network, with the line graph and its batching built from scratch, running on current-generation accelerators and unifying scalar, spectral, tensorial, per-atom, and force-field prediction behind a single graph, a combination that to our knowledge no existing framework provides. Comparing radius and k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graphs, the wider kNN graph is more accurate for properties while the smoothly varying radius graph is required for energy-conserving molecular dynamics. On the JARVIS-Leaderboard, ALIGNN 2.0 leads on 26 of 30 single-property benchmarks against the original ALIGNN, with large gains for piezoelectric and dielectric maxima, exfoliation energy, moduli, and superconducting Tc. The LAMMPS- and OpenMM-compatible ALIGNN-FF matches leading universal potentials on the Matbench-Discovery and CHIPS-FF benchmarks at a small fraction of their parameters while scaling to hundred-thousand-atom cells. We further use ALIGNN 2.0 as the denoiser in a conditional crystal-diffusion model, where explicit line-graph message passing consistently lowers structural denoising loss. We also show, as work in progress, that an independently diffused, redundant bond-angle state is learnable but does not uniformly improve reconstruction or combine additively with the line graph. Finally, from a single relaxed structure the same framework reconstructs infrared, Raman, optical-dielectric, and neutron spectra in agreement with experiment and DFT, and drives frozen-phonon electron-microscopy image simulation.

articles.title: Pairing symmetry and superconductivity from long-range Coulomb interactions in the extended t-t'-t''-Jz model for cuprates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the pairing symmetry of the ground-state phase diagram of an extended two-dimensional t-t'-t''-J_z model, in which the first-, second-, and third-nearest neighbor electron hopping terms (t,t' and t'') and an anisotropic Ising-like antiferromagnetic interaction J_z are treated on the same framework. We find that the dominant pairing symmetry depends sensitively on the sign and magnitude of the hopping parameters t' and t'', showing pure p-wave, pure d-wave, or coexisting pairing channels, highlighting the decisive role of these terms. We further explore the role of the long-range and short-range repulsive interactions in the formation of pairs and analyze the specific case of hole-doped cuprates. Our results indicate that repulsive interactions favors hole pair escaping of the stripe domains. Furthermore, pairing correlation calculations strongly suggest that repulsive Coulomb interactions drive reentrant superconducting behavior at experimentally observed underdoped regime (δapprox0.07 to 0.15), as in Neodymium-based cuprates.

articles.title: Universality of the 1/9 Magnetization Plateau and Quantum-Disordered States in the Kagome Family mathrmCs₈AB₃Ti₁₂F₄₈ (A=Rb,Li; B=K,Na)
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The microscopic origin of the low-field 1/9 magnetization plateau in spin-1/2 kagome antiferromagnets remains unresolved. Here, we show that chemical pressure reshapes the hierarchy of fractional magnetization plateaus in the titanium-based kagome family mathrmCs₈AB₃Ti₁₂F₄₈ (A=Rb,Li; B=K,Na). High-field magnetization measurements up to 60 T reveal a robust 1/9 plateau-like phase in the expanded mathrmCs₈RbK₃Ti₁₂F₄₈ and mathrmCs₈LiK₃Ti₁₂F₄₈ compounds, despite the absence of the conventionally more robust 1/3 plateau. In contrast, compressed mathrmCs₈LiNa₃Ti₁₂F₄₈ exhibits neither the 1/9 plateau-like phase nor a quantum-disordered ground state. Specific-heat measurements and first-principles calculations show that lattice expansion preserves a frustrated, fully connected kagome exchange network and gapless quantum-disordered ground states, whereas compression reorganizes the exchange network into weakly coupled quasi-one-dimensional subsystems and induces successive magnetic transitions. These results demonstrate that the 1/9 and 1/3 plateaus need not share a common microscopic origin and suggest that the 1/9 plateau may represent a more universal feature of frustrated spin-1/2 kagome magnetism.
